##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्रस्तुतिः न प्रयुक्तिः (*prastutiḥ na prayuktiḥ*)—"The prastuti cannot be the prayukti": the Ṛk points out the difference between the two, and yet it indicates the assurance that by the mere prastuti alone one can win the favour of Mitra and Varuṇa and obtain their abode. The purport is that if the abode of Mitra and Varuṇa can be obtained through the help of the prastuti, which is only one part of the rite, then if the rite is performed in full its fruit will be greater still.
प्रस्तुतिः प्रस्तावना ; करोमीति संकल्प एव (*prastutiḥ prastāvanā ; karomīti saṃkalpa eva*)—Sāyaṇa has explained this as the resolve in the form of the introduction, "I shall perform the rite in full". What is the prastāva, and what place it has in the rite, Sāyaṇa has explained in his commentary on the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. And those who recite such a prastāva are called "desirous of prastuti" in the Chāndogya and other texts. The origin and nature of the prastāva are told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa in the form of a story, as follows:
ऋक्च वा इदमग्रे साम चास्तां सैव नाम ऋगासीदमो नाम साम सा ना ऋक्सामोपावदन्मिथुनं संभवाव प्रजात्या इति नेत्यब्रवीत्साम ज्यायान्वा अतो मम महिमेति ते द्वे भूत्त्वोपावदतां तेन प्रतिचन समवदत तास्तिस्रो भूत्त्वोपावदंस्तत्तिसृभिः समभवद्यत्तिसृभिः समभवत्तस्मात्तिसृभिः स्तुवंति तिसृभिरुद्गायंति तिसृभिर्हि साम संमितं तस्मादेकस्य बह्वो जाया भवंति नैकस्यै बहवः सह पतयो यद्वै तत्सा चामश्च समभवतां तत्सामाभवत्तत्साम्नः सामत्वं, सामन्भवति य एवं वेद योवै भवति यः श्रेष्ठ तामश्नुते स सामन्भवत्यसामन्य इति हि निंदंति । तेवै पंचान्यद्भूत्वा पंचान्यद्भूत्वा कल्पेतामाहावश्च हिंकारश्च प्रस्तावश्च प्रथमा च ऋगुद्दीथश्च मध्यमा च प्रतिहारश्चोत्तमा च निधनं च वषट्कारश्च इति ॥ (*ṛkca vā idamagre sāma cāstāṃ saiva nāma ṛgāsīdamo nāma sāma sā nā ṛksāmopāvadanmithunaṃ saṃbhavāva prajātyā iti netyabravītsāma jyāyānvā ato mama mahimeti te dve bhūttvopāvadatāṃ tena praticana samavadata tāstisro bhūttvopāvadaṃstattisṛbhiḥ samabhavadyattisṛbhiḥ samabhavattasmāttisṛbhiḥ stuvaṃti tisṛbhirudgāyaṃti tisṛbhirhi sāma saṃmitaṃ tasmādekasya bahvo jāyā bhavaṃti naikasyai bahavaḥ saha patayo yadvai tatsā cāmaśca samabhavatāṃ tatsāmābhavattatsāmnaḥ sāmatvaṃ, sāmanbhavati ya evaṃ veda yovai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭha tāmaśnute sa sāmanbhavatyasāmanya iti hi niṃdaṃti | tevai paṃcānyadbhūtvā paṃcānyadbhūtvā kalpetāmāhāvaśca hiṃkāraśca prastāvaśca prathamā ca ṛguddīthaśca madhyamā ca pratihāraścottamā ca nidhanaṃ ca vaṣaṭkāraśca iti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 12-13)
In the beginning the Ṛk was in feminine form and the Sāma in masculine form. Desiring offspring, the Ṛk wished to unite with the Sāma. Then the Sāma, to show the superiority of its masculinity, said that this could not be. Taking two forms, the Ṛk again entreated the Sāma, and even then the Sāma refused. Growing into three and entreating the Sāma once more, then, with its consent, when the two came together there arose two groups of śastras, each with five parts. These are the prastāva and the rest. Which are they?
ते वै त एव वक्ष्यमाणाः शस्त्रावयवाः पंचसंख्याता अन्यत्पृथगेव शस्त्ररूपं भूत्वा वर्तंते । तथा हिंकारादयः पंच सामांशा वैश्वदेवावयवा अन्यत्पृथक्सामरूपं भूत्वा वर्तंते च । .............तदेतत्पंचकं शस्त्र स्वरूपं । उद्गात्रा पठितव्यः साम्न आदौ हिमित्येवंशब्दो हिंकारः । गातव्यः सामावयवः प्रस्तावः । उद्गात्रा गातव्य उद्गीथः । प्रतिहर्त्रा गातव्यः प्रतिहारः । अंते सर्वैर्गातव्यो भागो निधनं । तदेतत्पंचकं स्तोत्रस्वरूपं । (*te vai ta eva vakṣyamāṇāḥ śastrāvayavāḥ paṃcasaṃkhyātā anyatpṛthageva śastrarūpaṃ bhūtvā vartaṃte | tathā hiṃkārādayaḥ paṃca sāmāṃśā vaiśvadevāvayavā anyatpṛthaksāmarūpaṃ bhūtvā vartaṃte ca | .............tadetatpaṃcakaṃ śastra svarūpaṃ | udgātrā paṭhitavyaḥ sāmna ādau himityevaṃśabdo hiṃkāraḥ | gātavyaḥ sāmāvayavaḥ prastāvaḥ | udgātrā gātavya udgīthaḥ | pratihartrā gātavyaḥ pratihāraḥ | aṃte sarvairgātavyo bhāgo nidhanaṃ | tadetatpaṃcakaṃ stotrasvarūpaṃ |*) (Ai. Brā. 12-13, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 550
Of these, the first is the hiṅkāra, recited by the Udgātṛ at the beginning in the form of the sound हिं (*hiṃ*). The second is the prastāva, a part of the Sāma, to be sung by the Prastotṛ. The third, called udgītha, is what the Udgātṛ has to recite. The fourth is the pratihāra, to be recited by the Pratihartṛ. The fifth, to be sung at the end by all together, is called nidhana. Of these five parts, the second, the prastāva, is to be recited by the Prastotṛ. Taking an example, in the Ṛk
अभि ते मधुना पयोऽथर्वाणो अशिश्रयुः । देवं देवाय देवयु ॥ (*abhi te madhunā payo 'tharvāṇo aśiśrayuḥ | devaṃ devāya devayu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-11-2)
the portion अभि ते मधुना पय (*abhi te madhunā paya*) (Om) is the part called prastāva, to be recited by the Prastotṛ. This is a mantra addressed to the deity Soma. It has been said that if one knows only this portion of the mantra and does not know the nature of the deity to whom it is addressed, there is no benefit at all, and moreover harm results. In this connection Uśasti Cākrāyaṇa explained the nature of the Sāma consisting of the five parts beginning with the prastāva. He declared the importance of knowing the relation between the prastuti and the deity indicated by it, and the trouble that results from reciting only the mantra without that knowledge. Since that part of the story is told in order to make known the nature of the prastāva and the characteristics of one desirous of prastuti, it is also given here briefly. Śaṅkarācārya too, in his introduction, says:
उद्गीथोपासनप्रसंगेन प्रस्तावप्रतिहारविषयमप्युपासनं वक्तव्यमितीदमारभ्यते । (*udgīthopāsanaprasaṃgena prastāvapratihāraviṣayamapyupāsanaṃ vaktavyamitīdamārabhyate |*) (Bhā. U. 1-10-1, Śāṅkara-bhāṣya) **NOTE**
that is, in connection with the worship of the udgītha, the worship of its parts, the prastāva and the rest, is also necessary; to make this known the story of Cākrāyaṇa is told. That part of the story runs as follows:
मटचीहतेषु कुरुष्वाटिक्या सह जाययोषस्तिर्ह चाक्रायण इभ्यग्रामे प्रद्राणक उवास । स हेभ्यं कुल्माषान्बादंतं विभिक्षे तं होवाच । (*maṭacīhateṣu kuruṣvāṭikyā saha jāyayoṣastirha cākrāyaṇa ibhyagrāme pradrāṇaka uvāsa | sa hebhyaṃ kulmāṣānbādaṃtaṃ vibhikṣe taṃ hovāca |*)

### Printed p. 551
"Nor are there others (to be found), and these that are laid by for me." "Give me some of these," he said. He gave them to him. "Here, drink after it," (said the owner). "But then what I drink would be a leftover of his," he said. "Were not these (beans) also leftovers?" "I could not have lived without eating these," he said; "water is at my pleasure." Having eaten, he took the remainder to his wife. She had already obtained food (elsewhere) and kept them, having received them. In the morning he rose and said: "If we could get some food, we might get some wealth; the king yonder is about to perform a sacrifice, and he will choose me for all the priestly offices." His wife said to him, "Here, my lord, are these very beans." Having eaten them, he went to that sacrifice which was in progress.

There he sat down near the Udgātṛs who were about to sing praise at the Stotra. He said to the Prastotṛ: "Prastotar, the deity that is connected with the Prastāva, if you chant the Prastāva without knowing her, your head will fall off." Likewise he said to the Udgātṛ: "Udgātar, the deity connected with the Udgītha—if you sing the Udgītha without knowing her, your head will fall off." In the same way he said to the Pratihartṛ: "Pratihartar, the deity connected with the Pratihāra—if you perform the Pratihāra without knowing her, your head will fall off." They stopped, and sat down in silence.
(Bhā. U. 1-10, 11)

[Kannada exposition:] In the land of Kuru lived a poor man named Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa, with his wife Āṭikī. Once, when a storm had brought distress, Cākrāyaṇa, afflicted by poverty, went to a rich man of his village and begged for something to eat. That rich man, who was eating beans, said he had nothing but the small quantity of that grain he had. Cākrāyaṇa insisted that he be given some of it, and the rich man gave a little. Then he showed a vessel nearby and said there was water to drink. Cākrāyaṇa said that the rest was leftover water and he did not want it. When the rich man asked whether the beans too were not leftovers he had eaten, he replied that, being in dire need, he had taken the grain for the sake of sustaining life, even if it was a leftover, that this rule did not apply to water; and he gave a little grain to his wife also. By then she had obtained her own food and said she did not want it. The next day, learning that the king would perform a sacrifice, Cākrāyaṇa thought he might obtain the priesthood there, and went. There he went to the Udgātṛs who were reciting the stotra and said, "If you chant the Prastāva without knowing the full nature of the deity toward whom the Prastāva-stotra is to be chanted, your head will burst and fall off,"

### Printed p. 552
to the Prastotṛ; likewise, "If you pronounce the Udgītha and Pratihāra without knowing the nature of the deity, the head of each will burst and fall off." Thus he warns them and shows the relation between the recitation of mantras such as the Prastāva and knowledge of the deity and the like. In this context the mutual and inseparable relation between ritual and spiritual knowledge is also understood. Likewise, in the discussion of the philosophers in the royal assembly the nature of the Sāman is explained in detail, and at the end the identity of the physical principles, the spiritual principles and the parts of the Sāman is explained.

[[Chāndogya passage:]] One should meditate on the fivefold Sāman in the worlds: पृथिवी हिंकारः (*pṛthivī hiṃkāraḥ*), *agniḥ prastāvaḥ*, the atmosphere the Udgītha, the sun the Pratihāra, the heaven the Nidhana—thus in the ascending order. Then in the reverse order: heaven the Hiṅkāra, the sun the Prastāva ….

One should meditate on the fivefold Sāman in rain: the east wind is the Hiṅkāra, the cloud that is formed is the Prastāva ….

One should meditate on the fivefold Sāman in the seasons: spring is the Hiṅkāra, summer the Prastāva ……..

One should meditate on the fivefold Sāman in animals: goats are the Hiṅkāra, sheep the Prastāva ………..

One should meditate on the fivefold Sāman in the vital breaths, the "higher and higher": breath is the Hiṅkāra, speech the Prastāva ………..
(Bhā. Tā. 2-4-2 to 7)

Among the earth-principles fire, among the rain-principles the cloud, among the seasons summer, among the animals sheep, among the living beings speech, are the forms of the Prastāva.

अथ यत्प्रथमोदिते स प्रस्तावस्तवदस्य मनुष्या अन्वायत्तास्तस्मात्ते प्रस्तुतिकामाः प्रस्तावभाजिनो ह्येतस्य सान्मुः ॥ (*atha yatprathamodite sa prastāvastavadasya manuṣyā anvāyattāstasmātte prastutikāmāḥ prastāvabhājino hyetasya sānmuḥ ‖*)
(Bhā. U. 2-9-3)

The mantra to be recited after sunrise is called Prastāva. It has a very close relation with man. That is why men are desirous of praise (prastuti), and are also engaged in reciting the Prastāva, a part of the Sāman. Having thus shown the identity of the physical principles with the Sāman-parts such as the Prastāva, the text then shows the relation of identity of the spiritual principles with the Prastāva and the rest.

मनो हिंकारो वाक्प्रस्तावः (*mano hiṃkāro vākprastāvaḥ*) …………… स य एवमेतद्दायत्रं प्राणेषु प्रोतं (*sa ya evametaddāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protaṃ*)

### Printed p. 553
अभिमंथति स हिंकारो धूमो जायते स प्रस्तावः (*abhimaṃthati sa hiṃkāro dhūmo jāyate sa prastāvaḥ*) …. …. …. स य एवमेतद्रथंतरमग्नौ प्रोतं (*sa ya evametadrathaṃtaramagnau protaṃ*) ।
उपमंत्रयते स हिंकारो ज्ञपॆयते स प्रस्तावः (*upamaṃtrayate sa hiṃkāro jñapèyate sa prastāvaḥ*) …. …. …. स य एवमेतद्वामदेव्यं मिथुने प्रोतं (*sa ya evametadvāmadevyaṃ mithune protaṃ*) ।
उद्यन्हिंकार उदितः प्रस्तावः (*udyanhiṃkāra uditaḥ prastāvaḥ*) …. …. स य एव मेतद्बृहदादित्ये प्रोत ० (*sa ya eva metadbṛhadāditye prota 0*) ।
…. …. …. …. …. …. ।
त्रयी विद्या हिंकारस्त्रय इमे लोकाः स प्रस्तावोग्निर्वायुरादित्यः स उद्गीथो नक्षत्राणि वयांसि मरीचयः स प्रतिहारः सर्पा गंधर्वाः पितरस्तन्निधनमेतत्साम सर्वस्मिन् प्रोतं । स य एवमेतत्साम सर्वस्मिन् प्रोतं वेद सर्वं ह भवति ॥ (*trayī vidyā hiṃkārastraya ime lokāḥ sa prastāvognirvāyurādityaḥ sa udgītho nakṣatrāṇi vayāṃsi marīcayaḥ sa pratihāraḥ sarpā gaṃdharvāḥ pitarastannidhanametatsāma sarvasmin protaṃ | sa ya evametatsāma sarvasmin protaṃ veda sarvaṃ ha bhavati ‖*)
(Bhā. E. 2-11 to 21)

For the Gāyatra-sāman, woven into the vital breaths, speech; for the Rathantara-sāman, woven into fire, smoke; for the Vāmadevya-sāman, woven into the couple, prayer; for the Bṛhat-sāman, woven into the sun, the risen sun; …. …. …. likewise for the Sāman pervading and woven into the whole universe, fire, wind and the sun (earth, atmosphere and heaven) are reckoned as Prastāvas. This is the greatness of the Prastāva.

In this way the hymn of praise, which reflects the principle of the whole universe, which is to be recited by the Prastotṛ and which is to be recited foremost at the beginning of the rite, is called "prastuti" in the present Ṛk. But however great the importance of this prastuti, if the completeness of prayukti is not joined to it, there is not only the loss that results from it: as was said earlier, या देवता प्रस्तावमन्वायत्ता तां चेदविद्वान्प्रस्तोष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यति (*yā devatā prastāvamanvāyattā tāṃ cedavidvānprastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyati*)—if there is no knowledge of the deity with whom the Prastāva is closely connected, the head of the reciter will burst and fall off—so here too it is a general rule that without completion through prayukti the praise is of no use. But to show that even the mere recitation of praise addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa has extraordinary power, this mantra, though not (accompanied by) prayukti, says वां धाम अयामि (*vāṃ dhāma ayāmi*): "I attain your abode of radiance."

Prayukti: प्रयुक्तिः कृत्स्नप्रयोगः (*prayuktiḥ kṛtsnaprayogaḥ*). Knowing the separate places of the mantras to be recited at the times of the rite, and likewise the mutual relation of them all, and performing the rite as the harmony of them all, thereby giving the rite completeness—this is called prayukti. The purport is the completion of the prescribed rite.

### Printed p. 554
Without this, the recitation of individual mantras one by one is plainly said to be of no use. Even when explaining the greatness of Oṃkāra in the Praśna Upaniṣad:

तिस्रो मात्रा मृत्युमत्यः प्रयुक्ता अन्नोन्यसक्ता अनविप्रयुक्ताः । क्रियासु बाह्याभ्यंतरमध्यमासु सम्यक्रयुक्तासु न कंपते ज्ञ ॥ (*tisro mātrā mṛtyumatyaḥ prayuktā annonyasaktā anaviprayuktāḥ | kriyāsu bāhyābhyaṃtaramadhyamāsu samyakrayuktāsu na kaṃpate jña ‖*)
(Praśna U. 5-6)

If these three mātrās (a, u, m) are applied one after another separately, without knowing their mutual relation, harm results. Whether the outer rite, the inner rite, or the rite between them, it has significance only when it is wholly blended with it and unity is achieved between inner meditation and outer practice. In the same way, in the present Ṛk prayukti means कृत्स्नप्रयोगः (*kṛtsnaprayogaḥ*): rite-performance that attains or has attained completeness.

Dhāma: तेजःस्थानं (*tejaḥsthānaṃ*). As said before, among the many meanings of the word dhāma, here it means the radiant and pleasure-giving abode of Mitra and Varuṇa.

Anakti: Two meanings are given for this word. First, हविषा आगच्छति । होमं करोति (*haviṣā āgacchati | homaṃ karoti*): he performs the oblation by offering havis and the like. Second, होता शस्त्रादिना वां अनक्ति व्यंजयति (*hotā śastrādinā vāṃ anakti vyaṃjayati*): the Hotṛ, by śastras and the like, recounts your qualities and makes your nature shine forth.

Sūri: युष्मन्माहात्मवित् (*yuṣmanmāhātmavit*): one who knows your greatness. The word sūri is used to show excellent knowledge. It is read among the names of praisers, rebha, jaritā, kāru, etc. (Ni. 3-19). The word sūri is used in many places in the sense of the wise, the discerning, the intelligent. When used of the seers who have the supernatural power of vision, both of the eye and of the mind, to grasp the true nature of the deities and the secret principles of the universe, this epithet gives a special meaning.

तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः । दिवीव चक्षुराततं ॥ (*tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣurātataṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-20)

In such places it indicates not merely praisers but also the extraordinary power of vision of the seers. Other meanings of this word have been explained in detail earlier.

Iyakṣan: यागं कर्तुमिच्छन् (*yāgaṃ kartumicchan*): desiring to perform a sacrifice,

##### Grammar

- प्रस्तुतिः—ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ धातुः । भावार्थे स्त्रियां क्तिन् इति क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । तादौ च निति (पा. सू. ६-२-५०) इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- प्रयुक्तिः—युजिर् योगे धातुः । पूर्ववत् क्तिन् प्रत्ययः कृदुत्तरपदस्वरस्य बाधकः । पूर्ववत् गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- अयामि—अय गतौ धातुः । व्यत्ययो बहुलम् इति परस्मैपदी भवति । लट् उत्तमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । शप् मिप् अनुदात्तौ भवतः इति धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- सुवृक्तिः—वृजी वर्जने धातुः । क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । चोःकुः इति धातुजकारस्य कुत्वं चर्त्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- अनक्ति—अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिषु धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् (पा. सू. ३-१-७८) इति श्नम् विकरणम् । मिदचोंत्यात्परः इति अंत्याचः परः आगच्छति । श्नान्नलोपः (पा. सू. ६-४-२३) इति धातुनकारस्य लोपः । चोःकुः इति जकारस्य कुत्वं चर्त्वम् । अनक्ति इति रूपं भवति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । विकरणस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- विदथेषु—विद ज्ञाने धातुः । अस्मात् औणादिकः अथ प्रत्ययः । कित्वातिदेशात् लघूपधगुणः न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- सूरिः—षूज् प्राणिप्रसवे धातुः । सूजः क्रिः (उ. सू. ४-५०४) इति क्रि प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् गुणः न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति ।
- इयक्षन्—यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु धातुः । यष्टुं इच्छति इयक्षति । इयक्षतीति इयक्षन् । धातोः कर्मणः स— (पा. सू ३-१-७) इति इच्छार्थे सन् । सन्नजोः इति द्वित्वम् । बहुलं छंदसि इति अभ्यासस्य संप्रसारणं भवति । सन्यंतात् लट् आगते तस्य शत्रादेशः । अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१८९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।

> पूजयन् मानुषो होता न मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य संबंध्येतन्नामक ऋत्विगिव
> विदथे यज्ञे वां हिनोति हविरादिना प्रीणयति । तदा पीपायेत्याह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa: for the sacrifice (ṛta) that is yours, and for the person who gives the havis (havirde)—the sacrificer—the cow (dhenu) that gives satisfaction, being aditi, that is, undiminished and abundant in milk, पीपाय (*pīpāya*): let her swell again and again with milk. The root pyāy takes the Vedic Liṭ in the sense of prayer. The meaning is: let her swell the sacrifice whose oblation is milk and the like, and the sacrificer, in the milk-vows and so on. If one asks at what time, he says: when, yadā, that well-known king named Rātahavya, praising and honouring you, like a human Hotṛ—a priest of that name belonging to the human sacrificer—gratifies you in the sacrifice (vidatha) with havis and the like, then he says "pīpāya".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणौ (*mitrāvaruṇau*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सः रातहव्यः (*saḥ rātahavyaḥ*)—that well-known king named Rātahavya
- सपश्यन् (*sapaśyan*)—honouring with praise **NOTE**
- मानुषः होता न (*mānuṣaḥ hotā na*)—like a Hotṛ priest belonging to the human sacrificer
- विदथे (*vidathe*)—in the sacrifice
- नां (*nāṃ*)—you both **NOTE**
- हिनोति (*hinoti*)—gratifies (by offering havis and the like); (then)
- ऋताय (*ṛtāya*)—for the sacrifice
- हविर्दे (*havirde*)—who offers havis
- जनाय (*janāya*)—for the sacrificer
- धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*)—the cow
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—having abundant milk
- पीपायॆ (*pīpāyè*)—let her be filled (with that milk)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, may the cow that assists that well-known king Rātahavya in the task of gratifying you both—as he, honouring you with praise, offers oblations in the sacrifice like a priest, the Hotṛ—be filled with abundant milk.

### Printed p. 557

##### Printed English

Let the productive milch cow, Mitra and Varuna, furnish abundant nutriment to the pious man who presents you with oblations, as when Ratahavya, glorifying you, propitiates you in the solemnity, like the ministrant priest of a man (who institutes the rite).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

रातहव्यः (*rātahavyaḥ*)—Ordinarily the word रातहव्यः (*rātahavyaḥ*) is formed from the root रै (*rai*), which means giving. It means "one whose oblation has been given" and is an epithet either of the sacrificer who has offered the oblation or of the deity to whom the oblation is offered. In the present Ṛk it is taken to mean a king of this name. There is not enough evidence to know about him properly. The seer Rātahavya is said to be the seer of the 65th and 66th sūktas of the fifth Maṇḍala. By रातहव्यस्यात्रेयस्यार्षं मैत्रावरुणं । (*rātahavyasyātreyasyārṣaṃ maitrāvaruṇaṃ |*) the Bhāṣyakāra says that it was composed by the seer named Rātahavya, of the Ātreya family.
In the Ṛk ता वामेषे रथानामुर्वीं गव्यूतिमेषां । रातहव्यस्य सुष्टुतिं वधृक् स्सोमैर्मनामहे ॥ (*tā vāmeṣe rathānāmurvīṃ gavyūtimeṣāṃ | rātahavyasya suṣṭutiṃ vadhṛk ssomairmanāmahe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-66-3) the seer mentions his own name and expresses his devotion.
In places such as कस्मा अद्य सुजाताय रातहन्याय प्र ययुः । एना यामेन मरुतः ॥ (*kasmā adya sujātāya rātahanyāya pra yayuḥ | enā yāmena marutaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-53-12) the word is everywhere taken to mean "one who has given the oblation".
विदथे (*vidathe*)—The derivation of the word विदथ (*vidatha*) and the various meanings of this word have been given in this same volume in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-143-7 (pp. 331–324). Here विदथे-यज्ञे । (*vidathe-yajñe |*) is explained as "in the sacrifice".
अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—It means one who possesses fullness without deficiency. The derivation etc. of this word were given earlier.
पीपाय (*pīpāya*)—क्षीरेण पुनःपुनः आप्यायतां । (*kṣīreṇa punaḥpunaḥ āpyāyatāṃ |*) By filling itself abundantly with milk, the prayer is that the cow may satisfy the sacrifice, which has to be carried out with milk, and the sacrificer who relies on her for the gift of oblations. The word indicates both meanings: increase and the satisfaction that results from it.

### Printed p. 558
In Ṛks such as पीपाय स श्रवसा मर्त्येषु यो अग्नये ददाश विप्र उक्थैः । चित्राभिस्तमूतिभिश्चित्रशोचिव्रजस्य साता गोमतो दधाति ॥ (*pīpāya sa śravasā martyeṣu yo agnaye dadāśa vipra ukthaiḥ | citrābhistamūtibhiścitraśocivrajasya sātā gomato dadhāti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-10-3) both meanings are indicated; likewise in the present Ṛk the fullness of milk in the cows, and through it the delight of the sacrificer and others, is indicated.

##### Grammar

- पीपाय — ओप्यायी वृद्धौ धातुः । छंदसि लुज् लज् लिटः (पं- सू. ३-४-६) इति लोडर्थे लिट् । प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने परस्मैपदानांणल — इति णलादेशः । लिड्यज्जोश्च (पा. सू ६-१-२९) इति धातोः सीभावः । द्वित्वे जाते अचोञ्छति इति ईकारस्य वृद्धिः । तस्य अयादेशः । पादादित्वान्न निघातस्वरः । णल् लित्त्वात् लिति (पा.सू. ६-१-१९३) इति प्रत्ययात् पूर्वस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- अदितिः — न दितिः अदितिः । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ — (पा. सू. ६-२-२) इति अव्ययं, पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- हविर्दे — हविः ददाति इति हविर्दाः । आतो मनिन्‌वनिप्क्वनिपश्च (पा.सू. ३-२-७४) इति दाञ् दाने इति धातोः विच् प्रत्ययः । आकारांतशब्दो भवति । समासे गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । अस्मात् चतुर्थीएकवचने परे भसंज्ञात्वात् अतोधातोः (पा. सू. ६-४-१४०) इति आकारस्य लोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- हिनोति — हि गतौ वृद्धौ च धातुः स्वादिः । श्लुविकरणः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपं । पादादित्वान्न निघातस्वरः । विकरणस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- सपर्यन् — सपर पूजायां धातुः । कंड्वादिः । कंड्वादिभ्योयक् (पा.सू. ३-१-२७) इति स्वार्थे यक् प्रत्ययः । लटः शत्रादेशः । प्रथमाएकवचनांतरूपं । यक् स्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- रातहव्यः — रातं हव्यं येन रातहव्यः बहुव्रीहिः । प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदम् इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- मानुषः — मनोः संबंधी मानुषः । मनोर्जातावञ् इत्यौषुक्‌च इति अञ् प्रत्ययः । तत्सन्नियोगेन षुकागमः । आदिवृद्धिः । ञित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । ॥ ३ ॥

> उ॒त वां॑ वि॒क्षु मद्या॒स्वंधो॒ गाव॒ आप॑श्च पीपयंत दे॒वीः ।  
> उ॒तो नो॑ अ॒स्य पू॒र्व्यः पति॒र्दन्वि॒तं पा॒तं पय॑स  ॒॑
> उस्रियायाः ॥ ४ ॥

> उत । वां । विक्षु । मद्यासु । अंधः । गावः । आपः । च । पीपयंत । देवीः।  
> उतो इति । नः । अस्य । पूर्व्यः । पतिः । दन् । वीतं । पातं । पयसः । उसियायाः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे मित्रावरुणौ नां युवामंधोदनीयमन्नं पयोरूपं
> पुरोडाशादिरूपं वा देवीर्द्योतनशीला गाव आपश्च व्रीह्यादिप्रवर्धकान्युदकानि च
> मद्यासु युष्माभिर्मदनीयासु विक्षु प्रजासु यजमानलक्षणासु तासामभिवृद्ध्यर्थं पीपयंत । आप्याययंतु । उतो अपि च नोऽस्मत्संबंधिनोऽस्य
> यज्ञस्य पूर्व्यः पूर्वकालीनः पतिः पालकोग्निर्दन् दाता भवत्विति शेषः । अग्नौ
> हूयमानत्वात्सर्वेषामपि हविषां । यस्मादेवॆं तस्माद्दे मित्रावरुणौ नीतं ।
> भक्षयतं पुरोडाशादिकं । उस्रियायाः -क्षीराम्युत्साविण्या गोः पयसः पयः
> पातं । यद्वा । घनीभूतं पयस्याया नीतं स्रवद्रूपं पातं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Also, O Mitra and Varuṇa": the divine, shining cows and the waters, which make rice and the like grow, are to fill up (पीपयंत (*pīpayaṃta*), "let them cause to swell") your food (अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*), food to be given: either in the form of milk or in the form of purodāśa and the like) among the विक्षु (*vikṣu*), the people in the form of the sacrificer, who are to be gladdened by you (मद्यासु (*madyāsu*)), for the increase of those people. "And" नः (*naḥ*), our, अस्य (*asya*), of this sacrifice, पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*), the ancient पतिः (*patiḥ*), the protector, Agni, is to be the giver (दन् (*dan*); "let him be" is to be supplied), since all oblations are offered in Agni. Since this is so, O Mitra and Varuṇa, eat (वीतं (*vītaṃ*)) the purodāśa and the rest, and drink (पातं (*pātaṃ*)) the milk of the उस्रियायाः (*usriyāyāḥ*), the cow that pours out milk. Or else, a further explanation of पयस्याया नीतं स्रवद्रूपं पातं (*payasyāyā nītaṃ sravadrūpaṃ pātaṃ*) is given, speaking of thickened (milk) and of the flowing form. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—(O Mitra and Varuṇa) moreover
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—shining
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—cows
- अपश्च (*apaśca*)—and waters also
- मध्यासु (*madhyāsu*)—(you) who gladden
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—for the increase of the people in the form of sacrificers
- अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)—with food fit to be eaten
- वां (*vāṃ*)—both of you
- पीपयंत (*pīpayaṃta*)—let them fill
- उतो (*uto*)—moreover
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this
- यज्ञद (*yajñada*)—sacrifice
- पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)—the ancient one
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—and protector, Agni
- र्द (*rda*)—let him be the giver (of the oblation)
- वीतं (*vītaṃ*)—eat (the purodāśa and the rest)
- उस्रियायाः (*usriyāyāḥ*)—of the cow that pours out milk and the like
- पयसः (*payasaḥ*)—the milk
- पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink

### Printed p. 560

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, may the shining cows and the waters fill you both with food fit to be eaten, for the increase of the people in the form of sacrificers who gladden you. Moreover, may Agni, the ancient one and protector of this our sacrifice, be the giver of the oblation; may he eat the purodāśa and the rest. And may he drink the milk of the cow.

##### Printed English

May the devine cows, and the waters, supply you with (sacrifical) food, for the prospertv of the people whom you favour; or mav (Agni) the former protector of this (our patron), be the donor (of the oblation): eat (of the butter and curds), drink of the milk of the cows.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

देवीः (*devīḥ*)—द्योतनशीला । (*dyotanaśīlā |*) It is explained as "shining". For this word there is the derivation of the Nirukta authors: देवो दानाद्रा, द्योतनाद्वा, द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा । (*devo dānādrā, dyotanādvā, dyusthāno bhavatīti vā |*) — that is, it becomes देव (*deva*) either because the root means giving, or because it gives the sense of "to make shine", or because it means "possessing radiance", or because it dwells in the heavenly world (Ni. 7-15). If it is an epithet of deities such as Agni, all these meanings fit. Because it gives milk abundantly, it may be of the sense of giving or of shining. Sāyaṇa has explained it as "shining".
विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—प्रजासु । यजमानलक्षणासु । (*prajāsu | yajamānalakṣaṇāsu |*) "(for the increase) of the human beings who perform the sacrifice". This word is read in the Nirukta among the names of men (3-7).
पीपयंत (*pīpayaṃta*)—आप्याययंतु । (*āpyāyayaṃtu |*) The wish expressed is that first the food may increase abundantly, and then satisfaction and delight may come from it. That this word has both meanings, increase and delight, was stated in the Special Topics of the previous Ṛk.
अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)—This word is read among the names of food, अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*), वाजः (*vājaḥ*) and so on (Ni. 3-9). अंध इत्यन्न नामाध्यानीयं भवति । अध्ययनीयं प्रार्थनीयं । (*aṃdha ityanna nāmādhyānīyaṃ bhavati | adhyayanīyaṃ prārthanīyaṃ |*) — "to be recited, to be prayed for". To support this derivation, that food is called अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) also because of the extreme need for it, the Nirukta author (Ni. 5-1) cites the Ṛk
अध्वरवो भरतेंद्राय सोममामत्रेभिः सिंचता मद्यमंधः । कामी हि वीरः सदमस्य प्रीतिं जुहोत वृष्टे तदिदेष वष्टि ॥ (*adhvaravo bharateṃdrāya somamāmatrebhiḥ siṃcatā madyamaṃdhaḥ | kāmī hi vīraḥ sadamasya prītiṃ juhota vṛṣṭe tadideṣa vaṣṭi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-1)

### Printed p. 561
and explains the meaning of the word अंध (*aṃdha*) there as stated above.
तमोऽप्यंध उच्यते नास्मिन् ध्यानं भवति । (*tamo 'pyaṃdha ucyate nāsmin dhyānaṃ bhavati |*) He explains that since one cannot be single-minded in darkness, darkness too is called अंध (*aṃdha*), and
cites the Ṛk स्त्रीयः सतीस्ता उ मे पुंस आहुः पश्यदक्षण्वान्न वि चेतदंधः । कविर‍्यः पुत्रः स ईमा चिकेत यस्ता विजानात्स पितुष्टिता सत् ॥ (*strīyaḥ satīstā u me puṃsa āhuḥ paśyadakṣaṇvānna vi cetadaṃdhaḥ | kaviryaḥ putraḥ sa īmā ciketa yastā vijānātsa pituṣṭitā sat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-16),
showing that there the word अंध (*aṃdha*) means darkness. In the present Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains पयोरूपं पुरोडाशादि रूपं वा । (*payorūpaṃ puroḍāśādi rūpaṃ vā |*): the food is either food in the form of milk or food in the form of purodāśa and the like.
पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)—This word is read among the names of the ancient (Ni. 3-19).
लोकादिमग्निं तमुवाच तस्यॆ या इष्टका यावतीर्वा यथा वा । (*lokādimagniṃ tamuvāca tasyè yā iṣṭakā yāvatīrvā yathā vā |*) (Kaṭhopaniṣad 1-15). Śruti sentences of this kind praise Agni as the primal being of all the worlds. Śaṅkarācārya explains this sentence as लोकानामादिं प्रथमशरीरत्वादग्निं (*lokānāmādiṃ prathamaśarīratvādagniṃ*), "Agni, the first body of all the worlds". This same greatness of Agni is stated in the present Ṛk too.
उस्रियायाः (*usriyāyāḥ*)—This word is read among the names of the cow, अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*), उस्रा (*usrā*), उस्रिया (*usriyā*) and so on (Ni. 3-8). उस्रियेति गोनाम । उस्राविणोऽस्यां भोगाः । (*usriyeti gonāma | usrāviṇo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ |*) The Nirukta author, citing this same Ṛk, explains the meaning of the word: the name उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*) is well known because milk, a means of happiness, flows from her (Ni. 4-19).

##### Grammar

- विक्षु — विश्‌शब्दः । सप्तमीबहुवचनांतरूपं । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) इति विभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- मद्यासु — मद तृप्तियोगे धातुः । गदमदचरयमश्चानुपसर्गे (पा. सू, ३-१-१००) इति यत् प्रत्ययः । यतोनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति अद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । स्त्रीत्वविवक्षायां टाप् भवति ।
- पीपयंत — ओप्यायी वृद्धौ धातुः । प्रयोजकव्यापारदर्शनात् हेतुमति च (पा. सू. ३-१-२६) इति णिच् । णिचि परे छांदसः पीभावः । छंदसि लुज्लज्‌लिटः (पा. सू. ३-४-६) इति लोडर्थे णिजंतात् लुज् । प्रथमपुरुष

### Printed p. 562
- पीपयंत (अनुवृत्तिः) — बहुवचने झिप्रत्ययस्य अंतादेशः । च्लेः णिश्रिद्रुस्रु — इति चज् । चज् निमित्तं धातोः द्वित्वादि । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्‌योगेऽपि इति अडागमो न भवति । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- देवीः — अस्मात् जसि परे सुपां सुलुक् इति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः भवति ।
- पूर्व्यः — पूर्वे भवः पूर्व्यः । पूर्वैः कृतमिनयौच (पा. सू. ४-४-१३३) इति य प्रत्ययः । यस्येति च इति अकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- दन् — डुदाञ् दाने धातुः । अस्मात् लटि आगते तस्य शत्रादेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य (श्लु) लुक् । प्रत्ययस्य जित्त्वात् आतोलोपइटिच (पा. सू. ६-४-६४) इति अकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- वीतम् — वी गत्यादिषु धातुः । अदादिः । अत्र भक्षणार्थे प्रयुक्तः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचने वीतम् इति रूपं भवति । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- पातम् — पा पाने धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचने तमादेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपः लुक् । शपि परे पिबादेशो न भवति । तिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । पूर्ववत् प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- उस्रियायाः — वसंतीति उस्रियाः वस निवासे । अस्मात् कर्तरि रियक् प्रत्ययः । छांदसत्वात् षत्वं न भवति । कित्त्वात् संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपं । प्रत्ययस्वरेण इकारः उदात्तो भवति । षष्ठीएकवचनांतरूपं ॥ ४ ॥

Here the 153rd sūkta ends.

### Printed p. 563
## Sūkta 154 (Maṇḍala 1)

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning "Viṣṇor nu kam" is the fifteenth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Dīrghatamas, son of Ucathya. Viṣṇu is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says: "Viṣṇoḥ ṣaḍ vaiṣṇavaṃ hīti." In the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha and Ukthya sacrifices, at the third pressing, while Ṛks for the increase of Soma are recited, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this sūkta and the next one for the extension of the stoma. This is set out in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the section "Stome vardhamāne", by the sūtra "Viṣṇor nu kam iti sūkte paro mātrayety acchāvākaḥ" (Ā. 7-9). Further, at the third pressing, in the rite called Somātireka, the sūkta is applied also in reciting the śastra-mantras of the Atirātra that follows; this is indicated in the same Sūtra, in the section "Tatraitad eva sūktaṃ somātireke", by the sūtra "Mahā indro nṛvad viṣṇor nu kam" (Ā. 6-7). The first Ṛk is applied in the Āgnimāruta-śastra, as set out in the section "Atha yathetam" by the sūtra "Viṣṇor nu kaṃ vīryāṇi pra vocaṃ tantuṃ tan nanrajaso bhānum anvihi" (Ā. 5-20).

> पदानि । नै. ३-१२ । इत्युक्तत्वात् । शाखांतर एकत्वेन पाठाच्च नु इत्येतस्मिन्नेवार्थे
> नु कमिति पदद्वयं । कानि तानीशि तत्राह । यो विष्णुः पार्थिवानि पृथिवीसंबंधीनि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O men, I swiftly proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, the all-pervading deity." Although नु कं (*nu kaṃ*) is two words, because Yāska says that words ... (Ni. 3-12) and because other recensions read it as one, the two words have the one sense of नु (*nu*) (quickly). What are those deeds? He says: Viṣṇu who has measured out the earthly realms.

> इत्यादिश्रुतिषु प्रसिद्धं । अतएवोरुगाय उरुभिर्महद्निर्गियमानः अतिप्रभूतं
> गीयमानो वा । य एवं कृतवान् तादृशस्य विष्णोर्वीर्याणि प्र वोचं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The "realms" (rajāṃsi) are the colourful ones, the forms of Agni, Vāyu and Āditya presiding over the three worlds beginning with earth; he measured them out specially. Here the three worlds are also denoted by the word "earth". So another mantra: यदींद्राग्नी अवमस्यां पृथिव्यां मध्यमस्यां परमस्या मुत स्थः (*yadīṃdrāgnī avamasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ madhyamasyāṃ paramasyā muta sthaḥ*) (Ṛ. 1-108-9); and in the Taittirīya, beginning योऽस्यां पृथिव्यामस्यायुष (*yo 'syāṃ pṛthivyāmasyāyuṣa*) and continuing *yo dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ* (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-12-1). Hence the three worlds are called "earth". Also, Viṣṇu propped up the higher, very wide common abode, the atmosphere that supports the three worlds, i.e. made it; so he is said to have created the three worlds resting on it.
Alternatively: the earthly realms are the seven worlds beneath the earth, which he made variously; the word rajas means world, since Yāska says "worlds are called rajāṃsi". And he propped up the higher abode, the group of seven worlds beginning with Bhūr, fit for the joint dwelling of the virtuous, i.e. created it. The root skambh takes the ending śnā by the rule of vyatyaya.
Or: the realms caused by the earth, the three worlds Bhūr etc.; the other worlds exist for the enjoyment of deeds earned on earth, so earth is their cause. And the higher, most excellent abode above all worlds, from which there is no return, is the Satyaloka, which he fixed firm. Doing what? Striding thrice, going variously through the worlds he created. Viṣṇu's threefold stride is famed in śruti such as विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे (*viṣṇurvi cakrame*) (Ṛ. 1-22-17). Hence he is "wide-praised" (urugāya), sung by many or greatly. I proclaim the heroic deeds of such a Viṣṇu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Viṣṇu
- पार्थिवानि (*pārthivāni*)—belonging to the earth
- रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—the colourful ones, the presiding deities of the three worlds in the forms of Agni, Vāyu and Āditya; or the seven worlds beneath the earth; or the worlds Bhū, Bhuvar and Svar that depend on the earth
- विममे (*vimame*)—made specially (and)
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Viṣṇu
- त्रेधा (*tredhā*)—thrice
- विचक्रमाणि (*vicakramāṇi*)—moving variously (through all the worlds he made)
- उरुगायः (*urugāyaḥ*)—praised by the great
- उत्तरं (*uttaraṃ*)—very wide
- सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*)—the atmosphere, support of the three worlds
- अस्कभायत् (*askabhāyat*)—made (such)
- विष्णोः (*viṣṇoḥ*)—of the all-pervading Viṣṇu
- वीर्याणि (*vīryāṇi*)—heroic deeds (feats of daring)
- नु कं (*nu kaṃ*)—very swiftly
- प्रवोचं (*pravocaṃ*)—I recite in praise

### Printed p. 566

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I swiftly recite and praise the heroic deeds of the all-pervading Viṣṇu, who specially made the earth and all worlds, who thrice moves variously through all the worlds he made, praised by the great, and who made the very wide atmosphere.

##### Printed English

Earnestly I glorify the exploits of Vishnu, who made the three worlds; who sustained the lofty aggregate site (of the spheres); thrice traversing (the whole); who is praised by the exalted.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Somātireka at the third pressing, the three Ṛks beginning प्र तद्विष्णुः (*pra tadviṣṇuḥ*) are to be included as anurūpa Ṛks in the śastra-mantra; this is set out in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the section सोमातिरेके (*somātireke*), by the sūtra प्र तद्विष्णुस्तवते वीर्येणेति स्तोत्रियानुरूप् (*pra tadviṣṇustavate vīryeṇeti stotriyānurūp*) (Ā. 6-7). And in the section वाजपेयेनाधिपत्य (*vājapeyenādhipatya*) it is likewise indicated by the sūtra प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्टनाम प्र तद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येण (*pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭanāma pra tadviṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇa*) (Ā. 9-9).
This is the first independent sūkta on Viṣṇu in the whole Ṛk-saṃhitā. Earlier, Ṛks 16 to 21 of sūkta 1-22 praise Viṣṇu, and Viṣṇu's nature and greatness learnt from that description were explained in the third part of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, pp. 19, 124-126, 132 to 135, as occasion arose. As this part contains two sūktas solely on Viṣṇu and one to Indra-Viṣṇu, some further special qualities not mentioned earlier are stated here. From these descriptions one can learn Viṣṇu's greatness and his place in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. Since there are disagreements about Viṣṇu's nature and this deity's place among Indra and the other deities, the personal opinions of Vedic and Western scholars were given in the introductory section of this same part. Here the points described in each Ṛk are explained. As in 1-32-1 Hiraṇyastūpa Aṅgirasa resolved "इंद्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्रवोचं (*iṃdrasya nu vīryāṇi pravocaṃ*)", so in this Ṛk Dīrghatamas Aucathya resolves "विष्टोर्नु कं वीर्याणि प्रवोचं (*viṣṭornu kaṃ vīryāṇi pravocaṃ*)". आग्निमारुतशस्त्रे आद्या विनियुक्ता (*āgnimārutaśastre ādyā viniyuktā*): the first Ṛk of these sūktas is applied in the Agnimāruta-śastra, says the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (5-20). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa states the greatness of this Ṛk thus.
ययोरोजसा स्कभिता रजांसीति वैष्णुवारुणीमृचं शंसति विष्णुवै यज्ञस्य दुरिष्टं पाति वरुणः स्विष्टं तयोरुभयोरेव शान्तैः । (*yayorojasā skabhitā rajāṃsīti vaiṣṇuvāruṇīmṛcaṃ śaṃsati viṣṇuvai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ pāti varuṇaḥ sviṣṭaṃ tayorubhayoreva śāntaiḥ |*)

### Printed p. 567
“ विष्णोर्नु कं वीर्याणि प्रवोच ”मिति वैष्णवीं शंसति यथा वैमत्यमेवं यज्ञस्य विष्णुस्तद्यथा दुष्कृष्टं दुर्मतीकृतं सुकृष्टं सुमतीकृतं कुर्वन्नियादेवनेवैतद्यज्ञस्य दुष्टुतं दुःशस्तं सुष्टुतं सुशस्त्रं कुर्वन्नेति यदेतां होता शंसति । (*“ viṣṇornu kaṃ vīryāṇi pravoca ”miti vaiṣṇavīṃ śaṃsati yathā vaimatyamevaṃ yajñasya viṣṇustadyathā duṣkṛṣṭaṃ durmatīkṛtaṃ sukṛṣṭaṃ sumatīkṛtaṃ kurvanniyādevanevaitadyajñasya duṣṭutaṃ duḥśastaṃ suṣṭutaṃ suśastraṃ kurvanneti yadetāṃ hotā śaṃsati |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-14)
In worldly affairs, मत्य (*matya*) is: मतौ बुद्धि सम्यक्त्वेन प्रतिभातं कार्यं मत्यं । यथा मत्यं कार्यं लोके फलपरवसायि भवति तथा विष्णुरपि फलपरवसायीत्यर्थः । (*matau buddhi samyaktvena pratibhātaṃ kāryaṃ matyaṃ | yathā matyaṃ kāryaṃ loke phalaparavasāyi bhavati tathā viṣṇurapi phalaparavasāyītyarthaḥ |*) As an act done with right discernment yields its fruit, so Viṣṇu too helps in sacrificial acts to obtain fruit. Moreover, as a man of excellent mind removes faults of a field and causes good plants to grow, and as a good minister rectifies the king's affairs spoiled by a bad minister, so Viṣṇu removes all faults arising in sacrificial acts and makes the sacrifice fruitful. Therefore it says: when the Hotṛ recites this Vaiṣṇavī, "विष्णोर्नु कं वीर्याणि (*viṣṇornu kaṃ vīryāṇi*)", the Ṛk in praise of Viṣṇu. "यः पार्थिवानि विममे रजांसि (*yaḥ pārthivāni vimame rajāṃsi*)" etc. are Viṣṇu's heroic deeds.
पार्थिवानि रजांसि (*pārthivāni rajāṃsi*): Sāyaṇa explains this in three ways. First: पृथिवी संबंधीनि रंजनात्मकानि क्षित्यादिलोकत्रयाभिमानीनि अग्निवाय्वादित्यरूपाणि । (*pṛthivī saṃbaṃdhīni raṃjanātmakāni kṣityādilokatrayābhimānīni agnivāyvādityarūpāṇi |*) That is, he made (vimame) the presiding deities of the three worlds, belonging to the earth, colourful, in the forms of Agni, Vāyu and Āditya. To the doubt how the epithet "earthly" suits the three worlds, he answers by citing śruti:
यदिंद्राग्नी अवमस्यां पृथिव्यां मध्यमस्यां परमस्यामुत स्थः । अतः परि वृषणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥ (*yadiṃdrāgnī avamasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ madhyamasyāṃ paramasyāmuta sthaḥ | ataḥ pari vṛṣaṇāvā hi yātamathā somasya pibataṃ sutasya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-108-9)
There अवमस्यां पृथिव्यां (*avamasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ*) is explained as "on the earth", मध्यमस्यां पृथिव्यां (*madhyamasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ*) as "in the atmosphere", परमस्यां पृथिव्यां (*paramasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ*) as "in the distant heaven". अत्र पृथिवीशब्दः त्रिष्टपि लोकेषु वर्तते । (*atra pṛthivīśabdaḥ triṣṭapi lokeṣu vartate |*) — the word earth applies to the worlds too, he makes clear again. Moreover,
वित्तायनी मेसि तिक्तायनी मेस्यवतान्मा नाथितमवतान्मा व्यथितं विदेरग्निर्नभो नामाग्ने अंगिरो योऽस्यां पृथिव्यामस्यायुषा नाम्नेहि यत्तेनाधृष्टं नानु यज्ञियं तेन त्वा दधेग्ने अंगिरो यो द्विती- (*vittāyanī mesi tiktāyanī mesyavatānmā nāthitamavatānmā vyathitaṃ videragnirnabho nāmāgne aṃgiro yo 'syāṃ pṛthivyāmasyāyuṣā nāmnehi yattenādhṛṣṭaṃ nānu yajñiyaṃ tena tvā dadhegne aṃgiro yo dvitī-*)

### Printed p. 568
यस्यां पृथिव्यामस्यायुषा नाम्नेहि यत्तेना धृष्टं नाम । (*yasyāṃ pṛthivyāmasyāyuṣā nāmnehi yattenā dhṛṣṭaṃ nāma |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-12-1)
Citing this Taittirīya-saṃhitā passage he shows that there too the three worlds are denoted by the word earth: अस्यां पृथिव्यां (*asyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ*), द्वितीयस्यां पृथिव्यां (*dvitīyasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ*), तृतीयस्यां पृथिव्यां (*tṛtīyasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ*). So "earthly realms" means: he made Agni, Vāyu and Āditya, the colourful presiding deities of the three worlds.
Second: citing the Nirukta-kāra's words लोका रजांस्युच्यंते (*lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte*) — worlds are called rajas by usage — पार्थिवानि पृथिवीसंबंधीनि पृथिव्या आधस्तन सप्तलोकान् विममे (*pārthivāni pṛthivīsaṃbaṃdhīni pṛthivyā ādhastana saptalokān vimame*): he created the seven worlds beneath the earth, Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasātala, Talātala, Mahātala and Pātāla.
Third: पार्थिवानि पृथिवीनिमित्तकानि रजांसि लोकान् विममे । भूरादि लोकत्रयमित्यर्थः । भूम्यां उपार्जितकर्मभोगार्धत्वात् इतरलोकानां तत्कारणत्वं। (*pārthivāni pṛthivīnimittakāni rajāṃsi lokān vimame | bhūrādi lokatrayamityarthaḥ | bhūmyāṃ upārjitakarmabhogārdhatvāt itaralokānāṃ tatkāraṇatvaṃ|*) The worlds Bhūr etc. were created to experience the fruits of all deeds done on earth and according to them, so the earth is the cause of the creation of those worlds. Hence he created the three worlds Bhūr etc. that have the earth as their cause. Sāyaṇa thus explains three possible meanings.
रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—रजो रजतेज्योर्ती रज उच्यते । उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका रचांस्युच्यंते ॥ (*rajo rajatejyortī raja ucyate | udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā racāṃsyucyaṃte ‖*) (Ni. 4-15)
Derived from the root raṃj, "to shine", the word rajas means light, water, and worlds. Other meanings possible for this word, with examples, are set out in detail on p. 58 of this same part. In the present Ṛk it may be said to mean shining worlds.
त्रीणि भांति रजांस्यस्य यत्पदानि तु तेजसा । तेन मेधातिथिः प्राह विष्णुमेनं त्रिविक्रमं ॥ (*trīṇi bhāṃti rajāṃsyasya yatpadāni tu tejasā | tena medhātithiḥ prāha viṣṇumenaṃ trivikramaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-24)
As the three worlds shine by Viṣṇu's three steps, so in the present Ṛk too it is natural that rajas means world.

### Printed p. 569
*(Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued)*

त्रेधा विचक्रमाणः (*tredhā vicakramāṇaḥ*)—स्वसृष्टान् लोकान् विविधं क्रममाणः (*svasṛṣṭān lokān vividhaṃ kramamāṇaḥ*): moving in various ways through the worlds he himself created. As described in Ṛks such as इदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे त्रेधा नि दधे पदं । समूळ्हमस्य पांसुरे ॥ (*idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame tredhā ni dadhe padaṃ | samūḷhamasya pāṃsure ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-17), त्रिभिः प्रकारैः पादं प्रक्षिप्तवान् (*tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ pādaṃ prakṣiptavān*). Sāyaṇa explains the sense as: he strode, or pervaded, placing his feet in three ways. This point will be explained in detail in the Special Topics of the next Ṛk.

उरुगायः (*urugāyaḥ*)—उरुभिः महद्भिः गीयमानः (*urubhiḥ mahadbhiḥ gīyamānaḥ*): one praised by great souls. This is one meaning. Taking उरु (*uru*) to mean "abundant", he gives another: अतिप्रभूतं गीयमनो ना (*atiprabhūtaṃ gīyamano nā*), one praised exceedingly and abundantly. Thus he has explained it in two ways.

उत्तरं (*uttaraṃ*)—उत्तर उद्धततरो भवति । उद्धततरोऽसौ उपरिष्ठादवस्थानात् (*uttara uddhatataro bhavati | uddhatataro 'sau upariṣṭhādavasthānāt*). The author of the Nirukta has explained it as "that which is exceedingly high" (Ni. 2-11). And, quoting the Ṛk आर्ष्टिषेणो होत्रमृषिर्निषीदन् देवापिर्देवसुमतिं चिकित्वान् । स उत्तरस्मादधरं समुद्रमपो दिव्या असृजद्वर्ष्या अभि (*ārṣṭiṣeṇo hotramṛṣirniṣīdan devāpirdevasumatiṃ cikitvān | sa uttarasmādadharaṃ samudramapo divyā asṛjadvarṣyā abhi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-98-5), in order to show that the word समुद्र (*samudra*) means the atmosphere (antarikṣa) here, he makes two divisions, the upper sea and the lower sea, and shows that the word उत्तर (*uttara*) means उपरिवर्तमानात् (*uparivartamānāt*), "situated in the upper part". In the present Ṛk also उद्दततरं (*uddatataraṃ*) means that which extends toward the upper region, and is an adjective of the word सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*); or it may mean अतिविस्तीर्णं (*ativistīrṇaṃ*), that which extends very widely.

सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*)—सहस्थानं लोकत्रयाश्रयभूतमंतरिक्षं (*sahasthānaṃ lokatrayāśrayabhūtamaṃtarikṣaṃ*). The word सधस्थ (*sadhastha*) means "a place of staying together". Only here does it refer to the atmosphere. It is also customary to call the place in the form of the altar (vedikā), where all the priests gather together, a सधस्थ (*sadhastha*). The author of the Nirukta (3-15), quoting the Ṛk कुह स्विद्योषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः । को नां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मरयं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥ (*kuha svidyoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karataḥ kuhoṣatuḥ | ko nāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ marayaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-40 / 10-40-2) **NOTE**, takes the word सधस्थ (*sadhastha*) there to mean "a place of staying together". Sāyaṇa takes it as the altar; the Nirukta-author takes it as a dwelling-place in the form of a house where all live together in common. In the same way, for the word त्रिषधस्थः (*triṣadhasthaḥ*) also (in Ṛks such as 6-8-7; 6-12-2 etc.) the meaning is given as लोकेषु सहावस्थानं (*lokeṣu sahāvasthānaṃ*)

### Printed p. 570

(see above). In the present Ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained it as the atmosphere that is the common support of the three worlds; or else as सहस्थानं पुण्यकृतां सहनिवासयोग्यं भूरादिलोकसप्तकं (*sahasthānaṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ sahanivāsayogyaṃ bhūrādilokasaptakaṃ*), the seven worlds beginning with Bhūr, in which the righteous can dwell together; or else as उत्तरं उत्कृष्टतरं सर्वेषां लोकानामुपरिभूतं सहस्थानं सत्यलोकं (*uttaraṃ utkṛṣṭataraṃ sarveṣāṃ lokānāmuparibhūtaṃ sahasthānaṃ satyalokaṃ*), the Satyaloka, which is above all worlds and the best of all.

विष्णोः (*viṣṇoḥ*)—अथ यद्विषितो भवति तद्विष्णुर्भवति विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा व्यश्नोतेर्वा (*atha yadviṣito bhavati tadviṣṇurbhavati viṣṇurviśatervā vyaśnotervā*). The Nirukta-author shows the derivation of this word as formed either from the root विश् (*viś*), which gives the sense "to pervade, or to enter so as to become one by joining with everything", or from the root व्यश् (*vyaś*) (नि + अशू (*ni + aśū*)). Then, quoting the Ṛk इदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे त्रेधा नि वधे पदं । समूळ्दमस्य पांसुरे ॥ (*idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame tredhā ni vadhe padaṃ | samūḷdamasya pāṃsure ‖*) (**NOTE**), he explains the Viṣṇu's pervasive nature **NOTE** described there.

नु कं (*nu kaṃ*)—The usages of these particles in different senses were stated earlier; here Sāyaṇa has explained it as अतिशीघ्रं (*atiśīghraṃ*), "very quickly". And: नु कं इति पदद्वयं (*nu kaṃ iti padadvayaṃ*). Although there are two particles, नु (*nu*) and कं (*kaṃ*), yet since Yāska has said नवोत्तराणि पदानि (*navottarāṇi padāni*) (Ni. 3-13), and since it is read as one word in another śākhā, this is included among the nine words that the author of the Nirukta has gathered as "read in all words"; hence, following the same rule, it is made one word नुकं (*nukaṃ*), and whatever meaning the word नु (*nu*) alone has, the same can be said for नुकं (*nukaṃ*).

##### Grammar

- विष्णोः — विष्‌ल्य व्याप्तौ इति धातुः । विषेः किच्च (उ. सू. ३-३१९) इति णुप्रत्ययः । कित्वविधानात् लघोपधगुणो न भवति । सित् इति पूर्वसूत्रादनुवृत्तत्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । षष्ठि विकवचनांतरूपं ।
- वीर्याणि — शूर वीर विक्रांतौ इति धातुः । अस्मात् णिच् आगते अचोयत् (पा. सू. ३-१-९७) इति यत्प्रत्ययः । णेरनिटि (पा. सू. ६-४-५१) इति णिचो लोपः । तित् स्वरितम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१८५) इति स्वरितस्वरो भवति । वीरशब्दविषये यतोनावः इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो न भवति इति (ऋ. स. १ ३२-१) इत्यत्र उक्तं ।

### Printed p. 571

- वोचम् — वच परिभाषणे इति धातुः । (अथवा) ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि इति धातुः । अस्य अर्धधातुकविषये वच्यादेशः । लुज् उत्तमपुरुषएकवचने अमादेशः । अस्यतिवक्ति इति च्लेः चणादेशः । वच उम् (पा.सू ७-४-२०) इति चज् परे उमागमः । गुणः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- पार्थिवानि — पृथिव्याः इमानि पार्थिवानि । पृथिव्याञ्ञाञौ इति अञ्प्रत्ययः । तद्धितेष्वचामादेः इति आदिवृद्धिः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- विममे — माज् माने इति धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने ममे इति रूपं भवति । यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (पा सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातप्रतिषेधात् प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तं भवति । तिजिचोदात्तवति (पा. सू- ८-१-७१) इति सूत्रेण गतेः (वि) अनुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- अस्कभायत् — स्कभि प्रतिबंधे इति धातुः । लज् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । स्तंभु स्तुंभु स्कंभु— (पा. सू. ३-१-८२) इति विहितस्य श्नाविकरणस्य छंदसि शायचपि (पा. सू. ३-१-८२) इति व्यत्ययेन शायचादेशः । आगमानुशासनमनित्यम् इति वचनात् नुमागमो न भवति । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । अडागमस्य उदात्तत्वात् आद्युदात्तं भवति ।
- सधस्थम् — ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ इति धातुः । सुस्थि स्थः (पा. सू. ३-२-४) इति कप्रत्ययः । आतो लोप इटि च (पा. सू. ६-४-९४) इति आकारलोपः । सधमादस्थयोष्छंदसि (पा. सू. ६-३-९६) इति सह इत्यस्य सधादेशः । द्वितीयाएकवचनांतरूपं ।
- विचक्रमाणि — क्रमु पादविक्षेपे इति धातुः । अस्मात् लडर्थे शानच् प्रत्ययः । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपः श्लुविकरणं । श्लुनिमित्तत्वात् धातोर्द्वित्वादि । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- त्रेधा — त्रिशब्दात् विधाच्च (पा. सू ५-३-४६) इति प्रकारार्थे विधाच् प्रत्ययः । चित्त्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- उरुगायः — गा स्तुतौ इति धातुः । अचो यत् (पा सू. ३-१-९७) इति यत् प्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन अंतोदात्तं भवति । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

> प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नाम प्र तद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येण । आ. ९-९ । इति ॥
> यस्येति वक्ष्यमाणत्वात् स इति अवगम्यते । स महानुभावो वीर्येण
> स्वकीयेन वीरकर्मणा पूर्वोक्तरूपेण स्तवते । स्तूयते सर्वैः ॥ कर्मणि व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ वीर्येण स्तूयमानत्वे दृष्टांतः । मृगो न सिंहादिरिव । यथा स्वविरोधिनो मृगयिता सिंहो भीमो भीतिजनकः कुचरः कुत्सितहिंसादिकर्ता दुर्गप्रदेशगंता वा गिरिष्ठाः पर्वताद्युन्नतप्रदेशस्थाया सर्वैः स्तूयते । अस्मिन्नर्थे

> भीत्यपादानभूतः । परमेश्वराद्भीतिर्भीषास्माद्वातः पवते । तै. आ. ८-८-१ । इत्यादिश्रुतिषु प्रसिद्धा । किंच कुचरः शत्रुवधादिकुत्सितकर्मकर्ता कुषु सर्वासु भूमिषु

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viniyoga: at the third savana, in the Somātireka, the śastra is to be performed; there प्र तत् (*pra tat*) is the anurūpa of the tṛca. In the khaṇḍa on Somātireka the Sūtra says: प्र तद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येणेति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*pra tadviṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇeti stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. 6-7). In the khaṇḍa on the Vājapeya for one desiring sovereignty it says: प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नाम प्र तद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येण (*pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa nāma pra tadviṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇa*) (Ā. 9-9).

Since यस्य (*yasya*) is to be said later, स (*sa*) ("he") is understood. That great one is praised by all (स्तवते (*stavate*) = स्तूयते (*stūyate*), with the passive sense, the affix śap by vyatyaya) through his own heroic deed (वीर्येण (*vīryeṇa*)) of the kind stated before. An illustration of being praised for prowess: मृगो न (*mṛgo na*), like a lion or similar beast. As a lion, the hunter of its adversaries, is fearful (भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*), causing fear), कुचरः (*kucaraḥ*) (the doer of base violence and the like, or one who goes to inaccessible places) and गिरिष्ठाः (*giriṣṭhāḥ*) (dwelling on high places such as mountains), and is praised by all. On this the Nirukta says: मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः । मृग इव भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठा मृगो मार्पर्गेर्गतिकर्मणो भीमो बिभ्यत्यस्माद्भिष्मोऽप्येतस्मादेव । कुचर इति चरतिकर्म कुत्सितमथ चेद्देवताभिधानं क्वायं न चरतीति वा । गिरिष्ठा गिरिस्थाया गिरिः पर्वतः समुद्दीर्णो भवति पर्ववान् पर्वतः पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा । (*mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ | mṛga iva bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhā mṛgo mārpargergatikarmaṇo bhīmo bibhyatyasmādbhiṣmo 'pyetasmādeva | kucara iti caratikarma kutsitamatha ceddevatābhidhānaṃ kvāyaṃ na caratīti vā | giriṣṭhā giristhāyā giriḥ parvataḥ samuddīrṇo bhavati parvavān parvataḥ parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātīrvā |*) (Ni. 1-20): मृग (*mṛga*) comes from the root मृग (*mṛga*) of motion; भीम (*bhīma*) is the one from whom one is afraid, and भिष्म (*bhiṣma*) also from the same; कुचर (*kucara*): चरतिकर्म कुत्सितं (*caratikarma kutsitaṃ*), or, if it is the name of a deity, "where does he not move?"; गिरिष्ठा (*giriṣṭhā*) is गिरिस्थाया (*giristhāyā*); गिरि (*giri*) is a mountain, "risen high"; a mountain is one with joints (पर्व (*parva*)), and पर्व (*parva*) is from *pṛṇāti* or *prīṇāti*. Both qualities apply to him: he is the seeker of enemies (मृगः (*mṛgaḥ*)), भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*), terrifying, the ablative-source of fear for all; this is well known in Śruti passages such as परमेश्वराद्भीतिर्भीषास्माद्वातः पवते (*parameśvarādbhītirbhīṣāsmādvātaḥ pavate*) (Tai. Ā. 8-8-1). Further, कुचरः (*kucaraḥ*) is the doer of base acts such as slaying enemies, or one who moves in all the earths (कुषु (*kuṣu*)), that is in the three worlds; and गिरिष्ठा (*giriṣṭhā*) is one who dwells in high worlds as a mountain does

### Printed p. 573

> लोकत्रये संचारी वा तथा गिरिष्ठा गिरिवदुच्छ्रितलोकस्थायी । यद्वा । गिरि
> मंत्रादिरूपायां वाचि सर्वदा वर्तमानः । ईदृशोऽयं स्वमहिम्ना स्तूयते ।
> किंच यस्य विष्णोरुरुषु विस्तीर्णेषु त्रिसंख्याकेषु विक्रमणेषु पादप्रक्षेपेषु
> विश्वा सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातान्यधिक्षियंति आश्रित्य निवसंति स विष्णुः स्तूयते !!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Or else: गिरि (*giri*) is speech in the form of mantras and the like, and he abides in it always. Such is he, praised for his own greatness. Moreover, that Viṣṇu in whose wide (उरुषु (*uruṣu*)), three-numbered strides (विक्रमणेषु (*vikramaṇeṣu*), placings of the foot) all (विश्वा (*viśvā*)) beings (भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*), creatures) dwell, resting upon them (अधिक्षियंति (*adhikṣiyaṃti*))—that Viṣṇu is praised.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Viṣṇu
- उरुषु (*uruṣu*)—in the very wide
- त्रिषु (*triṣu*)—and three-numbered
- विक्रमणेषु (*vikramaṇeṣu*)—placings of the feet
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—beings (or) all worlds
- अधि क्षियंति (*adhi kṣiyaṃti*)—abide, standing firm
- (and) यः (*yaḥ*)—which Viṣṇu
- मृगो न (*mṛgo na*)—like a wild beast such as a lion
- भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*)—terrible (to enemies)
- कुचरः (*kucaraḥ*)—one who harms (enemies) in a base manner, or one who moves in inaccessible places
- गिरिष्ठाः (*giriṣṭhāḥ*)—one who dwells in the high places of the mountains
- [(or) कुचरः (*kucaraḥ*)—one who moves in all three worlds; गिरिष्ठाः (*giriṣṭhāḥ*)—one who abides in speech in the form of mantras]
- तद्विष्णुः (*tadviṣṇuḥ*)—such a Viṣṇu
- वीर्येण (*vīryeṇa*)—with (his) heroic deeds
- प्रस्तवते (*prastavate*)—is praised supremely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Viṣṇu in whose placings of the feet, very wide and three in number, all beings abide firmly, and who, like a wild beast such as the lion, is terrible to enemies, harms enemies exceedingly, and dwells in the high places of the mountains—that Viṣṇu is especially praised along with his heroic deeds.

##### Printed English

Vishnu is therefore glorified, that by his prowess he is like a fearful, ravenous, and mountain-haunting wild beast, and because that in his three paces all worlds abide.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः (*mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ*). Here Viṣṇu is compared to a beast that is कुचर (*kucara*) and गिरिस्थ (*giristha*). Two kinds of meaning are given for the words कुचर (*kucara*) and गिरिष्ठ (*giriṣṭha*). First,

कुचरः (*kucaraḥ*)—कुत्सितहिंसादिकर्ता, दुर्गमप्रदेशगंता वा (*kutsitahiṃsādikartā, durgamapradeśagaṃtā vā*): one who harms enemies greatly, or who moves in fortresses and the like where others cannot move; this is an adjective of the beast

### Printed p. 574

. The author of the Nirukta, citing this same passage, shows this derivation for the word: कुचर इति चरतिकर्म कुत्सितं । अथ चेद्देवताभिधानं । क्वायं न चरतीति । (*kucara iti caratikarma kutsitaṃ | atha ceddevatābhidhānaṃ | kvāyaṃ na caratīti |*) (Ni. 1-20). If it is an adjective of the beast, the meaning is "one that moves crookedly". If it is explained with reference to the deity, the meaning is "where indeed can he not move?". Since Viṣṇu is all-pervading, there can be no obstruction to his movement anywhere. Therefore this adjective is most fitting for Viṣṇu.

गिरिष्ठाः (*giriṣṭhāḥ*)—गिरिः पर्वतः समुद्गीर्णो भवति (*giriḥ parvataḥ samudgīrṇo bhavati*). Because it spreads upward and high, a mountain is called गिरि (*giri*). [मेघोऽपि गिरिरेतस्मादेव (*megho 'pi giriretasmādeva*)—for this same reason the cloud also is called गिरि (*giri*). Ni. 1-20.] Since the beast dwells on mountains, the adjective गिरिष्ठाः (*giriṣṭhāḥ*) is used. Viṣṇu also being कुचर (*kucara*) and गिरिष्ठ (*giriṣṭha*), he is compared to the beast. Second—

कुषु सर्वासु भूमिषु लोकत्रये संचारी (*kuṣu sarvāsu bhūmiṣu lokatraye saṃcārī*). Since the word कु (*ku*) means "world", it means one who moves in all the worlds. गिरिष्ठः (*giriṣṭhaḥ*)—मंत्रादिरूपायां वाचि सर्वदा वर्तमानः (*maṃtrādirūpāyāṃ vāci sarvadā vartamānaḥ*): since the word गीर् (*gīr*) means speech in the form of mantras, and since Viṣṇu is established in speech in the form of mantras, he is explained also as गिरिष्ठ (*giriṣṭha*).

The word गिरिष्ठाः (*giriṣṭhāḥ*) is used as an adjective of Viṣṇu only in this one Ṛk. In other places this word is mostly an adjective of the Soma plant. In Ṛks such as परि सुवानो गिरिष्ठाः पवित्रे सोमो अक्षाः । मदेषु सर्वधा असि । (*pari suvāno giriṣṭhāḥ pavitre somo akṣāḥ | madeṣu sarvadhā asi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-18-1), the word गिरि (*giri*) is explained as the stone that presses out the Soma juice, and the meaning is the Soma that stands among such गिरि (*giri*)s, that is, among the pressing stones; and in places such as असाव्यंशुर्मदायाप्पु दक्षो गिरिष्ठाः । श्येनो न योनिमासदत् ॥ (*asāvyaṃśurmadāyāppu dakṣo giriṣṭhāḥ | śyeno na yonimāsadat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-62-4), the word गिरि (*giri*) is explained as "mountain" and the meaning is पर्वते जातः (*parvate jātaḥ*), Soma born on such a mountain. In the present Ṛk, it is an adjective of Viṣṇu, meaning either "dwelling on a mountain" or, since मेघोऽपि गिरिः (*megho 'pi giriḥ*) (Ni. 1-20), "dwelling in the cloud".

मृगो न (*mṛgo na*)—मृगो मार्षॆर्गतिकर्मणः (*mṛgo mārṣèrgatikarmaṇaḥ*). Formed from the root मृग् (*mṛg*) ("to seek", मृग अन्वेषणे (*mṛga anveṣaṇe*)) of the sense of motion; it gives the meaning "one who always moves about".

भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*)—भीतिजनकः (*bhītijanakaḥ*): the fearful one. मृगवदयमपि मृगोऽन्वेषा शत्रोणां भीमो भयानकः सर्वेषां भीत्यपादानभूतः (*mṛgavadayamapi mṛgo 'nveṣā śatroṇāṃ bhīmo bhayānakaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhītyapādānabhūtaḥ*). The wild beast, to other creatures

### Printed p. 575

*(Continuation of the Special Topics on Ṛk 2 of Sūkta 154.)*

Since (Ni. 1-20 **NOTE**) says so, [the word is a qualifier] of Viṣṇu, whether taken as "dwelling in the clouds" or otherwise.

*mṛgo na*—*mṛgo mārṣèrgatikarmaṇaḥ*: formed from the root *mṛg* (*mṛga anveṣaṇe*), which denotes movement, it gives the sense "always moving about." भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*)—*bhītijanakaḥ*: the terrifying one. *mṛgavadayamapi mṛgo 'nveṣā śatroṇāṃ bhīmo bhayānakaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhītyapādānabhūtaḥ*. Just as a beast of the forest is a cause of fear to other creatures and goes about searching for the animals that are its enemies, so Viṣṇu too seeks out his enemies and is a cause of fear to them. Not only enemies fear him: all the worlds fear him and keep to their own ordinances.

भीषास्माद्वातः पवते । भीषोदेति सूर्यः । भीषास्मावग्निश्चेंद्रश्च । मृत्युर्धावति पंचम इति ॥ (*bhīṣāsmādvātaḥ pavate | bhīṣodeti sūryaḥ | bhīṣāsmāvagniśceṃdraśca | mṛtyurdhāvati paṃcama iti ‖*) (Śrī. A. 8-8-1) **NOTE**. In such passages it is described that all the deities, the wind and the rest, fear this all-pervading Viṣṇu and perform their appointed duties. The same point is conveyed here.

त्रिषु विक्रमणेषु (*triṣu vikramaṇeṣu*)—त्रिसंख्याकेषु पादप्रक्षेपेषु (*trisaṃkhyākeṣu pādaprakṣepeṣu*): in the three kinds of steps (विश्वा भुवनानि अधिक्षियंति (*viśvā bhuvanāni adhikṣiyaṃti*)). What are these three steps, and where? There is disagreement on these matters. Western scholars have explained them as the three states of the sun: rising, standing at the zenith, and setting.

##### Printed English

This stepping of Vishnu is emblamatic of the rising, the culminating and setting of the sun.
[Max Muller. Sacred Books of the East. Vol. XXXI]. p. 133]

It is known from a Nirukta passage that ancient scholars such as Aurṇavābha also supported this meaning. समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यार्णवाभः (*samārohaṇe viṣṇupade gayaśirasītyārṇavābhaḥ*) (Ni. 12-19): thus the view of Aurṇavābha is stated. On this passage Durgācārya [explains]: समारोहणे—उदय गिरावुद्यन् पदमेकं निधत्ते । विष्णुपदे माध्यंदिनेंतरिक्षे । गयशिरसि—अस्तंगिरा । (*samārohaṇe—udaya girāvudyan padamekaṃ nidhatte | viṣṇupade mādhyaṃdineṃtarikṣe | gayaśirasi—astaṃgirā |*). The one foot to be placed in the form of the rising on the mountain of sunrise at sunrise, the second foot to be placed at the zenith in the atmosphere at midday, and the third foot to be placed on the mountain of sunset at sunset—these too are indicated by the sentence त्रेधा निदधे पदं (*tredhā nidadhe padaṃ*): such is the view of Aurṇavābha, as the Nirukta-author reports. Furthermore:

विष्णु स्त्रिधा निधत्ते पदं त्रेधाभावायु पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः । (*viṣṇu stridhā nidhatte padaṃ tredhābhāvāyu pṛthivyāmaṃtarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ |*) (Ni. 12-19). It is also stated that, in Śākapūṇi's view, this threefold placing of the foot indicates the three states of the sun, who moves in the three worlds: earth, atmosphere and heaven.

### Printed p. 576

On this Durgācārya [says]: पार्थिवोऽग्निर्भूत्वा पृथिव्यां यत्किंचिदस्ति तद्विक्रमते । अंतरिक्षे विद्युदात्मना, दिवि सूरात्मना । (*pārthivo 'gnirbhūtvā pṛthivyāṃ yatkiṃcidasti tadvikramate | aṃtarikṣe vidyudātmanā, divi sūrātmanā |*). He explains that in the forms of Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya Viṣṇu pervades the three worlds. Supporting this same meaning:

विष्णुमुखा वै देवाश्चंदोभि रिमांल्लोकाननपजय्यमभ्यजयन् यद्विष्णुक्रमान्नमते विष्णुरेव भूत्वा यजमानश्चंदोभिरिमांल्लोकाननपजय्यमभिजयति विष्णोः क्रमोस्यभिमातिहेत्याह गायत्री वै पृथिवी त्रैष्टुभमंतरिक्षं जागती द्यौरानुष्टुभीर्दिशश्चंदोभिरेवेमांल्लोकान् यथापूर्वमभि जयति । (*viṣṇumukhā vai devāścaṃdobhi rimāṃllokānanapajayyamabhyajayan yadviṣṇukramānnamate viṣṇureva bhūtvā yajamānaścaṃdobhirimāṃllokānanapajayyamabhijayati viṣṇoḥ kramosyabhimātihetyāha gāyatrī vai pṛthivī traiṣṭubhamaṃtarikṣaṃ jāgatī dyaurānuṣṭubhīrdiśaścaṃdobhirevemāṃllokān yathāpūrvamabhi jayati |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-5-4)

अन्या देवतासीथ्योब्रवीद्विष्णवेहीदमा हरिष्यावो येनायमिदमिति स विष्णुस्रेधात्मानं वि न्यधत्त पृथिव्यां तृतीयमंतरिक्षे तृतीयं दिवि तृतीय मभिपर्यावर्ताद्भ्यबिभेद्यत्पृथिव्यां तृतीयमासीत्तेनेंद्रो वज्रमुदयच्छद्विष्णवनुस्थितस्सोऽब्रवीन्मा मे प्र हारस्ति वा इदं ॥ (*anyā devatāsīthyobravīdviṣṇavehīdamā hariṣyāvo yenāyamidamiti sa viṣṇusredhātmānaṃ vi nyadhatta pṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamaṃtarikṣe tṛtīyaṃ divi tṛtīya mabhiparyāvartādbhyabibhedyatpṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamāsītteneṃdro vajramudayacchadviṣṇavanusthitasso 'bravīnmā me pra hārasti vā idaṃ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12-3)

In these Saṃhitā passages, and in

यद्वेव विष्णुक्रमान्मते । यज्ञोवै विष्णुः स देवेभ्य इमां विक्रांतिं विचक्रमे यैषामियं विक्रांतिरिदमेव प्रथमेन पदेन पस्पाराथेदमंतरिक्षं द्वितीयेन दिवमुत्तमेन्नैताम्वेवैष एतस्मै विष्णुर्यज्ञं विक्रांतिं विक्रमते तस्माद्विष्णुक्रमान्मते । (*yadveva viṣṇukramānmate | yajñovai viṣṇuḥ sa devebhya imāṃ vikrāṃtiṃ vicakrame yaiṣāmiyaṃ vikrāṃtiridameva prathamena padena paspārāthedamaṃtarikṣaṃ dvitīyena divamuttamennaitāmvevaiṣa etasmai viṣṇuryajñaṃ vikrāṃtiṃ vikramate tasmādviṣṇukramānmate |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-9-3-9)

यद्वेव विष्णु क्रमवात्सप्रे भवतः । विष्णु क्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिरिमं लोकमसृजत वात्सप्रेणाग्निं विष्णु क्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिरंतरिक्षमसृजत वात्सप्रेण वायुं विष्णु क्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिर्दिवमसृजत वात्सप्रेणादित्यं । (*yadveva viṣṇu kramavātsapre bhavataḥ | viṣṇu kramairvai prajāpatirimaṃ lokamasṛjata vātsapreṇāgniṃ viṣṇu kramairvai prajāpatiraṃtarikṣamasṛjata vātsapreṇa vāyuṃ viṣṇu kramairvai prajāpatirdivamasṛjata vātsapreṇādityaṃ |*) (Pa. Brā. 6-7-4-2) **NOTE**

and in such Brāhmaṇa passages too, in accordance with Śākapūṇi's view, a connection is shown between Viṣṇu's three feet, the earth, atmosphere and heaven, and the deities Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya. And further:

आ यो विवाय सचथाय दैव्य इंद्राय विष्णुः सुकृते सुकृत्तरः । वेधा अजिन्वत्रिषधस्थ आर्यमृतस्य भागे यजमानमाभजत् ॥ (*ā yo vivāya sacathāya daivya iṃdrāya viṣṇuḥ sukṛte sukṛttaraḥ | vedhā ajinvatriṣadhastha āryamṛtasya bhāge yajamānamābhajat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-156-5)

### Printed p. 577

In this Ṛk it is said that Viṣṇu himself pervades the three worlds, earth and the rest. As stated in the mantra Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 6-3-4-7, quoted above, the fact that Viṣṇu's three feet are the cause of the creation and the maintenance of the worlds, earth and the rest, is conveyed in the present Ṛk by अधिक्षियंति भुवनानि विश्वा (*adhikṣiyaṃti bhuvanāni viśvā*): all the worlds rest on the support that takes the form of Viṣṇu's three steps. Thus the greatness of Viṣṇu's steps is praised.

##### Grammar

- स्तवते — ष्टुञ् स्तुत् धातुः । कर्मणि लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने त प्रत्ययः । टेरेत्वम् । व्यत्ययो बहुलम् इति युकः स्थाने शप् विकरणं भवति । सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः इति इको गुणः । अवादेशः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- भीमः — भीमादयो अपादाने (पा. सू. ३-४-७४) इति औणादिकेन मर् प्रत्ययेन सिद्ध्यति ।
- कुचरः — कुत्सितं चरतीति कुचरः । चर गतिभक्षणयोः । पचादिषु पठितत्वाद् अच् प्रत्ययः । चित्त्वाद् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । कुषु चरतीति वा कुचरः ।
- गिरिष्ठाः — ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । गिरा तिष्ठतीति गिरिष्ठाः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- विक्रमणेषु — क्रमु पादविक्षेपे धातुः । भावे ल्युट् प्रत्ययः । युवोरनाकौ (पा. सू ७-१-१) इति तस्य अनादेशः । अट् कुप्वाङ् इति सूत्रेण प्रत्ययनकारस्य णत्वम् । लिति (पा. सू ६-१-१९३) इति प्रत्ययस्य पूर्वस्योदात्तस्वरो भवति । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- अधिक्षियंति — क्षि निवासगत्योः धातुः तुदादिः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । विकरणस्वरः अवशिष्यते । उदात्तवति तिजंते परे तिजिचोदात्तवति (पा. सू ८-१-७१) इति गतेः (अधि) निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- विश्वा — नपुंसके शि आदेशे जाते रूपे शेश्चंदसि बहुलं (पा. सू ६-१-७०) इति शेर्लोपः ।

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र विष्ण॑वे शू॒षमे॑तु॒ मन्म॑ गिरि॒क्षित॑ उरुगा॒याय॒ वृष्णे॑ ।  
> य इ॒दं दी॒र्घं प्रय॑तं स॒धस्थ॒मेको॑ विम॒मे त्रि॒भिरित्प॒देभिः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । विष्णवे । शूषं । एतु । मन्म । गिरिक्षिते । उरुगायाय । वृष्णे ।  
> यः । इदं । दीर्घं । प्रयतं । सधस्थं । एकः । विममे । त्रिभिः । इत् । पदेभिः ।  
> ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विष्णवे सर्वव्यापकाय शूषमस्मत्कृत्यादिजन्यं बलं महत्त्वं मन्म मननं
> स्तोत्रं मननीयं शूषं बलं वा विष्णुमेतु । प्राप्नोतु ॥ कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थी । कीदृशाय । गिरिक्षिते वाचि गिरिवदुन्नतप्रदेशे वा तिष्ठते उरुगायाय
> बहुभिर्गियमानाय वृष्णे वर्षित्रे कामानां । एवं महानुभावं शूषं
> प्राप्नोतु । कोऽस्य विशेष इति उच्यते। यो विष्णुरिदं प्रसिद्धं दृश्यमानं दीर्घमतिविस्तृतं प्रयतं नियतं सधस्थं सहस्थानं लोकत्रयमेक इदेक एवाद्वितीयः
> सन् त्रिभिः पदेभिः पादैर्विममे विशेषेण निर्मितवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To Viṣṇu, the all-pervading, may the strength (शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*))—the power, the greatness, produced by our rites and the like—and the मन्म (*manma*), a thought-worthy hymn (or: a thought-worthy शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*), strength), go; may it reach Viṣṇu. The dative is used because the action has him as recipient. Of what kind is he? गिरिक्षिते (*girikṣite*): he who abides in speech, or in a lofty place like a mountain; उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*): sung by many; वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*): the showerer of desires. May such strength of great power reach him. What is his special feature? It is said: Viṣṇu, who alone, being without a second, with three steps measured out specially this well-known, visible, very extensive, regulated common dwelling (सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*)), the three worlds.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Viṣṇu
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this well-known, perceptible
- दीर्घं (*dīrghaṃ*)—very extensive
- प्रयतं (*prayataṃ*)—lasting for a long time
- सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*)—existing together: the three worlds
- एक इत् (*eka it*)—alone (without anyone's help)
- त्रिभिः पदेभिः (*tribhiḥ padebhiḥ*)—with three feet
- विममे (*vimame*)—made; such a one
- गिरिक्षिते (*girikṣite*)—who abides in the speech that takes the form of praise, or who abides in a lofty place like a mountain
- उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*)—who is praised by many
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—who showers (desired things)
- विष्णवे (*viṣṇave*)—to Viṣṇu
- शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*)—great strength
- मन्म (*manma*)—a thought-worthy hymn
- एतु (*etu*)—may it approach and reach (may it be offered to Viṣṇu)

### Printed p. 579

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May great strength and a thought-worthy hymn be offered to that Viṣṇu who, without anyone's help, alone and without a second, with his three feet made the three worlds—this well-known, perceptible, very extensive, long-lasting, together-existing [dwelling].

##### Printed English

May acceptable vigour attend Vishnu, who abides in prayer, the hymned of many, the showerer (of benefits), who alone made, by three steps this spacious and durable aggregate (of the three worlds).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*)—अस्मत्कृत्यादिजन्यं बलं महत्त्वं (*asmatkṛtyādijanyaṃ balaṃ mahattvaṃ*): the meaning is strength produced by the sacrificial rites and the like of us (the sacrificers). The word शूष (*śūṣa*) is read among the names of strength such as ओजः (*ojaḥ*), पाजः (*pājaḥ*) (Ni. 3-9), and among the names of happiness such as शिंबाता (*śiṃbātā*), शतरा (*śatarā*) (Ni. 3-13). In the Ṛk-Saṃhitā the word is used in both senses.

सुतेसुते न्यूकसे बृहद्बृहत एवरिः । इंद्राय शोषमर्चति ॥ (*sutesute nyūkase bṛhadbṛhata evariḥ | iṃdrāya śoṣamarcati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-10)

In this Ṛk, with इंद्रस्य बलं पराक्रमं स्तौति (*iṃdrasya balaṃ parākramaṃ stauti*)—"he praises Indra's strength, his prowess"—the word शूष (*śūṣa*) is explained as strength; and

प्र मन्महे शवसानाय शूषमांगूषं गिर्वणसे अंगिरस्वत् । सुवृक्तिभिः स्तुवत ऋग्मियायार्चामार्कं नरे विश्रुताय ॥ (*pra manmahe śavasānāya śūṣamāṃgūṣaṃ girvaṇase aṃgirasvat | suvṛktibhiḥ stuvata ṛgmiyāyārcāmārkaṃ nare viśrutāya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-1)

here with शूषं अंगूषं (*śūṣaṃ aṃgūṣaṃ*)—"a hymn that is a cause of happiness"—the word शूष (*śūṣa*) is explained as happiness. In the present Ṛk it is explained as strength.

मन्म (*manma*)—मननीयं (*mananīyaṃ*): that which is of the nature of meditation. मननीयं स्तोत्रं मननीयं शूषं वा (*mananīyaṃ stotraṃ mananīyaṃ śūṣaṃ vā*): it may be a qualifier either of the hymn or of शूष (*śūṣa*).

प्रयतं (*prayataṃ*)—When the prefix प्र (*pra*) joins the root यम् (*yam*), the meanings are विस्त्रतं, दत्तं, नियतं (*vistrataṃ, dattaṃ, niyataṃ*): extended, given, and regulated. In the present Ṛk it is explained as नियतं (*niyataṃ*). Since it is a qualifier of the word सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*),

### Printed p. 580

it shows the aggregate of the three worlds that exist in a regulated, collective form and are a common dwelling.

गिरीक्षिते (*girīkṣite*)—वाचि गिरिवदुन्नतदेशे ना तिष्ठते (*vāci girivadunnatadeśe nā tiṣṭhate*): either "established in the speech that takes the form of mantra," or "dwelling in a place lofty like a mountain"; thus it is a qualifier of the word विष्णवे (*viṣṇave*).

एक इत् त्रिभिः पदेभिः विममे (*eka it tribhiḥ padebhiḥ vimame*)—"Without a second" means: without the help of others, he alone created all the worlds with his three feet; such is the purport. विममे (*vimame*)—विशेषेण निर्ममे (*viśeṣeṇa nirmame*): he made in an excellent manner.

##### Grammar

- एतु — इण् गतौ धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- विष्णवे — कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वात् संप्रदाने चतुर्थी इति चतुर्थी आगता ।
- मन्म — मन ज्ञाने । सर्वधातुभ्य मन् इति मन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वाद् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- गिरिक्षिते — क्षि निवासगत्योः धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । ह्रस्वस्य पितिकृति तुक् (पा. सू. ६-१-७१) इति तुगागमः । प्रथमव्याख्याने तत्पुरुषेकृति बहुलं इति सप्तम्या अलुक् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- वृष्णे — वृषु सेचने धातुः । कनिन्‌युवृषि- (उ. सू. १-१५४) इति कनिन् प्रत्ययः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । चतुर्थ्येकवचने अल्लोपोनः इति अनोऽकारस्य लोपः । **NOTE**
- प्रयतम् — यम उपरमे धातुः । क्त प्रत्ययः । अनुदात्तोपदेशवनति- (पा. सू. ६-४-३७) इत्यनुनासिकमकारस्य लोपः । गतिरनंतरः- (पा. सू. ६-२-४९) इति गतेः (प्र) प्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- विममे, सधस्थम् — अस्यैव सूक्तस्य प्रथममंत्रे व्याख्यातम् ।
- पदेभिः — बहुलं छंदसि इति भिस ऐस्भावस्य विकल्पत्वाद् अत्र न भवति । बहुवचने झल्येत् इति एत्वम् ।

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्य॒ त्री पू॒र्णा मधु॑ना प॒दान्यक्षी॑यमाणा स्व॒धया॒  ॑
> मदंति ।

> विश्वा ॥ ४ ॥
