> ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्य विष्णोर्मधुना मधुरेण दिव्येनामृतेन पूर्णा पूर्णानि त्रीणि पदानि
> पादप्रक्षेपणान्य क्षीयमणाक्षीयमाणानि स्वधयान्नेन मदंति मादयंति तदाश्रितजनान् । य उ य एव पृथिवीं प्रख्यातां भूमिं द्यामुत द्योतनात्मकमंतरिक्षं
> च विश्वा भुवनानि सर्वाणि भूतजातानि चतुर्दश लोकांश्च । यद्वा । पृथिवीशब्देनाधोवर्तिन्यतलवितलादिसप्तभुवनान्युपात्तानि । म्युशब्देन तदनांतररूपाणि भूरादि
> सप्तभुवनानि। एवं चतुर्दश लोकान् विश्वा भुवनानि सर्वाण्यपि तत्रत्यानि भूतजातानि।
> त्रिधातु । त्रयाणां धातूनां समाहारस्त्रिधातु । पृथिव्यप्तेजोरूपधातुत्रयविशिष्टं यथा भवति तथा दाधार । धृतवान् ॥ तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वं । उत्पादितवानित्यर्थः । छंदोगारण्यके । तत्तेजोऽसृजत तदन्नमसृजत ता आप ऐक्षंतेति
> भूतत्रयसृष्टिमुक्ता हन्ताहमिमास्तिस्रो देवतास्तासां त्रिवृतं त्रिवृतमेकैकां
> करवाणीत्यादिना त्रिवृत्करणसृष्टिरुपपादिता । छा. उ. ६-२-३ ; ६-३-३ । यद्वा ।
> त्रिधातु कालत्रयं गुणत्रयं वा दाधारेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of whom, that is, of Viṣṇu, the three steps (the three placings of the foot) are filled with honey, that is, sweet divine nectar, and are imperishable; with svadhā, food, they gladden (मदंति (*madaṃti*)) the people who take refuge in him. He alone, य उ (*ya u*), who has upheld the renowned earth and the shining atmosphere, and all beings, the fourteen worlds. Alternatively: by the word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) are meant the seven lower worlds, Atala, Vitala and the rest; by the word for heaven the seven worlds above them, Bhū and the rest; thus the fourteen worlds, and all the beings that live in them. त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) is the aggregate of three elements: he upheld them in such a way that the three elements, earth, water and fire, are included; the reduplicate of दाधार (*dādhāra*) is lengthened. The sense is "produced". In the Chāndogya Āraṇyaka, after stating the creation of the three elements ("that created fire, it created food, the waters thought…"), the creation by tripling is set out with "Let me make each of these three deities threefold" and so on (Chā. U. 6-2-3; 6-3-3). Or else: the construction is that he upheld the three times or the three guṇas.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of that Viṣṇu
- मधुना (*madhunā*)—with sweet nectar
- पूर्णा (*pūrṇā*)—filled
- पदानि (*padāni*)—the three placings of the foot
- अक्षीयमाणा (*akṣīyamāṇā*)—being without destruction

### Printed p. 582
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—with pure food
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—gladden (the people who take refuge)
- य उ (*ya u*)—that same Viṣṇu
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the renowned earth
- उत (*uta*)—and
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the shining atmosphere. [Or पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the seven lower worlds, Atala, Vitala and the rest; द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the seven upper worlds, Bhū and the rest.]
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—the (fourteen) worlds
- त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—as though joined with the three elements, earth, water and fire
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—alone
- दाधार (*dādhāra*)—has upheld (lifted and held)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The three steps of Viṣṇu, filled with sweet nectar and imperishable, gladden the people who take refuge in them with the gift of pure food. And that same Viṣṇu has upheld the seven lower worlds and the seven upper worlds, all the fourteen worlds, as though joined with the three elements, earth, water and fire.

##### Printed English

Whose three imperishable pices, filled with ambrosia, delight (mankind) with sacred food; who verily alone upholds the three elements, and earth and heaven.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मधुना पूर्णा पदानि स्वधया मदंति (*madhunā pūrṇā padāni svadhayā madaṃti*)—दिव्येन अमृतेन पूर्णानि पादप्रक्षेपणानि अन्नेन आश्रितजनान् मादयंति (*divyena amṛtena pūrṇāni pādaprakṣepaṇāni annena āśritajanān mādayaṃti*). The steps, sweet with divine nectar or like nectar, delight devotees and others with food; thus the nature of the steps and their fruit are praised.

स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—This word has been explained as "with food". That meaning hardly seems suitable in this context. Since in some places Sāyaṇa himself explains स्वधया (*svadhayā*) in two ways, आत्मीयेन तेजसा हविर्लक्षणेन अन्नेन वा (*ātmīyena tejasā havirlakṣaṇena annena vā*), the first meaning fits best here. The Nirukta-writers have included this word both among the names of water (Ni. 2-23) and among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). But in many contexts the word स्वधा (*svadhā*) also means one's own greatness, one's own brilliance, or self-support. For example, in
शश्वत्पुरोषा व्युवास देव्यथो अद्येदं व्यावो मघोनी । अथो व्युच्छादुत्तरा आनु म्यूनजरामृता चरति स्वधाभिः । (*śaśvatpuroṣā vyuvāsa devyatho adyedaṃ vyāvo maghonī | atho vyucchāduttarā ānu myūnajarāmṛtā carati svadhābhiḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-183-13)

### Printed p. 583
this word, used of Uṣas, is explained आत्मियैस्तेजोभिः (*ātmiyaistejobhiḥ*), "with her own brilliances". Likewise in
यदंतरिक्षे सतथः पुरुभुजा यद्वेमे रोदसी अनु । यद्वा स्वधाभिरधितिष्ठथो रथमत आ यातमश्विना ॥ (*yadaṃtarikṣe satathaḥ purubhujā yadveme rodasī anu | yadvā svadhābhiradhitiṣṭhatho rathamata ā yātamaśvinā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-10-6)
the sense is आत्मियैस्तेजोभिर्बलैर्वा सार्धं (*ātmiyaistejobhirbalairvā sārdhaṃ*), "with your own brilliances or with your own powers".
न मृत्युरासीवमृतं न तर्हि न रात्र्या अह्न आसीत्पकेतः । आनीदवातं स्वधया तदेकं तस्माद्भान्यन्न परः किं चनास ॥ (*na mṛtyurāsīvamṛtaṃ na tarhi na rātryā ahna āsītpaketaḥ | ānīdavātaṃ svadhayā tadekaṃ tasmādbhānyanna paraḥ kiṃ canāsa ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-2)
In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains स्वस्मिन् धीयते ध्रियते आश्रित्य वर्तते इति स्वधा (*svasmin dhīyate dhriyate āśritya vartate iti svadhā*): since it depends on itself, it is स्वधा (*svadhā*), an epithet of Māyā, the wondrous power of Īśvara (Parabrahman). Hence in the present Ṛk too it can be understood that Viṣṇu gladdens all the worlds by his brilliance, his greatness, and his extraordinary world-protecting power.
त्रीण्येक उरुगायो वि चक्रमे यत्र देवासो मदंति । (*trīṇyeka urugāyo vi cakrame yatra devāso madaṃti |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 35-29-2)**NOTE**
In such Ṛks it is said that Viṣṇu's stepping was in the worlds where even the gods rejoice; the same point is praised in the present Ṛk.
Where the expressions स्वधां अनु (*svadhāṃ anu*) or आनु स्वधां (*ānu svadhāṃ*) occur, the meanings are "naturally, by nature, according to custom"; this was shown earlier citing Ṛks 8-20-7; 7-56-13 and others. It was also shown that in 4-26-4 and similar places it means "chariot", and in 10-27-19 "army".
त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—त्रयाणां धातूनां समाहारस्त्रिधातु । पृथिव्यप्तेजोरूपधातुत्रयविशिष्टं यथा भवति तथा (*trayāṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samāhārastridhātu | pṛthivyaptejorūpadhātutrayaviśiṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathā*). It is explained as the totality of the three elements, earth, water and fire. And from the Chāndogya Upaniṣad:
तदैक्षत बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति तत्तेजोऽसृजत तत्तेज ऐक्षत बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति तदपोऽसृजत । .... .... ता आप ऐक्षंत बह्वः स्याम प्रजा- येमहीति ता अन्नमसृजंत । सेयं देवतैक्षत हंताहमिमास्तिस्रो देवता अनेन जेवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरवाणीति । तासां त्रिवृतं त्रिवृतमेकैकां करवाणीति सेयं देवतेमास्तिस्रो देवता अनेनैव जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरोत् । (छा. उ. ६-३-२, ३) ऎंब (*tadaikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti tattejo 'sṛjata tatteja aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti tadapo 'sṛjata | .... .... tā āpa aikṣaṃta bahvaḥ syāma prajā- yemahīti tā annamasṛjaṃta | seyaṃ devataikṣata haṃtāhamimāstisro devatā anena jevenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti | tāsāṃ trivṛtaṃ trivṛtamekaikāṃ karavāṇīti seyaṃ devatemāstisro devatā anenaiva jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākarot | (chā. u. 6-3-2, 3) èṃba*)
### Printed p. 584

(Chā. U. 6-3-2, 3)
Citing these sentences, Sāyaṇa says that here too is praised the greatness of Parabrahman, who created the three principles of food, water and fire, and upheld them by his greatness. This explanation is only one of the many explanations possible for the word त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*). In this very Ṛk Sāyaṇa himself also says: यद्वा । त्रिधातु कालत्रयं गुणत्रयं वा दाधारेत्यन्वयः । (*yadvā | tridhātu kālatrayaṃ guṇatrayaṃ vā dādhāretyanvayaḥ |*) It may mean that he upheld within his all-pervading principle either the three times, past, future and present, or the three guṇas, sattva, rajas and tamas.
अग्निरस्मि जन्मना जातवेदा धृतं मे चक्षुरमृतं म आसन् । अर्कस्त्रिधातू रजसो विमानोऽजस्रो घर्मो हविरस्मि नाम ॥ (*agnirasmi janmanā jātavedā dhṛtaṃ me cakṣuramṛtaṃ ma āsan | arkastridhātū rajaso vimāno 'jasro gharmo havirasmi nāma ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-26-7)
In this Ṛk the word त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) is explained प्राणापानव्यानात्मना त्रिधा वर्तमानोऽर्कोऽर्चनीयो यः प्राणोऽस्ति सोऽपि अहमेवास्मि (*prāṇāpānavyānātmanā tridhā vartamāno 'rko 'rcanīyo yaḥ prāṇo 'sti so 'pi ahamevāsmi*): the principle of breath in its three forms, prāṇa, apāna and vyāna. In
यद्देवाः शर्म शरणं यद्भद्रं यदनातुरं । त्रिधातु यद्वरूथ्यं १ तदस्मासु वि यंतनानेहसो व ऊतयः सु ऊतयो व ऊतयः (*yaddevāḥ śarma śaraṇaṃ yadbhadraṃ yadanāturaṃ | tridhātu yadvarūthyaṃ 1 tadasmāsu vi yaṃtanānehaso va ūtayaḥ su ūtayo va ūtayaḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-47-10)
it is explained as the three guṇas, sattva, rajas and tamas. Moreover, in
आ धर्णसिबर्ृहद्दिवो रराणो विश्वेभिर्गन्वोमभिर्हुवानः । ग्ना वसान ओषधीरमृध्रस्त्रिधातुशृंगो वृषभो वयोधाः ॥ (*ā dharṇasibarṛhaddivo rarāṇo viśvebhirganvomabhirhuvānaḥ | gnā vasāna oṣadhīramṛdhrastridhātuśṛṃgo vṛṣabho vayodhāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-43-13)
there is a description of Agni's flame. Here त्रिधातु शृंगः (*tridhātu śṛṃgaḥ*) is explained त्रिप्रकार शृंगवदुन्नतलोहितशुक्लकृष्णवर्णज्वालः (*triprakāra śṛṃgavadunnatalohitaśuklakṛṣṇavarṇajvālaḥ*): one whose flames rise high like horns, in three kinds, white, black and red.
त्रिरा दिवः सवितर्वार्याणि दिवेदिव आ सुव त्रिर्नो अह्नः । त्रिधातु राय आ सुवा वसूनि भग त्रातर्थिषणे सातये धाः ॥ (*trirā divaḥ savitarvāryāṇi divediva ā suva trirno ahnaḥ | tridhātu rāya ā suvā vasūni bhaga trātarthiṣaṇe sātaye dhāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-56-6)

### Printed p. 585
Here, as an epithet of वसूनि धनानि (*vasūni dhanāni*), त्रिधातूनि पशुकनकरत्नभेदेन त्रिप्रकाराणि (*tridhātūni paśukanakaratnabhedena triprakārāṇi*) is explained: wealth of three kinds, cattle, gold and jewels.
तव त्रिधातु पृथिवी उत द्यौर्वैश्वानर व्रतमग्ने सचंत । त्वं भासा रोदसी आ ततंथाजस्रेण शोचिषा शोशुचानः । (*tava tridhātu pṛthivī uta dyaurvaiśvānara vratamagne sacaṃta | tvaṃ bhāsā rodasī ā tataṃthājasreṇa śociṣā śośucānaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-5-4)
Here, in describing that the three worlds serve the vow of Vaiśvānara, त्रिधातु, पृथिवी, द्यौः (*tridhātu, pṛthivī, dyauḥ*) are named, and त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) is used as a synonym of the atmosphere.
तस्य यो योनिराशय आस। तमनु परामृश्य संलुप्याच्छिनत्सैषेष्टिरभवत्तद्यदेतस्मिन्नाशये त्रिधातुरिवैषा विद्याशेत तस्मात्त्रैधातवी नाम ॥ (*tasya yo yonirāśaya āsa| tamanu parāmṛśya saṃlupyācchinatsaiṣeṣṭirabhavattadyadetasminnāśaye tridhāturivaiṣā vidyāśeta tasmāttraidhātavī nāma ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 5-5-5-6)
From these sentences of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa it is known that at the slaying of the demon Vṛtra, because the knowledge consisting of the three Vedas was the basis, the iṣṭi performed on that occasion is famous as the Traidhātavī iṣṭi.
ततो वै स इमान् लोकाग्स्त्रेधादुहत्तत्रिधातोस्त्रिधातुत्वं यं कामयेतान्नादस्त्यादिति तस्मा एतं त्रिधातुं निर्वपेदिंद्राय राजे पुरोडाशं । (*tato vai sa imān lokāgstredhāduhattatridhātostridhātutvaṃ yaṃ kāmayetānnādastyāditi tasmā etaṃ tridhātuṃ nirvapediṃdrāya rāje puroḍāśaṃ |*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 2-3-6-1)
For the word त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) in these sentences of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā the commentary says: तिस्र एतास्त्रिधातोर्देवता लोकत्रयात्मिकाः । ततः खलु त्रिधातु देवतानां त्रित्वात्पजापतिः लोकत्रयव्यापी व्याप्तानिमान् लोकांस्त्रेधादुहत् त्रिप्रकारमदुहत् । त्रयो धातवो धनान्यस्मिन्निति त्रिधातुः, त्रेधा धातव्यत्वात्पुरोडाशस्य । यद्वा सर्वाधारलोकत्रयात्मकत्वात् त्रिधातुः ॥ (*tisra etāstridhātordevatā lokatrayātmikāḥ | tataḥ khalu tridhātu devatānāṃ tritvātpajāpatiḥ lokatrayavyāpī vyāptānimān lokāṃstredhāduhat triprakāramaduhat | trayo dhātavo dhanānyasminniti tridhātuḥ, tredhā dhātavyatvātpuroḍāśasya | yadvā sarvādhāralokatrayātmakatvāt tridhātuḥ ‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. Bhāṣya)
Thus, to the deities who dwell in the three worlds and in three forms, Prajāpati assigned the food in the form of the puroḍāśa at three times; and for the word त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) the meanings world, food, the three elements and so on are given.
Thus the word त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) is used in various places in different senses. In the present Ṛk it can mean the principles of earth, water and fire, or the times past, future and present,

### Printed p. 586
or the guṇas sattva, rajas and tamas. The purport is that the whole universe, with all its principles, rests in Viṣṇu's support.
Or: just as in Ṛk 7-5-4 quoted above the word त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) stands together with पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) and द्यौः (*dyauḥ*) as a synonym of the atmosphere, so in the present Ṛk too, since the names of the three worlds are indicated as त्रिधातु, पृथिवीं उतद्यां (*tridhātu, pṛthivīṃ utadyāṃ*), the meaning here may be the atmosphere. The purport is that all the worlds, earth and the rest, are in Viṣṇu's support.

##### Grammar

- त्री — नपुंसके शि आदेशे आगते त्रीणि इति रूपे जाते शेश्छंदसि बहुलं इति शेर्लोपः । एवं पूर्णा इत्यत्रापि रूपं भवति ।
- अक्षीयमाणा — न क्षीयमाणानि अक्षीयमाणानि । तत्पुरुषेतुल्यार्थ (पा. सू. ६-२-२) इति नञ् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । नपुंसकरूपे शेर्लुक् ।
- मदंति — मद तृप्तियोगे धातुः । अयमंतर्भावितण्यर्थकः प्रयुक्तः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । यच्छब्दसंबंधान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । तास्यनुदात्तेत् इति सूत्रेण लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ।
- त्रिधातु — डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । सितनिगमिमसि (उ. सू. १-६९) इति तुन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः भवति । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- दाधार — धृञ् अवस्थाने धातुः । लिट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने णलादेशः । धातोर्द्वित्वादि । तुजादीनां दीर्घोऽभ्यासस्य (पा. सू. ६-१-७) इति अभ्यासस्य दीर्घो भवति । यच्छब्दसंबंधान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य लित्त्वात् लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- विश्वा — पूर्ववद्बहुवचने शेर्लोपः ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अतिथ्यायां तवस्येत्येषा प्रधानस्य याज्या । अथातिथ्येति खंडे सूत्रितं ।

> अस्य महतो विष्णोः प्रियं प्रियभूतं तत्सर्वै सेव्यत्वेन प्रसिद्धं पाथः ।
> अंतरिक्षनामैतत् साथोऽंतरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यातं । नि. ६-७ । इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् ।
> अविनश्वरं ब्रह्मलोकमित्यर्थः । अश्यां । व्याप्प्नुयां । तदेव विशेष्यते । यत्र स्थाने
> देवयवो देवं द्योतनस्वभावं विष्णुमात्मन इच्छंतो यज्ञदानादिभिः प्राप्तमिच्छंतो नरो मदंति तृप्तिमनुभवंति । तदश्यामित्यन्वयः । पुनरपि तदेव विशेष्यते । उरुक्रमस्यात्यधिकं सर्वं जगदाक्रममाणस्य तत्तदात्मना अत एव विष्णोव्यापकस्य परमेश्वरस्य परम उत्कृष्टे निरतिशये केवलसुखात्मके पदे स्थाने
> मध्वो मधुरस्योत्सो निष्यंदो वर्तते । तदश्यां । यत्र क्षुत्तृष्णाजरामरणपुनरावृत्तादिभयं नास्ति संकल्पमात्रेणामृतकुल्यादिभोगाः प्राप्यंते तादृशमित्यर्थः । ततोऽधिकं नास्तीत्याह इत्येत्थमुक्तप्रकारेण स हि बंधुः स खलु सर्वॆषां सुकृतिनां बंधुभूतो हितकरो वा तस्य पदं प्राप्तवतां न पुनरावृत्तेः ।
> न च पुनरावर्तत इति श्रुतेस्तस्य बंधुत्वं । हिशब्दः सर्वश्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणादिप्रसिद्दिद्योतनार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa gives the ritual use first. In the Ātithya (guest-offering) rite this Ṛk, beginning तवस्य (*tavasya*) as he cites it, is the yājyā of the principal offering. The Sūtra in the section beginning *athātithyā* prescribes it: इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे तवस्य प्रियमभि पाथो अश्यां (*idaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame tavasya priyamabhi pātho aśyāṃ*) (Ā. 4-5).

He then explains the verse. "Of this great Viṣṇu the dear, i.e. beloved, that path, well known as to be resorted to by all": पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) is a name of the atmospheric region, since Yāska says साथोऽंतरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यातं (*sātho 'ṃtarikṣaṃ pathā vyākhyātaṃ*) (Ni. 6-7). It means the imperishable world of Brahman. अश्यां (*aśyāṃ*) is "may I pervade (attain)". The place is then characterised: it is the place where men who desire the god, that is, who wish to reach Viṣṇu, the shining one, by sacrifice, gifts and the like, rejoice, that is, experience satisfaction. The construction is "may I attain that."

Again the same is characterised: in the supreme, highest, unsurpassed station, consisting of pure bliss, of Viṣṇu the wide-strider, who pervades the whole world beyond measure and in the form of each thing and is therefore all-pervading, the Supreme Lord, there is a spring, a flow, of sweet nectar. That I would attain: a place where there is no fear of hunger, thirst, old age, death or return, and where by mere intention enjoyments such as streams of nectar are obtained. Nothing is higher than this. Then: "thus, in the manner said, he is indeed the kinsman", that is, he is the kinsman or benefactor of all the virtuous; for those who have reached his abode there is no return, and the Śruti says that one does not return, hence his kinship. The word हि (*hi*) points to what is well known from all Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇa and so on.

### Printed p. 588

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उरुक्रमस्य (*urukramasya*)—of him who widely (pervades the world) with his strides
- विष्णोः (*viṣṇoḥ*)—of Viṣṇu
- परमे (*parame*)—in the exalted
- पदे (*pade*)—in which place
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of sweet blissful nectar
- उत्सः (*utsaḥ*)—a stream (there is) (and)
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which place
- देवयवः (*devayavaḥ*)—those who strive to win Viṣṇu's favour
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—men
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—experience delight
- अस्य (*asya*)—of such a Viṣṇu
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—(to him) very dear, and
- तत् (*tat*)—well known, (resorted to by all)
- पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—the path of the atmospheric region
- अश्यां (*aśyāṃ*)—may I too attain
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in this manner
- स हि बंधुः (*sa hi baṃdhuḥ*)—that Viṣṇu is the kinsman (of all devotees)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May I too attain the atmospheric path, most dear to Viṣṇu, who in his vast strides pervades the whole world: the path in whose exalted station there is a stream of sweet blissful nectar, and where men who strive to win Viṣṇu's favour experience delight. In this way Viṣṇu is the kinsman even of all devotees.

##### Printed English

May I attain his favourite path, in which god-seeking men delight; (the path) of that wide-stepping Vishnu, in whose exalted station there is a (perpetual) flow of felicity; for to such a degree is he the friend (of the pious).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Soma sacrifice, when Soma is brought to the sacrificial ground, it is the custom to regard Soma (King Soma) as a guest and to perform rites such as the reception of a guest. This is stated in Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-1. The Ṛk तदस्य प्रियं (*tadasya priyaṃ*) is to be used then as the yājyā mantra of the principal offering; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section beginning अथातिथ्येति (*athātithyeti*), by the Sūtra इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे तदस्य प्रियमभि पाथो अश्यां (*idaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame tadasya priyamabhi pātho aśyāṃ*) (Ā. 4-5).

This Ṛk describes the greatness of Viṣṇu's supreme abode and expresses an intense wish to obtain the surpassing bliss found there.

पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—पाथः अंतरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यानतं (*pāthaḥ aṃtarikṣaṃ pathā vyākhyānataṃ*) (Ni. 6-7): the Nirukta says that पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) means the atmospheric region and that its derivation has been given where the derivation of the word पथिन् (*pathin*) was stated. It then quotes the Ṛk
यत्रा चक्रुरमृता गातुमस्मै श्येनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः । प्रति वां सूर उदिते विधेम नमोभिर्मित्रावरुणोत हव्यैः ॥ ( (*yatrā cakruramṛtā gātumasmai śyeno na dīyannanveti pāthaḥ | prati vāṃ sūra udite vidhema namobhirmitrāvaruṇota havyaiḥ ‖ (*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-63-5)
### Printed p. 589
and says इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*ityapi nigamo bhavati*), thereby showing that the word पाथ (*pātha*) is a synonym of the atmospheric region.

पंथाः पततेर्वा, पद्यतेर्वा, संथतेर्वा (*paṃthāḥ patatervā, padyatervā, saṃthatervā*) (Ni. 2-28): the derivation given for this word is that the form पंथा (*paṃthā*) may arise from any of the roots of motion पत् (*pat*), पद (*pada*) or पथि (पंथ्) (*pathi (paṃth)*). The word पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) also has these roots as its source; besides the sense "atmospheric region" it also means water and food.

उदकमपि पाथ उच्यते पानात् (*udakamapi pātha ucyate pānāt*) (Ni. 6-7): water too is called पाथ (*pātha*) because it is drunk. Having said this, the Nirukta quotes the Ṛk आ चष्ट आसां पाथो नदीनां वरुण उग्रः सहस्रचक्षाः । (*ā caṣṭa āsāṃ pātho nadīnāṃ varuṇa ugraḥ sahasracakṣāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-10), where पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) means water. And अन्नमपि पाथ उच्यते पानादेव (*annamapi pātha ucyate pānādeva*) (Ni. 6-7): since it is formed from the root पा (*pā*), which gives the sense of "to partake", food also has this name. It then quotes the Ṛk वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् । स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्धवींष्यवतां द्यावापृथिवी हवं मे ॥ (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān | svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavaddhavīṃṣyavatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī havaṃ me ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-10), where the word means food, as the Nirukta-author says.

In the present Ṛk the word is a synonym of the atmospheric region. It is said that this world is dear to Viṣṇu, that is, belongs to him. Therefore "god-seeking men rejoice": those who wish to win by sacrifice, gifts and the like the shining Viṣṇu, whom they desire for themselves, experience satisfaction. All sacrificers who wish to win his favour by pleasing the resplendent Viṣṇu through sacrifice, gifts and the like experience delight in this world.

उरुक्रमस्य विष्णोः (*urukramasya viṣṇoḥ*)—अत्यधिकं सर्वं जगदाक्रममाणस्य तत्तदात्मना अत एव व्यापकस्य परमेश्वरस्य । (*atyadhikaṃ sarvaṃ jagadākramamāṇasya tattadātmanā ata eva vyāpakasya parameśvarasya |*): this describes the nature of the all-pervading Viṣṇu, the Lord of the world, who pervades the whole universe by his own form.

परमे पदे (*parame pade*)—उत्कृष्टे निरतिशये केवलसुखात्मके स्थाने (*utkṛṣṭe niratiśaye kevalasukhātmake sthāne*): it is said to be a place wholly without sorrow, consisting only of happiness and supremely exalted.

### Printed p. 590
Therefore the word पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) too must be taken not in its commonly current sense of atmospheric region but as the excellent upper world. The nature of this supreme abode is described in the Upaniṣads thus:
यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः । स तु तत्सदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते ॥ विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनः प्रग्रहवान्नरः । सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं (*yastu vijñānavānbhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ | sa tu tatsadamāpnoti yasmādbhūyo na jāyate ‖ vijñānasārathiryastu manaḥ pragrahavānnaraḥ | so 'dhvanaḥ pāramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ*)
(Kaṭh. 3-8-9) **NOTE**
In the Kaṭha Upaniṣad the greatness of the supreme abode is praised: the self-controlled man who has gained spiritual knowledge and is endowed with the riches of calm, self-restraint and the like attains Viṣṇu's supreme abode and does not again become a transmigrating being. Hence this is not merely the commonly meant atmospheric region. The Muṇḍaka describes this same supreme abode:
सत्यमेव जयति नानृतं सत्येन पंथा विततो देवयानः । येनाक्रमंत्यषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानं ॥ (*satyameva jayati nānṛtaṃ satyena paṃthā vitato devayānaḥ | yenākramaṃtyaṣayo hyāptakāmā yatra tatsatyasya paramaṃ nidhānaṃ ‖*)
(Muṇḍaka. 3-1-6) **NOTE**
Seers whose desires are fulfilled and who know the supreme truth attain this most exalted world of Truth; this is the supreme abode. In this supreme abode there is "a sweet spring": a stream of the bliss of the Self. The nature of this bliss is described in the Upaniṣads:
सलिल एको द्रष्ट्वाद्वैतो भवत्येष ब्रह्मलोकः सम्राडिति हैनमनुशशास याज्ञवल्क एषास्य परमा गतिरेषास्य परमा संपदेषोऽस्य परमो लोक एषोऽस्य परम आनंद एतस्यैव आनंदस्यान्यानि भूतानि मात्रामुपजीवंति । (*salila eko draṣṭvādvaito bhavatyeṣa brahmalokaḥ samrāḍiti hainamanuśaśāsa yājñavalka eṣāsya paramā gatireṣāsya paramā saṃpadeṣo 'sya paramo loka eṣo 'sya parama ānaṃda etasyaiva ānaṃdasyānyāni bhūtāni mātrāmupajīvaṃti |*)
(Bṛ. U. 4-3-39)
and the like. Such unequalled bliss is not possible in any other world than this supreme abode. But even for obtaining this bliss Viṣṇu's favour is necessary; and for that favour the performance of sacrifice and other rites, and self-purification by calm, self-restraint and the like, are indispensable.

उत्सः (*utsaḥ*)—उत्थ उत्सरणाद्वोत्सदनाद्वोत्संदनाद्वोनत्तेर्वा (*uttha utsaraṇādvotsadanādvotsaṃdanādvonattervā*): the word उत्सः (*utsaḥ*) is formed from the root सृ (*sṛ*) combined with the prefix उत् (*ut*), meaning to spurt upward, to rise; or from the root सद् (*sad*) or स्यंद् (*syaṃd*); or from the root उद् (*ud*). It ordinarily means a spring or a well. The purport is "that which flows of itself without effort". The Nirukta-author (Ni. 10-8) quotes

### Printed p. 591
the Ṛk
अदर्दमुत्समसृजो वि खानि त्वमर्णवान्बद्वधाना अरम्माः । महांतमिंद्र पर्वतं वि यद्वः सृजो वि धारा अव दानवं हन् ॥ (*adardamutsamasṛjo vi khāni tvamarṇavānbadvadhānā arammāḥ | mahāṃtamiṃdra parvataṃ vi yadvaḥ sṛjo vi dhārā ava dānavaṃ han ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-1)
and explains the word उत्सं (*utsaṃ*) there as the cloud that flows forth, that is, the cloud that makes water stream in abundance.

Besides this, the word उत्स (*utsa*) is also read among the names of the well (Ni. 3-19). In the Ṛk
प्र ते नावं न समने वचस्युवं ब्रह्मणा यामि सवनेषु दाधृषिः । कुविन्णो अस्य वचसो निबोधिषदिंद्रमुत्सं न वसुनः सिचामहे । (*pra te nāvaṃ na samane vacasyuvaṃ brahmaṇā yāmi savaneṣu dādhṛṣiḥ | kuvinṇo asya vacaso nibodhiṣadiṃdramutsaṃ na vasunaḥ sicāmahe |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-16-7)
the explanation is जलस्य निधानभूतं कूपं (*jalasya nidhānabhūtaṃ kūpaṃ*), that is, a well which is the receptacle of water. In
शतधारमुत्समक्षीयमाणं विपश्चितं पितरं वक्तानां । मेळिं मदंतं पित्रोरुपस्थे तं रोदसी पिपृतं सत्यवाचं ॥ (*śatadhāramutsamakṣīyamāṇaṃ vipaścitaṃ pitaraṃ vaktānāṃ | meḷiṃ madaṃtaṃ pitrorupasthe taṃ rodasī pipṛtaṃ satyavācaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-26-9)
the explanation is सततप्रवाहोपेतं स्रोतः (*satatapravāhopetaṃ srotaḥ*), that is, a river with an unbroken flow.

In the present Ṛk also उत्स (*utsa*) means a stream of bliss that flows of itself, abundant and unbroken. This is a description of the surpassing bliss of Viṣṇu's world. Since he is the cause of such bliss, Viṣṇu is famed as the kinsman of all. What is praised in Upaniṣadic passages such as
स नो बंधुर्जुनिता स विधाता धामानि वेद भुवनानि विश्वा । (*sa no baṃdhurjunitā sa vidhātā dhāmāni veda bhuvanāni viśvā |*)
(Tai. U. 4-1-6) **NOTE**
is stated here.

##### Grammar

- पाथः—पा रक्षणे धातुः । उदकॆ थुट् च (उ. सू. ४-६४३) इति असुन् प्रत्ययः । धातोः थुट् आगमः । अत्र पाथोंतरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यातम् (निरु. ६-७) इति निर्वचनकरणात् अंतरिक्षार्थे प्रयुक्तम् ।
- अश्याम्—अशू व्याप्तौ धातुः । लिज् उत्तमपुरुषएकवचने परे बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । लिजः यासुट् आगमः । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- देवयवः—देवान् आत्मनः इच्छति इति अर्थविवक्षायां सुप आत्मनः क्याच् (पा सू. ३-१.-८) इति क्याच् । देवयति इति देवयुः क्याच्छंदसि (पा. सू. ३-२-१७०) इति क्यजंतात् उ प्रत्ययः । **NOTE**

### Printed p. 592
- देवयवः (अनुवृत्तिः)—अतो लोपः (पा. सू.६-४-४८) इति क्यचः अकारस्य लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
- मदंति—पूर्वमंत्रे व्याख्यातम् । यत्र इति पूर्वस्मिन् वर्तमानत्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति, धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
- बंधु—बंध बंधने धातुः । शृष्टस्निहि- (उ. सू १-१०) इति उ प्रत्ययः । धान्येनित् सूत्रात् नित् इति अनुवृत्तत्वात् इत्यादिर्नित्यम् इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- इत्था—इदमस्थमुः इति थमुप्रत्ययः । सुपां सुलुक्- इति तृतीयाविभक्तौ परस्यां तस्याः डा आदेशः ।
- मध्वः—जसादिषु छंदसि वा वचनम् इति षष्ठीएकवचने परे गुणादयः न भवंति । यणादेशः ।

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता वां॒ वास्तू॑न्युश्मसि॒ गम॑ध्यै॒ यत्र॒ गावो॒ भूरि॑शृंगा  ॒॑
> अयासः ।  
> अत्राह॒ तदु॑रुगा॒यस्य॒ वृष्णः॑ पर॒मं प॒दमन॑ भाति॒ भूरि॑ ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । वां । वास्तूनि । उष्मसि । गमध्यै । यत्र । गावः । भूरिशृंगाः । अयासः ।  
> अत्र । अह । तत् । उरुगायस्य । वृष्णः । परमं । पदं । अव । भाति । भूरि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पत्नीयजमान् नां युष्मदर्थं ता तानि गंतव्यत्वेन प्रसिद्धानि वास्तूनि
> सुखनिवासयोग्यानि स्थानानि गमध्यै युवयोग्रमनायोश्मसि । कामायामहे ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O wife and sacrificer" **NOTE**: for you, "those", that is, the well-known places to be gone to, the वास्तूनि (*vāstūni*), places fit for a pleasant dwelling, we desire "for going", that is, for your going. (The explanation continues in the next block.)

### Printed p. 593

> तदर्थं विष्णुं प्रार्थयाम इत्यर्थः । तानीत्युक्तं कानीत्याह । यत्र येषु
> वास्तुषु गावो रश्मयो भूरिशृंगा अत्यंतोन्नत्युपेता बहुभिराश्रयणीया
> वायासोऽयना गंतारोऽतिविस्तृताः । यद्वा । यासो गंतारः । अतादृशाः ।
> अत्यंतप्रकाशयुक्ता इत्यर्थः । अत्राहात्र खलु वास्ताधारभूते द्युलोक उरुगायस्य बहुभिर्महात्मभिर्गातव्यस्य स्तुत्यस्य वृष्णः कामानां वर्षितुर्विष्टोस्तत्तादृशं
> सर्वत्र पुराणादिषु गंतव्यत्वेन प्रसिद्धं परमं निरतिशयं पदं स्थानं भूर्यतिप्रभूतमव भाति । स्वमहिम्ना स्पुरति । अयं मंत्रो यास्केन गोशब्दो रश्मिवाचक
> इति व्याचक्षाणेन व्याख्यातः । तानि वां वास्तूनि कामायामहे गमनाय यत्र
> गावो भूरिशृंगा बहुश्चंगा भूरीति बहुनो नामधेयं प्रभवतीति सतः शृंगं
> श्रयतेर्वा शृणातेर्वा शम्मातेर्वा शरणायोद्गतमिति ना शिरसो निर्गतमिति
> वायासोऽयनाः । तत्र तदुरुगायस्य विष्णोर्महागतेः परमं पदं पराध्यस्थमवभाति भूरि । पादः पद्यतेः । नि. २-७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For that purpose we pray to Viṣṇu. Having said "those", he says which: those dwellings in which the गावः (*gāvaḥ*), the rays, are भूरिशृंगाः (*bhūriśṛṃgāḥ*), endowed with very high rising, to be resorted to by many; and the अयासः (*ayāsaḥ*) are the goers, far-spreading. Or else the यासः (*yāsaḥ*) are goers, and अ-यासः (*a-yāsaḥ*) means those unlike (ordinary goers), that is, endowed with great brilliance. अत्राह (*atrāha*): here, in this heavenly world which is the support of those dwellings, of the wide-sung one, to be sung by many great souls, that is, to be praised, of the showerer of desires, Viṣṇu, that supreme, unsurpassed station, well known everywhere in the Purāṇas and elsewhere as a goal, shines forth abundantly by its own greatness. Yāska explains this mantra, saying that the word गो (*go*) denotes rays. He also explains भूरि (*bhūri*) as a name of "much", and gives derivations of शृंग (*śṛṃga*) (from श्रय (*śraya*), शृ (*śṛ*) or श्या (*śyā*) roots; "risen up for shelter", or "issued from the head"); there the supreme station of Viṣṇu of the great stride, the highest, shines abundantly. Then पादः पद्यतेः (*pādaḥ padyateḥ*) (Ni. 2-7).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नां (*nāṃ*)—(O wives of the sacrificer) for you **NOTE**
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which regions
- भूरिशृंगाः (*bhūriśṛṃgāḥ*)—rising very high
- आयासः (*āyāsaḥ*)—very wide-spreading or else very resplendent
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—rays (spread)
- ता (*tā*)—those (that all wish to go to), well known
- वास्तूनि (*vāstūni*)—abodes of pleasant dwelling
- गमध्यॆ (*gamadhyè*)—that you too may go there
- उश्मसि (*uśmasi*)—we desire (and for that we pray to Viṣṇu)
- अत्राह (*atrāha*)—here, however
- उरुगायस्य (*urugāyasya*)—of him who is praised by many great souls, and
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—of the giver of desired ends
- परमं (*paramaṃ*)—the highest (above all), most surpassing
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—station
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—abundantly
- अव भाति (*ava bhāti*)—shines (by its own greatness)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wives of the sacrificers, we pray to Viṣṇu with the aim that you too may go and reach those pleasant dwelling-places, which all wish to go to and where rays rising very high and very resplendent are spread. Here the most surpassing station of Viṣṇu, who is praised by many great souls and showers down desired ends, shines forth abundantly by its own greatness.

##### Printed English

We pray (to Vishnu) that you may both go to those regions where the many-pointed and wide-spreading rays (of light expand); for here the supreme

### Printed p. 594

##### Printed English

station of the many-bymned, the showerer (of benefits), shines (with) great
(splendour).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The pandit Roth remarks that this Ṛk would be more fitting in a hymn addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa than in the Viṣṇu hymn, and he states his opinion as follows.
"This verse occurs in a hymn to Vishnu; consequently the dual वां (*vāṃ*) cannot refer to the deity of the hymn. Durga meets the difficulty, as the commentators frequently do with inconvenient duals, by saying वां इति दंपती अभीप्रेत्य (*vāṃ iti daṃpatī abhīpretya*) Etc. But here we have rather a proof of the fact that, in the arrangement of the Veda, many verses have been inserted in wrong places. The verse is addressed to Mitra and Varuna ; and perhaps, belonged to one of the hymns to those two Gods which immediately precede Riks in the Samhita. The verse has been introduced into the wrong place because Vishnu is referred to in it ".
(Quoted in Muir's Original Sanskrit Texts Vol. IV. P. 73-74)

This Ṛk addresses Mitra and Varuṇa with वां (*vāṃ*), and it has been included in the Viṣṇu hymn only because Viṣṇu's name is mentioned in it; there is no proper reason for its being here. Durgācārya, however, in explaining the Nirukta passage, says that वां (*vāṃ*) refers to the married couple who are the sacrificers. Roth's opinion is that this is not very reasonable. Sāyaṇa too takes the sense suggested by the word वां (*vāṃ*) as concerning the couple: हे पत्नीयजमानौ वां युष्मदर्थं (*he patnīyajamānau vāṃ yuṣmadarthaṃ*), "O wife and sacrificer, for you". The Nirukta-kāra has explained this Ṛk in this way:
तानि नां वास्तूनि कामयामहे गमनाय यत्र गावो भूरिशृंगाः । बहुशृंगा भूरीति बहुनो नामधेयं प्रभवतीति सतः । शृंगं श्रयतेर्वा, शृणातेर्वा, शम्ना तेर्वा शरणायोद्धतमिति ना शिरसो निर्गतमिति वायासोऽयनाः । तत्र तदुरुगायस्य विष्णोर्महागतेः परमं पवं परार्ध्यस्थमवभाति भूरि । पादः पद्यतेः ॥ (*tāni nāṃ vāstūni kāmayāmahe gamanāya yatra gāvo bhūriśṛṃgāḥ | bahuśṛṃgā bhūrīti bahuno nāmadheyaṃ prabhavatīti sataḥ | śṛṃgaṃ śrayatervā, śṛṇātervā, śamnā tervā śaraṇāyoddhatamiti nā śiraso nirgatamiti vāyāso 'yanāḥ | tatra tadurugāyasya viṣṇormahāgateḥ paramaṃ pavaṃ parārdhyasthamavabhāti bhūri | pādaḥ padyateḥ ‖*)
(Ni. 9-7)
The meaning is that the supreme station of Viṣṇu, established in the most excellent place, shines exceedingly. The Nirukta-kāra has cited this Ṛk incidentally, to explain the meaning of the word गावः (*gāvaḥ*).

### Printed p. 595
All rays are called गावः (*gāvaḥ*); since the name गावः (*gāvaḥ*) is well known for rays (Ni. 2-7), here too गावः (*gāvaḥ*) means rays. [The different meanings of the word गो (*go*), such as the sun, were given earlier with examples.] The two words भूरिशृंगाः (*bhūriśṛṃgāḥ*) and अयासः (*ayāsaḥ*) are qualifiers of this word.
भूरिशृंगाः (*bhūriśṛṃgāḥ*)—भूरीति बहुनो नामधेयं (*bhūrīti bahuno nāmadheyaṃ*). The word भूरि (*bhūri*) is used to show that something is numerous. And the word शृंग (*śṛṃga*) may be formed from the root श्रि (*śri*) meaning "to resort to", or from the root शृ (*śṛ*) meaning "to injure", or from the root शं (*śaṃ*) showing the same meaning. The Nirukta-kāra explains that the name शृंग (*śṛṃga*) is well known either because it protects living beings or because it grows out of the head and projects outward. (2-7).
अयासः (*ayāsaḥ*)—आयनाः (*āyanāḥ*). It is a qualifier of the rays, meaning that they move very swiftly. Sāyaṇa explains: अयना गंतारोऽतिविस्तृताः (*ayanā gaṃtāro 'tivistṛtāḥ*) ("moving, very widespread"). यद्वा यासो गंतारः (*yadvā yāso gaṃtāraḥ*) अतादृशाः (*atādṛśāḥ*) अत्यंतप्रकाशयुक्ता इत्यर्थः (*atyaṃtaprakāśayuktā ityarthaḥ*): it can mean "spreading very widely" or "having widespread light". This qualifier is used frequently in the sense of "those who move continually" or "that which moves everywhere".
तपो ष्टग्ने अंतरा अमित्रान् तपा शंसमरुषः परस्य । तपो वसो चिकितानो अचित्तान्वि ते तिष्यंतामजरा अयासः ॥ (*tapo ṣṭagne aṃtarā amitrān tapā śaṃsamaruṣaḥ parasya | tapo vaso cikitāno acittānvi te tiṣyaṃtāmajarā ayāsaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-2)
In such Ṛks, as a qualifier of the rays, it means "moving everywhere" (सर्वत्र गमनाः संतः (*sarvatra gamanāḥ saṃtaḥ*)). Likewise, in the same sense, it is used as a qualifier of the Maruts.
उश्मसि (*uśmasi*)—वश्मि (*vaśmi*), उश्मसि (*uśmasi*), वेति (*veti*) and others are read among the eighteen names of acts of propitiation. (Ni. 3-9). In the present Ṛk, कामयामहे (*kāmayāmahe*) means विष्णुं प्रार्थयामहे (*viṣṇuṃ prārthayāmahe*), "we pray to Viṣṇu"; the commentator has understood it as "we pray for you", addressing the couple.
वास्तूनि (*vāstūni*)—सुखनिवासयोग्यानि (*sukhanivāsayogyāni*), that is, dwelling-places most productive of happiness. पदे परमे मध्व उत्सः (*pade parame madhva utsaḥ*): since in Viṣṇu's supreme station the highest, unequalled bliss is obtained without interruption, the meaning is "we pray that such a dwelling-place may be obtained by you also". यत्र भूरिशृंगा आयासः गावः (विद्य्यंते) अत्राह उरुगायस्य परमं पदं भूरि अवभाति (*yatra bhūriśṛṃgā āyāsaḥ gāvaḥ (vidyyaṃte) atrāha urugāyasya paramaṃ padaṃ bhūri avabhāti*): where there are rays that are, as described above, very bright, lofty, spreading upward and numerous, there the supremely blissful supreme station of Viṣṇu is established.

### Printed p. 596
Although this is a description of the supreme station, the main subject of this hymn is the description of the three places of Viṣṇu's strides, their greatness, and the support of all the worlds comprised within these strides. In these descriptions, the matter to be explained by qualifiers such as विचक्रमाणि (*vicakramāṇi*), त्रिषु विक्रमणेषु (*triṣu vikramaṇeṣu*), त्रिभिरित्पदेभिः (*tribhiritpadebhiḥ*), त्री पूर्णा मधुना पदानि (*trī pūrṇā madhunā padāni*) deserves consideration. For in general all these qualifiers also suggest the special features of the Vāmana incarnation described in the Purāṇic works. In the Ṛksaṃhitā no story concerning the Vāmana incarnation, nor any other kind of reference to it, is directly seen. Yet the Trivikrama described here has become, as it were, the basis of the story of the Vāmana incarnation praised in the Purāṇas. Sāyaṇa too, in the commentary on the Ṛk
अतो देवा अवंतु नो यतो विष्णुर्विचक्रमे । पृथिव्याः सप्त धामभिः ॥ (*ato devā avaṃtu no yato viṣṇurvicakrame | pṛthivyāḥ sapta dhāmabhiḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22 6)
has said विष्णोः त्रिविक्रमावतारे पादत्रयक्रमणस्य (*viṣṇoḥ trivikramāvatāre pādatrayakramaṇasya*): that in the description of the Ṛk cited there there is a reference to the stepping of the three feet spread out at the time of the Trivikrama incarnation. But when the next Ṛk (1-22-17) is explained, the words of the Nirukta-kāra contain no hint relating to this story. Moreover, in the statements of Śākapūṇi or of Aurṇavābha that Yāska cites, there is no statement relating to this story.
The description of the Vāmana story is found in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as well. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the help given to the gods by Viṣṇu in the form of a dwarf, at the time of the fight between gods and Asuras, is told as follows.
देवाश्च वा असुराश्च । उभये प्राजापत्याः पस्पधिरे ततो देवा अनुव्यमिवासुरथ्य हासुरा मेनिरेऽस्माकमेवेदं खलु भुवनमिति ॥ ते होचुः । हंतेमां पृथिवीं विभजामहै तां विभज्योपजीवामेति ताम् क्ष्णुर्मभिः पश्चात्प्रांचो विभजमानाअभीयु ॥ तद्वै देवाः शुक्रुव । विभजंते ह वा इमामसुराः पृथिवीं प्रेत तदेष्यामो यत्रेमामसुरा विभजंतेके ततः स्याम यदस्यैन भजेमहीति ते यज्ञमेव विष्णुं पुरस्कृत्येयुः ॥ ते होचुः । अनु नोऽस्मां पृथिव्यामाभजतास्तेव नोऽप्यस्यां भाग इति ते हासुरा असूयंत इवोचुर्यावदेवैष विष्णुरभिशेते तावद्यो वद्द इति ॥ वामनो ह विष्णुरास । तद्देवा न जिहीडिरे महद्वै नोदुरै नो यज्ञसंमितमदुरिति । ते प्रांचं विष्णुं निपाद्य । छंदोभिरभितः परग्रहन् गायत्रेण ता छंदसा परिगृह्णामीति दक्षिणतस्रैष्टुभेन त्वा छंदसा परिगृह्णामीति पश्चाज्जागतेन त्वा च्छंदसा परिगृह्णामीत्युत्तरतः ॥ तं छंदोभिरभितः परिगृह्य ॥ .... .... .... .... सौम्यस्याध्वरस्य वेदिं चक्रे ॥ (*devāśca vā asurāśca | ubhaye prājāpatyāḥ paspadhire tato devā anuvyamivāsurathya hāsurā menire 'smākamevedaṃ khalu bhuvanamiti ‖ te hocuḥ | haṃtemāṃ pṛthivīṃ vibhajāmahai tāṃ vibhajyopajīvāmeti tām kṣṇurmabhiḥ paścātprāṃco vibhajamānāabhīyu ‖ tadvai devāḥ śukruva | vibhajaṃte ha vā imāmasurāḥ pṛthivīṃ preta tadeṣyāmo yatremāmasurā vibhajaṃteke tataḥ syāma yadasyaina bhajemahīti te yajñameva viṣṇuṃ puraskṛtyeyuḥ ‖ te hocuḥ | anu no 'smāṃ pṛthivyāmābhajatāsteva no 'pyasyāṃ bhāga iti te hāsurā asūyaṃta ivocuryāvadevaiṣa viṣṇurabhiśete tāvadyo vadda iti ‖ vāmano ha viṣṇurāsa | taddevā na jihīḍire mahadvai nodurai no yajñasaṃmitamaduriti | te prāṃcaṃ viṣṇuṃ nipādya | chaṃdobhirabhitaḥ paragrahan gāyatreṇa tā chaṃdasā parigṛhṇāmīti dakṣiṇatasraiṣṭubhena tvā chaṃdasā parigṛhṇāmīti paścājjāgatena tvā cchaṃdasā parigṛhṇāmītyuttarataḥ ‖ taṃ chaṃdobhirabhitaḥ parigṛhya ‖ .... .... .... .... saumyasyādhvarasya vediṃ cakre ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 1-2-3-1 to 9)

### Printed p. 597
The gods and Asuras, sons of Prajāpati, once fought with each other for supremacy; the Asuras became powerful and thought the whole earth belonged to them. Then they tried to measure the earth with a bull's hide and share it among themselves. The gods then placed Viṣṇu, the sacrifice in person, at their head, went to the Asuras, and asked that they too should have some share of the earth along with them. The Asuras, agreeing with half a mind, declared that they would leave to the gods only as much space as Viṣṇu, their leader, could occupy, and that certainly nothing more than that could be given. Viṣṇu was a dwarf. [The Asuras thought he would occupy only a little space.] Yet the gods, not dejected by this, said that as much space as Viṣṇu the sacrifice would occupy was enough for them. Then they placed him facing east and made an enclosure around him: on the south with the Gāyatrī metre, on the west with the Triṣṭubh metre, and on the north with the Jagatī metre. Thereupon the whole earth, as though fashioned into an altar, was pervaded by Viṣṇu, the sacrifice, alone. It became as though the whole earth had been easily provided for the gods; this has become the basis for the later Purāṇic story of the Vāmana incarnation, and for the part of the story in which, at the time of the fight between gods and Asuras, Vāmana deceived Bali and helped the gods. The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa indicates this same situation in the passage
तेऽग्निना प्रांच्योऽजयन् । वसुभिर्दक्षिणा । रुद्रैः प्रत्यंचः । आदित्यैरुदंचः । यस्यैवं विमषो वेदिं परिगृह्णंति ॥ (*te 'gninā prāṃcyo 'jayan | vasubhirdakṣiṇā | rudraiḥ pratyaṃcaḥ | ādityairudaṃcaḥ | yasyaivaṃ vimaṣo vediṃ parigṛhṇaṃti ‖*)
(Tai. Brā. 3-9-9-7; reference printed त्रै (*trai*), जाति (*jāti*).)**NOTE**
and the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa has the same matter:
न हि तयोः कतरश्चन पराजिग्ये । इंद्रश्च विष्णो यदपस्पृधेथां त्रेधा सहस्रं वि तद्वैरयेथामिति । इंद्रश्च ह वै विष्णुश्चासुरैर्युयुधाते तान्ह स्म जित्तोचतुः कल्पामहा इति ते ह तथेत्यसुरा ऊचुः सोऽब्रवीदिंद्रो यावदेवायं विष्णुस्त्रिविक्रमते तावदस्माकमथ युष्माकमितिरदिति स इमान् लोकान्विचक्रमेऽथो वेदानथो वाचं तदाहुः किं तत्सहस्रमितीमे लोका इमे वेदा अथो वागिति ब्रूयात् ॥ (*na hi tayoḥ kataraścana parājigye | iṃdraśca viṣṇo yadapaspṛdhethāṃ tredhā sahasraṃ vi tadvairayethāmiti | iṃdraśca ha vai viṣṇuścāsurairyuyudhāte tānha sma jittocatuḥ kalpāmahā iti te ha tathetyasurā ūcuḥ so 'bravīdiṃdro yāvadevāyaṃ viṣṇustrivikramate tāvadasmākamatha yuṣmākamitiraditi sa imān lokānvicakrame 'tho vedānatho vācaṃ tadāhuḥ kiṃ tatsahasramitīme lokā ime vedā atho vāgiti brūyāt ‖*)

### Printed p. 598
Neither Indra nor Viṣṇu ever suffered defeat. In the past, when they had fought the Asuras and defeated them, and a proposal came that the earth be divided, it was agreed that the regions covered by Viṣṇu's three feet should go to the gods and the whole remaining region to the Asuras; then Indra became the lord of the three worlds covered by Viṣṇu's three feet. Having driven out the Asuras, he (together with the gods) himself occupied the three worlds: this is the story described here.
But since it is difficult to know the precise meaning of the word वामन (*vāmana*), there are differences of opinion among modern scholars on this matter. Collecting the opinions of the various scholars on this subject, the scholar R. N. Dandekar has stated as follows.
What the primary notion underlying Vishnu's dwarf-form was, it is not easy to imagine. A. Khun thought that the dwarf represented the sun-light which shrinks inot dwarf size in the evening. Oldenberg Proposed that the idea evolved out of a fable about a wide-stepping giant who could turn himself into a dwarf. This is evidently far-fetched, since a fable-motive cannot be the centre of a myth. According to Keith, Macdonell, Hillebrandt Vishnu assumed the dwarf form only by way of a stratagem in order to mislead the Asura's An ethical interpretation of this अवतार (*avatāra*) is given by Macnicol who believes that it is suggestive of strength and safety issuing out of smallness and weakness. N. Iyyengar thinks that Vishnu seen as a little dwarf in the form of the sacrificial fire on earth takes the giant strides in the forms of Vidyut and Surya. R. Shania Shastry refers to the 'dwarfish shadow' while explaining the Avataras on the basis of astronomical phenomena.
( A Volume of Studies in Indology. Presented to Prof. P. V. Kane. P. 105 ).
Of all these, the opinion of Iyyengar (printed ऎर् (*èr*). अय्यंगार् (*ayyaṃgār*)) agrees with what is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. As this scholar says, the idea that the sacrificial fire, which was in a subtle form, grew gradually, covered the whole earth, and then, in the form of lightning and of the sun, covered the other two worlds, corresponds to the above description of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, that Viṣṇu, the sacrifice, in the form of the altar covered the earth, and in the form of fire the entire world.

## Sūkta 155 (Maṇḍala 1)

> प्र वः पांतमिति षडृचं षोडशं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं जागतं । पूर्वत्र
> वैष्णवं हीत्युक्तत्वाद्वैष्णवं । आद्यस्तृच इंद्रदेवताकश्च । प्र वो जागतं त्वैंद्रश्चाद्यस्तृच इत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ अभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु स्तोमातिशंसन उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta प्र वः पांतं (*pra vaḥ pāṃtaṃ*) has six Ṛks and is the sixteenth sūkta; it is of Dairghatamasa (Dīrghatamas) origin, in the Jagatī metre. Because it was said earlier that it is Vaiṣṇava, its deity is Viṣṇu; the first three Ṛks also have Indra as deity. The Anukramaṇikā says: प्र वो जागतं त्रैंद्रश्चाद्यस्तृचः (*pra vo jāgataṃ traiṃdraścādyastṛcaḥ*). The use (viniyoga) is stated: in the Abhiplava (ṣaḍaha) and Ukthya rites, for the स्तोमातिशंसन (*stomātiśaṃsana*).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta प्र वः पांतं (*pra vaḥ pāṃtaṃ*) is the sixteenth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Dīrghatamā Aucathya (दीर्घतमा औचथ्यः (*dīrghatamā aucathyaḥ*)); the metre is Jagatī. As said before, Viṣṇu is the deity of this sūkta; the first three Ṛks are also Indra-deitied. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: प्र वो जागतं त्रैंद्रश्चाद्यस्तृचः (*pra vo jāgataṃ traiṃdraścādyastṛcaḥ*). It is stated that the sūkta has its use for स्तोमातिशंसन (*stomātiśaṃsana*) in the special sacrifices called Abhiplavaṣaḍaha and Ukthya.**NOTE**

> या । सानुनि । पर्वतानां । अदाभ्या । महः । तस्थतुः । अर्वताइव । साधुना ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वय्यादयः वो युष्माकं संबंधि पांतं पालनस्वभावं पातव्यं
> छांदसोऽंधः सोमरूपमन्नं प्रार्चत । प्रकर्षेण संपादयत । कस्मै । धियायते स्तुतीरिच्छते महे महते शूराय विक्रांतायेंद्राय विष्णवे व्यापकाय्कॆतन्नामकाय देवाय च । कस्तयोरतिशय इति उच्यते । या याविंद्राविष्णू
> पर्वतानां प्रीणनवतां पूरणवतां वा पर्वतशब्दो यास्केनैवं निरुक्तः । पर्ववान्
> पर्वतः पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातेर्वेति । उक्तलक्षणानां लोकानां सानुनि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the adhvaryu and the other priests. Offer, he says, your protective food, the soma, which is to be protected (the word अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*) is Vedic usage for अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)): "present it forth", that is, prepare it with care. For whom? For the great, valiant Indra, who desires praise (धियायते (*dhiyāyate*) means "desires praises"), and for the pervasive deity named Viṣṇu. He then says that the question is which of the two excels, and answers by describing the pair, Indra and Viṣṇu, "who ... of mountains". The word parvata is explained by Yāska (Nirukta) thus: पर्ववान् पर्वतः । पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातेर्वेति (*parvavān parvataḥ | parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇāterveti*). So "of mountains" means of the worlds that have the stated character, that is, that fill or gratify. (The sentence continues on the next page.)

### Printed p. 601

> समुच्चि तप्रदेशे । सर्वलोक इत्यर्थः । अथवा मेघानां समुच्चि तप्रदेशे ।
> पर्वतशब्दो मेघनामसूक्तत्वात् । तत्र तस्थतुः । तिष्ठतः । कीदृशौ ता । अदाभ्यादंभनीयौ परैरनभिभाव्यौ अत एव महो महांतौ । यद्वा । महो महसि
> स्वतेजसि सानुनीत्यनेन संबंधः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । साधुनाभिमतदेशप्रापणसमर्थेनार्वता वेगवताश्वेनेव । तेन यथात्युच्चि तं प्रदेशमारोहति तद्वदुच्चं पदमारूढौ । तस्मात्ताभ्यामर्चत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They stand at the high place of those worlds, that is, in all the worlds. Or else it is the high place of the clouds, since parvata is a name of the cloud. They stand there. Of what sort are they? They are अदाभ्या (*adābhyā*), not to be harmed, not to be overcome by others, and therefore महः (*mahaḥ*), great. Or else महः (*mahaḥ*) is the locative "in their own splendour", construed with सानुनि (*sānuni*). The simile: like a good horse, one that is fast and able to carry its rider to the desired place; as a man by it climbs to a high place, so these two have climbed to a high station. Therefore worship the two.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यादिगळे (*adhvaryādigaḷe*)—O adhvaryus and the rest
- अदाभ्या (*adābhyā*)—those who are unobstructed
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—the great ones
- या (*yā*)—the two, Indra and Viṣṇu, who
- पर्वतानां (*parvatānāṃ*)—of mountains
- सानुनि (*sānuni*)—on the peaks. [Or पर्वतानां (*parvatānāṃ*)—of the clouds that are like mountains; सानुनि (*sānuni*)—(able to go to the places desired), (well-trained)] **NOTE**
- अर्वता इव (*arvatā iva*)—as if riding horses and climbing to high places
- तस्थतुः (*tasthatuḥ*)—stand (in splendour)
- धियायते (*dhiyāyate*)—to him who desires praise
- महे (*mahe*)—who is powerful
- शूराय (*śūrāya*)—and valiant, to Indra
- च (*ca*)—and
- विष्णवे (*viṣṇave*)—to Viṣṇu also
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*)—nourishing, or to be nourished
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—the food in the form of soma
- प्रार्चत (*prārcata*)—offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O adhvaryus and the rest, Indra and Viṣṇu, who are unobstructed and great, stand in splendour on the lofty regions of the clouds that are like peaks, as if climbing high places on well-trained horses. To Indra, who desires praise and is powerful and valiant, and to Viṣṇu also, offer your nourishing food in the form of soma.

##### Printed English

Offer your nutritious viands to the great hero, (Indra), who is pleased by praise, and to Vishnu, the two invincible deities who ride upon the radiant summit of the clouds, as upon a well-trained steed-

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अदाभ्या (*adābhyā*)—अदंभनीयौ परैरनभिभाव्यौ (*adaṃbhanīyau parairanabhibhāvyau*): those who are not harmed by enemies, and the unobstructed. The word is formed from the root दभ् (*dabh*), which means "to injure, destroy", in its negative sense, as अदाभ्या (*adābhyā*), and is an epithet of Indra and Viṣṇu.

### Printed p. 602
पर्वतानां (*parvatānāṃ*)—पर्ववान् पर्वतः । पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा (*parvavān parvataḥ | parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātīrvā*). The word parva is formed either from the root पृ (*pṛ*), meaning "to fill", or from the root प्री (*prī*), meaning "to gratify"; that which has such joints (parva) is a parvata, a mountain.
सानुनि (*sānuni*)—सानु समुच्च्रतं भवति । समन्नुन्नमिति ना (*sānu samuccrataṃ bhavati | samannunnamiti nā*). (It is "driven upward", set in motion upward): it rises upward, or spreads out loftily. Hence the name sānu.
Here Sāyaṇa has explained पर्वतानां सानुनि (*parvatānāṃ sānuni*) in two ways. First, taking the word parvata as meaning पूरणवतां प्रीणनवता ० वा लोकानां समुच्चि तप्रदेशे (*pūraṇavatāṃ prīṇanavatā 0 vā lokānāṃ samucci tapradeśe*), he takes it to mean "in Satyaloka, the lofty region of the worlds that fill or that give delight". Second, taking it as अथवा मेघानां समुच्चि तप्रदेशे । पर्वतशब्दः मेघनामसु उक्तत्वात् । (*athavā meghānāṃ samucci tapradeśe | parvataśabdaḥ meghanāmasu uktatvāt |*), he takes it to mean "in the upper region where the clouds are", because the word parvata is read among the names of the cloud.
In general the word parvata is used abundantly in the Indra sūktas and the Marut sūktas. In many places this word has been explained as "cloud". Even when it is explained as cloud, one follows Yāska's derivation. If the word is formed from the root पृ (*pṛ*), it means that which fills the empty regions of the atmosphere; if from the root प्री (*prī*), it means that which gives gratification to the whole world by releasing rain.
In some contexts the sense may be not literally the cloud but a dense mass of darkness that is in cloud form and has solidified. For example:
समु त्ये महतीरपः सं क्षोणी समु सूर्यं (*samu tye mahatīrapaḥ saṃ kṣoṇī samu sūryaṃ*) । सं वज्रं पर्वशो दधुः (*saṃ vajraṃ parvaśo dadhuḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-22)
वि वृत्रं पर्वशो ययुर्वि पर्वता आराजिनः (*vi vṛtraṃ parvaśo yayurvi parvatā ārājinaḥ*) । चक्राणा वृष्टि पौंस्यं (*cakrāṇā vṛṣṭi pauṃsyaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-23)
If one examines the words vajra and parvata used in these Ṛks, the sūkta containing them is addressed to the Maruts. Since the thunderbolt is used here, and since the thunderbolt is commonly regarded as Indra's weapon, if vajra is taken here as a weapon in the form of a mass of radiance and parvata as a solidified mass of darkness, the sense "he split the mountain by wielding the thunderbolt" fits. So parvata here is a metaphor; it may mean a mass of darkness in the shape of a mountain.

### Printed p. 603
In many contexts the parvata is invoked and praised together with deities such as Indra. For example:
इंद्रापर्वता बृहता रथेन वामीरिष आ वहतं सुवीराः । (*iṃdrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena vāmīriṣa ā vahataṃ suvīrāḥ |*) ।
वीतं हव्यान्यध्वरेषु देवा वर्धेथां गीर्भिरिळया मदंता ॥ ( (*vītaṃ havyānyadhvareṣu devā vardhethāṃ gīrbhiriḷayā madaṃtā ‖ (*) ॥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-1)
In this Ṛk, with इंद्रश्च पर्वतश्च हे इंद्रापर्वत् (*iṃdraśca parvataśca he iṃdrāparvat*), the parvata is invoked along with Indra.
सजोषस आदित्यैर्मादयध्वं सजोषस ऋभवः पर्वतेभिः । (*sajoṣasa ādityairmādayadhvaṃ sajoṣasa ṛbhavaḥ parvatebhiḥ |*) ।
सजोषसो दैव्येना सवित्रा सजोषसः सिंधुभी रत्नधेभिः ॥ (*sajoṣaso daivyenā savitrā sajoṣasaḥ siṃdhubhī ratnadhebhiḥ ‖*) ॥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-34-8)
Here, with पर्ववद्भिः पर्वण्यर्चमानैर्देवविशेषैः (*parvavadbhiḥ parvaṇyarcamānairdevaviśeṣaiḥ*), the invocation is also together with deities such as the Ādityas. In such contexts it is not easy to say what the precise meaning of the word parvata is.
In the present Ṛk, explaining the word parvata as "cloud" seems appropriate. This sense fits because nearly all Indra's activities take place in the region of the cloud, and because the great deeds of Indra and Viṣṇu are praised here.
अर्वता इव (*arvatā iva*)—वेगवता अश्वेन इव (*vegavatā aśvena iva*): it is compared to a horse that moves with extreme speed. The formation of the word arvan and its particular sense have already been explained in detail earlier.
साधुना (*sādhunā*)—अभिमतदेशप्रापणसमर्थेन (*abhimatadeśaprāpaṇasamarthena*): with the capacity to reach the place they desire; thus the word sādhu is explained as capacity. When the Nirukta explains the Ṛk
तुविक्षं ते सुकृतं सूमयं धनुः साधुर्बुंदो हिरण्ययः । (*tuvikṣaṃ te sukṛtaṃ sūmayaṃ dhanuḥ sādhurbuṃdo hiraṇyayaḥ |*) ।
उभा ते बाहू रण्या सुसंस्कृत ऋदूपे चिदृदूवृधा ॥ (*ubhā te bāhū raṇyā susaṃskṛta ṛdūpe cidṛdūvṛdhā ‖*) ॥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-77-11)
it takes साधुः साधयिता (*sādhuḥ sādhayitā*) to mean "able to carry out the work" (an epithet of the bow). Likewise here the sense is "a horse that has the capacity".

##### Grammar

- पांतम् — पा पाने इति वा पा रक्षणे इति वा धातोः । शतृ प्रत्ययः यद्वा औणादिकः झ प्रत्ययः । झोंतः (पा. सू. ७-१-३) इति अंतादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।

### Printed p. 604
- अंधसः — अद भक्षणे धातुः । अदेर्नुम्‌धौच (उ. सू. ४-६४५) इति अन्नरूपार्थे असुन् प्रत्ययः । धातोः नुमागमः । दकारस्य धकारादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- धियायते — धियं आत्मनः इच्छति धियायति । धियायति इति धियायन् क्यजंतात् लडर्थे शतृप्रत्ययः । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपं । नुम् रहितस्य शतृणः परस्मिन् विभक्तेः आगतत्वात् शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३) इति तस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- महे — मह पूजायां धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१.१६८) इति चतुर्थ्याः उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- शूराय — शु गतौ धातुः । (सौत्रः) शुसिजिमीनां दीर्घश्च (उ सू. २-१८३) इति क्रन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । **NOTE**
- आर्चत — आर्च पूजायां धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
- पर्वतानाम् — पर्व पूरणे धातुः । भ्यमृदृशियजि— (उ. सू. ३-३९०) इति अतच् प्रत्ययः भवति । षष्ठीबहुवचनांतरूपं ।
- अदाभ्या — न दाभ्यौ अदाभ्यौ । दभि धातुः वार्तिकपठितः । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (पा, सू. ३-१-१२४) इति ण्यत् प्रत्ययः । णित्त्वात् अत उपधायाः (पा सू ७-२-११९) इति धातोः उपधायाः वृद्धिः । नञ् समासे तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ— (पा. सू. ६-२-२) इति नञ् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । द्विवचने (औ) परे सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति तस्य आकारादेशः ।
- तस्थतुः — ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ धातुः । लिट् प्रथमपुरुषद्विवचनांतरूपं । योग्यत्वात् तिजंतनिघातस्वरः न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । **NOTE**
- अर्वता इव — ऋ गतौ धातुः । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंते (पा. सू. ३-२-१५) इति वनिष् प्रत्ययः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोः गुणः । र परो भवति । तृतीयैकवचने परे अर्वणस्तृसावनञ्ञः इति तृ अंतादेशः भवति ।
- साधुना — साध संसिद्धौ धातुः । कृवापाजि— (उ.सू. १-१) इति उण् प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । तृतीयैकवचनांतरूपं ।

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उरुष्यति ।  
> या । मर्त्याय । प्रतिधीयमानं । इत् । कृशानोः । अस्तुः । असनां ।  
> उरुष्यथः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोमातिरेके तृतीयसवन एषा वैकल्पिकी याज्या । तथा च सूत्रितं । त्वेषमित्था समरणं शिमावतोरिति वा याज्या । आ. ६-७ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्राविष्णू शिमावतोरिष्टप्रदानादिकर्मवर्तोर्वां युवयोरित्थेत्थं
> त्वेषं प्रदीप्तं समरणं सम्यग्यागदेशगमनं सुतपा हुतशिष्टसोमपीतयजमान
> उरुष्यति । रक्षति । यागेन पूजयति । यद्वा । शिमावतोः प्रहरणादिकर्मवर्तोर्वां
> युवयोश्चषं दीप्तं शौर्यपेतं समरणं सम्यक्परस्परगमनोपेतं वृष्टिप्रदानाय मेघविदारणरूपं यजमान उरुष्यति । रक्षति । स्तौतीत्यर्थः । कस्तयोरतिशय इति उच्यते । या याविंद्राविष्णू मर्त्याय मनुष्याय हनिर्दात्रे यजमानाय प्रतिधीयमानमित् प्रतिधातव्यं फलरूपमसनामसनं चलनशीलं प्रदानशीलमन्नादिकमस्तु रभिमतक्षेप्तुर्निरसितुर्वा शक्राणां कृशानोरग्नेः सकाशादुरुष्यथः । अविच्छेदेन प्रवर्तयथः । वहौ हुतं हविः स्वीकृत्य तन्मुखादेव फलमपि
> दास्यथ इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viniyoga: when there is an excess of soma at the third pressing, this is an optional yājyā. So it is laid down in the sūtra: त्वेषमित्था समरणं शिमावतोरिति वा याज्या । (*tveṣamitthā samaraṇaṃ śimāvatoriti vā yājyā |*) (Ā. 6-7).
Sāyaṇa explains: O Indra and Viṣṇu, you are शिमावतोः (*śimāvatoḥ*), engaged in actions such as bestowing the desired. Your त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*), blazing, समरणं (*samaraṇaṃ*), going properly to the place of the sacrifice, is thus; the sacrificer, सुतपा (*sutapā*), who has drunk the soma left over from the offering, उरुष्यति (*uruṣyati*), protects, or honours with sacrifice. Or else: you are engaged in actions such as striking; your त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*), blazing, heroic समरणं (*samaraṇaṃ*), which is attended by a proper mutual meeting and takes the form of splitting the cloud for the bestowal of rain, the sacrificer उरुष्यति (*uruṣyati*), protects, that is, praises. Which of the two excels? To this he replies: you two, Indra and Viṣṇu, who for the mortal, the human sacrificer who gives the oblation, प्रतिधीयमानमित् (*pratidhīyamānamit*), what is to be set in return, that is, the fruit, असनां (*asanāṃ*), the moving, giving food and the like, you two उरुष्यथः (*uruṣyathaḥ*), keep it flowing without interruption, from कृशानोः (*kṛśānoḥ*), Agni, the opponent of the one who shoots or hurls the desired (the one who casts away enemies). That is, accepting the oblation offered into the fire, you will give the fruit also from that very mouth.

### Printed p. 606

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu
- या (*yā*)—you who
- मर्त्याय (*martyāya*)—to the mortal sacrificer
- प्रतिधीयमानमित् (*pratidhīyamānamit*)—that which must needs be received (in the form of the fruit of the sacrifice)
- असनां (*asanāṃ*)—food and the like
- अस्तुः (*astuḥ*)—of the one who distributes (the desired things) or drives away enemies
- कृशानोः (*kṛśānoḥ*)—through Agni
- उरुषथः (*uruṣathaḥ*)—you provide (continually); such
- शिमीवतोः (*śimīvatoḥ*)—of those who have the works of granting desired things and the like, or the works of striking and the like
- वां (*vāṃ*)—of you two
- त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—the radiant, or the one accompanied by valour
- समरणं (*samaraṇaṃ*)—the coming together
- सुतपाः (*sutapāḥ*)—the sacrificer who has drunk the Soma juice (the remainder of the offering)
- इत्या (*ityā*)—in this manner
- उरुष्यति (*uruṣyati*)—worships

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you always provide, to the mortal sacrificer, through Agni who distributes the desired things, the food and the like that must be received in the form of the fruit of the sacrifice. Thus the sacrificer who has drunk the Soma juice that remained after the oblation worships (honours) the radiant and united coming of you two, who have the works of granting desired things and the like.

##### Printed English

Indra and Vishnu, the devout worshipper glorifies the radiant approach of you two, who are the granters of desires, and who bestow upon the mortal who worships you an immediately-receivable (reward), through the distribution of that fire which is the scatterer (of desired blessings).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Third Pressing (tṛtīyasavana), when the homa called Somātireka is performed, this Ṛk may optionally be used as the yājyā mantra; this is set out in the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra त्वेषमित्था समरणं शिमीवतोरिति वा याज्या (*tveṣamitthā samaraṇaṃ śimīvatoriti vā yājyā*) (A. 6-7). **NOTE**

कृशानोः—अग्नेः (*kṛśānoḥ—agneḥ*): "through Agni"; the word kṛśānu has been explained as meaning Agni. In the Ṛksaṃhitā this word is used as a synonym of Agni in this one Ṛk only. Although the name is used in four more places in the Ṛksaṃhitā, there is no reason there to take it as Agni; everywhere it is the name of a person called Kṛśānu. In the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, except for one passage (5-32), in no other Śruti text does the word kṛśānu appear to be used as a synonym of Agni. And that name is very well known in the Saṃhitās and also in the Brāhmaṇas and the like.

### Printed p. 607
Kṛśānu, the foremost among archers, is famed as a guardian of Soma. The story of how he pursued the falcon that was carrying off the Soma and cut its feather is told in the Ṛksaṃhitā thus:

अव यच्छेनो अस्वनीवध द्योर्वि यद्यदि वात ऊहुः पुरंधिं । सृजद्यदस्मा अव ह क्षिपज्जां कृशानुरस्ता मनसा भुरण्यन् ॥ (*ava yaccheno asvanīvadha dyorvi yadyadi vāta ūhuḥ puraṃdhiṃ | sṛjadyadasmā ava ha kṣipajjāṃ kṛśānurastā manasā bhuraṇyan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-27-3)

The story is indicated that when all the Soma-guardians resisted the falcon that came from the heavenly world to carry off the Soma, Kṛśānu approached it with the speed of thought, shot his arrow at it and cut its feather. Likewise,

स पूर्व्यः पवते यं दिवस्परि श्येनो मथायदिषितस्तिरो रजः । स मध्य आ युवते वेविजान इत्यृशानोरस्तुर्मनसाह बिभ्युषा ॥ (*sa pūrvyaḥ pavate yaṃ divaspari śyeno mathāyadiṣitastiro rajaḥ | sa madhya ā yuvate vevijāna ityṛśānorasturmanasāha bibhyuṣā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-77-2)

in this Ṛk too the same situation is indicated. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa this story is somewhat more elaborate and shows Kṛśānu's extraordinary power.

ते देवा अब्रुवन्गायत्रीं त्वं न इमं सोमं राजानमाहरेति सा तथ्येत्यब्रवीत्तां वै मा सर्वेण स्वस्त्ययनेनानुमंत्रयध्वमिति तथेति सोदपतत्तां देवाः सर्वेण स्वस्त्ययनेनान्वमंत्रयंत प्रेति चेति चेत्येतद्वै सर्वं स्वस्त्ययनं यत्प्रेति चेति तद्योऽस्य प्रियः स्यात्तमेतेनानु मंत्रयेत प्रेति चेति चेति स्वस्त्यैव गच्छति स्वस्त्यॆ पुनरागच्छति । सा पतित्वा सोमपालान्फीषयित्वा पद्भ्यां च मुखेन च सोमं राजानं समगृभ्णाद्यानि चेतरे छंदसी अक्षराण्यजहितां तानि चोपसमगृभ्णात् । तस्या आनु विसृज्य कृशानुः सोमपालः सव्यस्य पदो नखमच्छिदत्तच्छल्यकोऽभवत्तस्मात्सनखमिव यद्वशमस्रवत्सा वशाभवत् । (*te devā abruvangāyatrīṃ tvaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānamāhareti sā tathyetyabravīttāṃ vai mā sarveṇa svastyayanenānumaṃtrayadhvamiti tatheti sodapatattāṃ devāḥ sarveṇa svastyayanenānvamaṃtrayaṃta preti ceti cetyetadvai sarvaṃ svastyayanaṃ yatpreti ceti tadyo 'sya priyaḥ syāttametenānu maṃtrayeta preti ceti ceti svastyaiva gacchati svastyè punarāgacchati | sā patitvā somapālānphīṣayitvā padbhyāṃ ca mukhena ca somaṃ rājānaṃ samagṛbhṇādyāni cetare chaṃdasī akṣarāṇyajahitāṃ tāni copasamagṛbhṇāt | tasyā ānu visṛjya kṛśānuḥ somapālaḥ savyasya pado nakhamacchidattacchalyako 'bhavattasmātsanakhamiva yadvaśamasravatsā vaśābhavat |*) (Ai. Brā. 3-26)

It is described that the gods told Gāyatrī to bring away King Soma, spoke a blessing of safe passage (svastyayana) over her and sent her off, wishing her to return quickly; Gāyatrī in the form of a falcon descended to the earth and frightened the Soma-guardians, whereupon Kṛśānu cut off its nail with his arrow.

That in all the other places the word kṛśānu is a personal name, and that only in the present Ṛk it is a synonym of Agni, is not so very unnatural, may be understood from the basis of other Śruti texts.

### Printed p. 608
One may note the sentence in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā that teaches the identity "Agni himself is Kṛśānu". In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

अथ सोमक्रयणाननुदिशति । स्नान भ्राजांघारे बंभारे हस्त सुहस्त कृशान वेते वः सोमक्रयणास्तान्नक्षध्वं मा वो दभन्निति धिष्ण्यानां वा एते भाजनेनैतानि वै धिष्ण्यानां नामानि तान्न्येवैभ्य एदन्वदिक्षत् । (*atha somakrayaṇānanudiśati | snāna bhrājāṃghāre baṃbhāre hasta suhasta kṛśāna vete vaḥ somakrayaṇāstānnakṣadhvaṃ mā vo dabhanniti dhiṣṇyānāṃ vā ete bhājanenaitāni vai dhiṣṇyānāṃ nāmāni tānnyevaibhya edanvadikṣat |*) (Pa. Bo. 3-2-6-1) **NOTE**

In this passage it is indicated that Snāna, Bhrāja, Aṅghāri, Baṃbhāri, Hasta, Suhasta and Kṛśānu are Soma-guardians. **NOTE**. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā also,

.... .... ज्योतिस्सोमविक्रयिणि तमोमित्रोन ऐहि सुमित्रधा इंद्रस्योरुमा विश दक्षिणमुशन्नुशंतग्स् सोन्यसस्योनग्स् स्नानभ्राजांघारे बंभारे हस्त सुहस्त कृशानवेते वस्सोमक्रयणास्तान्नक्षध्वं मा वो दभन् । (*.... .... jyotissomavikrayiṇi tamomitrona aihi sumitradhā iṃdrasyorumā viśa dakṣiṇamuśannuśaṃtags sonyasasyonags snānabhrājāṃghāre baṃbhāre hasta suhasta kṛśānavete vassomakrayaṇāstānnakṣadhvaṃ mā vo dabhan |*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-7) **NOTE**

In these sentences it is said that those named above, Sthāna (sic), Bhrāja, Aṅghāri, Baṃbhāri, Hasta, Suhasta and Kṛśānu, are the vigilant protectors of Soma, and afterwards,

विभूरसि प्रवाहणो वह्निरसि हव्यवाहनश्वात्रोऽसि प्रचेतास्तुथोऽसि विश्ववेदा उशिगसि कविरंघारिरसि बंभारिववस्युरसि दुवस्वाञ्चन्युरसि मार्जालीयस्सम्राडसि कृशानुः परिषद्योऽसि पवमानः प्रतक्वासि नभस्वानसंमृष्टोऽसि हव्यसूद ऋतधामासि सुवर्ज्योतिर्ब्रह्मज्योतिरसि सुवर्धामाजोऽस्येकपादहिरसि बुद्धियो रौद्रेणानीकेन पाहि माग्ने पिपृहि मा मा मा हिग्ंसीः ॥ (*vibhūrasi pravāhaṇo vahnirasi havyavāhanaśvātro 'si pracetāstutho 'si viśvavedā uśigasi kaviraṃghārirasi baṃbhārivavasyurasi duvasvāñcanyurasi mārjālīyassamrāḍasi kṛśānuḥ pariṣadyo 'si pavamānaḥ pratakvāsi nabhasvānasaṃmṛṣṭo 'si havyasūda ṛtadhāmāsi suvarjyotirbrahmajyotirasi suvardhāmājo 'syekapādahirasi buddhiyo raudreṇānīkena pāhi māgne pipṛhi mā mā mā higṃsīḥ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-3)

Here Agni is addressed and entreated: "Aṅghāri, Baṃbhāri, Kṛśānu and all the rest, you yourself are." Moreover, in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa passage quoted above it is stated that Kṛśānu and the other Soma-guardians are धिष्ण्यानां नामानि (*dhiṣṇyānāṃ nāmāni*), names of the Agni-hearths (agnivedi) (Śa. Brā. 3-3-3-1). Therefore it is understood, on the basis of some sentences, that Kṛśānu and Agni are identical. In the Ṛksaṃhitā too, one may notice that the very epithets connected with the word kṛśānu in the present Ṛk are used also in other Ṛks in which this name occurs. For example—

### Printed p. 609
त्रिः सप्त सस्रा नद्यो महीरपो वनस्पतीन् पर्वता अग्निमूतये । कृशानुमस्तान् तिष्यं सदस्य आ रुद्रं रुद्रेषु रुद्रियं हवामहे ॥ (*triḥ sapta sasrā nadyo mahīrapo vanaspatīn parvatā agnimūtaye | kṛśānumastān tiṣyaṃ sadasya ā rudraṃ rudreṣu rudriyaṃ havāmahe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-64-8)

In this Ṛk the words kṛśānu and agni stand as qualified and qualifier. And just as in the Ṛk 9-77-2 quoted above the usage is अस्तुः कृशानोः (*astuḥ kṛśānoḥ*), and in Ṛk 4-27-3 अस्ता कृशानुः (*astā kṛśānuḥ*), so also in the present Ṛk there are the qualifier and qualified अस्तुः कृशानोः (*astuḥ kṛśānoḥ*). As in the quoted Ṛks the word astu is meant to be "one who hurls an arrow and harms the enemy", so in the present Ṛk too अस्तुः (*astuḥ*), "निरसितुः शत्रूणां (*nirasituḥ śatrūṇāṃ*)", is understood as the destroyer of enemies.

असनां—आसनं चलनशीलं प्रदानशीलमन्नादिकं (*asanāṃ—āsanaṃ calanaśīlaṃ pradānaśīlamannādikaṃ*): Sāyaṇa explains that since food and the like have the nature of moving from the giver and going to the receiver, they are called asana. In the Ṛk

पुरूणि दस्मो नि रिणाति जंभैराद्रोचते वन आ विभावा । आदस्य वातो अनु वाति शोचिरस्तुर्न शर्यामसनामनु द्यून् ॥ (*purūṇi dasmo ni riṇāti jaṃbhairādrocate vana ā vibhāvā | ādasya vāto anu vāti śocirasturna śaryāmasanāmanu dyūn ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-148-4)

it is an epithet of the arrow that moves (**NOTE**).

उरुष्यति (*uruṣyati*)—उरुष्यती रक्षाकर्म (*uruṣyatī rakṣākarma*) (Ni. 5-23): the meaning is "protects". The author of the Nirukta, quoting the Ṛk

स नो बोधि श्रुधी हवमुरुष्माणो अघायतः समस्मात् (*sa no bodhi śrudhī havamuruṣmāṇo aghāyataḥ samasmāt*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-24-3)

shows the meaning "protect us (naḥ) from all who wish us harm". But in the present Ṛk this word occurs twice. Sāyaṇa explains the first, उरुष्यति—रक्षति । यागेन पूजयति (*uruṣyati—rakṣati | yāgena pūjayati*) or स्तौति (*stauti*), as "worships by sacrifice" or "praises"; and the second, उरुष्यथः प्रेरयथः (*uruṣyathaḥ prerayathaḥ*), as "protect us, providing us food without interruption".

शिमीवतः—शिमीति कर्मनाम । शमयतेर्वा शक्नोतेर्वा (*śimīvataḥ—śimīti karmanāma | śamayatervā śaknotervā*) (Ni. 5-12). The word is formed either from the root śam, giving the meaning "toil" or "exert oneself", or from the root śak, giving the meaning "be able", and means "work".

आपांतमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिः शिमीनाञ्छरुमा ऋजीषी । सोमो विश्वान्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि देभुः ॥ (*āpāṃtamanyustṛpalaprabharmā dhuniḥ śimīnāñcharumā ṛjīṣī | somo viśvānyatasā vanāni nārvāgiṃdraṃ pratimānāni debhuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-5)

### Printed p. 610
Just as in such Ṛks śamīvān has the meaning "endowed with work", the same meaning is to be given in the present Ṛk also: Indra and Viṣṇu are always engaged in works such as protecting the world.

##### Grammar

- त्वेषम्—त्विष दीप्तौ धातुः । नंदिग्रहिपचा—(पा. सू. ३-१-१३४) इति अच् प्रत्ययः । चित्त्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति । प्रत्ययनिमित्तं लघूपधगुणः ।
- समरणम्—ऋ गौ धातुः । ल्युट् प्रत्ययः । तन्निमित्तं धातोर्गुणः । रपरत्वं भवति । लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इति प्रत्ययस्य पूर्वमुदात्तस्वरः भवति । प्रादिसमासे कृमत्तपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- इंद्राविष्णू—इंद्रश्च विष्णुश्च इंद्राविष्णू । देवताद्वंद्वे च (पा.सू. ६-३-२६) इति पूर्वपदस्य अनज् । देवत्वादंद्वे च (पा. सू. ६-२-१४१) इति उभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । **NOTE**
- सुतपाः—षुञ् अभिषवे धातुः । क्त प्रत्ययः । सुतं पिबति इति सुतपाः । पा पासे धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- उरुष्यति—उरुष्य धातुः रक्षणार्थे प्रयुक्तः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।
- प्रतिधीयमानम्—डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । कर्मणि लटः शानचादेशः । सार्वधातुके यक् (पा. सू. ३-१-६७) इति यक् । घुमास्थागापाज—(पा. सू. ६-४-६६) इति धातोरीत्वम् । आनेमुक् (पा. सू. ७-२-८२) इति मुकागमः । तास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू ६-१-१८६) इति लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् यक्स्वरः अवशिष्यते । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
- कृशानोः—कृश तनूकरणे धातुः । ऋन्यञ्चिवन्य—(उ. सू. ४.४४२) इति आनुक् प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
- अस्तुः—असु क्षेपणे धातुः । कर्तरि तृन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । पंचमीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
- असनाम्—पूर्वोक्तधातोः युच् प्रत्ययः । युवोरनाक् ( पा. सू. ७-१-१ ) इति अनादेशः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
