> अस्यायमर्थः । अग्नौ हुताः सोमाहुतय आदित्यमंडलं प्राप्य द्वादशात्मनः
> सवितुर्मूर्त्यंतराविंद्राविष्णू पोषयंति । तुष्टौ तौ मेघद्वारा वर्षतः । तया

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those well-known Soma-form oblations offered by the sacrificer increase (वर्धंति (*vardhaṃti*) = वर्धयंति (*vardhayaṃti*)) this Indra's great पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*), that is, the manly deed, strength of the kind to be described. Or else ईं (*īṃ*) is without meaning. That Indra brings (नि नयति (*ni nayati*), "brings fully") the capacity born of Soma-drinking to Heaven and Earth (मातरा (*mātarā*)). For what purpose? रेतसे (*retase*): for the capacity of living beings to beget sons and the like; भुजे (*bhuje*): for their enjoyment or their protection. Where? It is said: अधि (*adhi*) (above) the shining (रोचने (*rocane*)) orb of the radiant (दिवः (*divaḥ*)) sun. नाम (*nāma*) is नमनं (*namanaṃ*), the capacity established in Heaven and Earth; the पुत्रः (*putraḥ*) is the protector of many (पुरुत्राता (*purutrātā*)), every person, by the grace of the father, the protector Viṣṇu. Or else: because of being the begetter of himself, the father holds (दधाति (*dadhāti*) = धारयति (*dhārayati*)) the lower name, called "grandson", which has itself arisen; the higher name "son"; and, in relation to both, the third name "father". For the Śruti says त्रीणि नाव रेतसिंसि पिता पुत्रः पौत्रः (*trīṇi nāva retasiṃsi pitā putraḥ pautraḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-8-4). The meaning of this is: the Soma oblations offered in the fire reach the orb of the sun and nourish Indra and Viṣṇu, the other forms of Savitṛ who has twelve forms; pleased, the two rain through the clouds. (The block breaks off here, at तया (*tayā*).)

### Printed p. 612

> वृष्टा सस्यादिद्वारा प्रजाः पुत्रपौत्रादिरूपेण वर्धयत इत्येवंमहानुभावामिंद्राविष्णू इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes his explanation of the passage with the words: through the rain that falls, by way of plants and the like, the two increase the creatures in the form of sons, grandsons and so on. Thus great in power are Indra and Viṣṇu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ताः (*tāḥ*)—the oblations in the form of Soma
- अस्य (*asya*)—Indra's
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)—manly power (the Kannada adds the particle ईं (*īṃ*))
- वर्धंति (*vardhaṃti*)—cause to increase. (The same Indra)
- रेतसे (*retase*)—for the sake of giving (living beings) the capacity of begetting offspring
- भुजे (*bhuje*)—for the enjoyment of pleasures, or for protection
- मातरा (*mātarā*)—to heaven and earth
- नि नयति (*ni nayati*)—he makes (this power) go and join
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the shining Āditya
- अधि रोचने (*adhi rocane*)—in the orb that shines exceedingly
- नाम (*nāma*)—this generative power, established
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—every man, in the form of a son
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—by the favour of Viṣṇu the protector (or from himself, the begetter)
- अवरं (*avaraṃ*)—as bearing the inferior designation of grandson
- परं (*paraṃ*)—as bearing the designation of son, superior to that
- तृतीयं (*tṛtīyaṃ*)—as bearing the name of father, distinct from these two
- दधाति (*dadhāti*)—obtains

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The oblations in the form of Soma, offered by the sacrificer, make Indra's great manly power increase. The same Indra, for the sake of giving living beings the capacity of begetting offspring and for the enjoyment of pleasures, makes this power go and join heaven and earth. This power, established in the orb of the exceedingly bright Āditya, is obtained by every man, by the favour of Viṣṇu, as bearing the designation of grandson, the designation of son, and the name of father.

##### Printed English

These (oblations) augment his, (Indra,s), mighty manhood, by which he fits the parents (of all creatures, heaven and earth), for generation and enjoyment; where-by, in the upper region of the sky. the son has an inferior and superior appellation, and a third (name) of father.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is described how Indra's manly power increases through partaking of the Soma oblation; how the same Indra, directing his power to heaven and earth, becomes the cause of the enjoyment and growth of all beings; and how Indra, as the cause of growth in the form of sons, grandsons and so on, provides the world with Viṣṇu's favour. First,

### Printed p. 613

ताः अस्य महि पौंस्यं वर्धंति (*tāḥ asya mahi pauṃsyaṃ vardhaṃti*)—the well-known oblations in the form of Soma, pressed by the sacrificer, increase the form, that is, the strength, of Indra, which will be spoken of. The Soma oblations offered by the sacrificer make Indra's great strength increase. This manly power is not a benefit to Indra alone; it becomes a cause of the sacrificer's growth too.

This matter is described in detail in the Ṛk
वयो न वृक्षं सुपलाशमासदन्तोमास इंद्रं मुंदिनश्च मूषदः । प्रैषामनीकं शवसा दविद्युतद्विदत्स्वर्मरनवे ज्योतिरार्यं ॥ (*vayo na vṛkṣaṃ supalāśamāsadantomāsa iṃdraṃ muṃdinaśca mūṣadaḥ | praiṣāmanīkaṃ śavasā davidyutadvidatsvarmaranave jyotirāryaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-43-4).
Here the Soma oblations offered from the Camasa vessels are likened to birds and Indra to a tree. As birds, settling in a tree, give the tree a kind of brilliance and beauty, so the Soma oblations, established in Indra, increase Indra's strength by their power and make him full of brilliance. Having thus shown the power of the Soma oblation, the Ṛk prays that Indra's strength and brilliance, produced by it, may benefit the human sacrificer as well.

In Brāhmaṇa passages such as
वायोः पूतः पवित्रेण । प्रत्यज्‌सोमोऽतिद्रुत इति सोमातिपूतस्य पुनाति यथारूपमेवैनं पुनातींद्रस्य युज्यः सखेति यदेवास्य तेनेंद्रियं वीर्यमतिक्रांतं भवति तदस्मिन्पुनर्दधाति ॥ (*vāyoḥ pūtaḥ pavitreṇa | pratyajsomo 'tidruta iti somātipūtasya punāti yathārūpamevainaṃ punātīṃdrasya yujyaḥ sakheti yadevāsya teneṃdriyaṃ vīryamatikrāṃtaṃ bhavati tadasminpunardadhāti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 12-7-3-9)
too, the Soma, purified by Vāyu and others and offered in the form of an oblation, is a fitting friend of Indra and increases his heroic vigour. Therefore it gives vigour to the sacrificer also, and restores his vigour to one who has become powerless. Thus the greatness of the Soma oblation is described here as it is everywhere else.

पौंस्यं—पुंसः कर्म (*pauṃsyaṃ—puṃsaḥ karma*): the sense is the power of a man. This word is read among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9) and also among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). In the present Ṛk it has to be understood as strength. Even if it is understood as battle, the sense is that the Soma juice fills Indra's battle with fresh vigour and brings him victory. In the 15th sūkta of the 2nd Maṇḍala, describing the daring deeds accomplished by Indra, satisfied and strengthened by drinking Soma, the first Ṛk
प्र घा न्वस्य महतो महानि सत्या सत्यस्य करणानि वोचं । त्रिकद्रुकेष्टपिबत्सुतस्यास्य मदे अहिमिंद्रो जघान ॥ (*pra ghā nvasya mahato mahāni satyā satyasya karaṇāni vocaṃ | trikadrukeṣṭapibatsutasyāsya made ahimiṃdro jaghāna ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-1)

### Printed p. 614

declares that he will praise the great, truthful deeds of Indra, intoxicated by the Soma oblation offered at the rite-time called Trikadruka, such as the slaying of Ahi. In Ṛks such as
अवंशे द्यामस्तभायद्बृहंतमा रोदसी अप्पणदंतरिक्षं । स धारयत्पृथिवीं पप्रथच्च सोमस्य ता मद इंद्रश्चकार ॥ (*avaṃśe dyāmastabhāyadbṛhaṃtamā rodasī appaṇadaṃtarikṣaṃ | sa dhārayatpṛthivīṃ paprathacca somasya tā mada iṃdraścakāra ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-2)
it is described how Indra, intoxicated by drinking Soma, has the power to fill earth and the other worlds with his brilliance; and by passages such as भिनद्वलमंगिरोभिर्गृणानो (*bhinadvalamaṃgirobhirgṛṇāno*) (2-15-8) how he subdued Vala and other Asuras. All these great deeds are likewise praised as the effect of the Soma oblations offered on the Ābhiplavika days: सोमस्य ता मद इंद्रश्चकार (*somasya tā mada iṃdraścakāra*).

मातरा (*mātarā*) is a synonym for heaven and earth, the causes of the origin of the universe. Heaven and earth are in some places addressed as पितरा (*pitarā*) (1-159-2; 3-3-11; 7-53-2; 10-65-8), and sometimes as मातरा (*mātarā*) (9-85-12; 10-1-7; 10-35-3). In
य इमे व्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥ (*ya ime vyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā | tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 11-110-9)**NOTE**
they are addressed as जनित्री (*janitrī*). Elsewhere again there is an address to the world of heaven (the Kannada word is म्यलोक (*myaloka*)) as father and to the earth alone as mother (1-89-4; 1-90-7; 1-160-2, etc.). **NOTE**
In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa an episode concerning the wedlock of heaven and earth is told in story form:
इमौ वै लोकौ सहास्तां तौ व्यतां नावर्षन्न समतपत्ते पंचजना न समजानत तौ देवाः समनयंस्तौ संयंतावेतं देवविवाहं व्यवहेतां रथंतरेणैवेयममां जिन्वति बृहतासाविमां । .... .... .... असौ वै लोक इमं लोकमभिपर्यावर्तत । ततो वै द्यावापृथिवी अभवतां न द्यावांतरिक्षान्नांतरिक्षाद्दूमिः ॥ (*imau vai lokau sahāstāṃ tau vyatāṃ nāvarṣanna samatapatte paṃcajanā na samajānata tau devāḥ samanayaṃstau saṃyaṃtāvetaṃ devavivāhaṃ vyavahetāṃ rathaṃtareṇaiveyamamāṃ jinvati bṛhatāsāvimāṃ | .... .... .... asau vai loka imaṃ lokamabhiparyāvartata | tato vai dyāvāpṛthivī abhavatāṃ na dyāvāṃtarikṣānnāṃtarikṣāddūmiḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 4-27).
Heaven and earth, formerly joined together, for some time became separate. As soon as they separated, the light of the sun and the falling of rain stopped completely. The Pañcajanas (who they are was explained earlier) also could not foster mutual goodwill and a peaceful life. Then the gods approached heaven and earth and entreated them to become one

### Printed p. 615

again. Then the prescribed marriage was performed for the two. Ever since, heaven and earth have been in an unseparated relation. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka too,
जाया भूमिः पतिर्व्योम (*jāyā bhūmiḥ patirvyoma*) (Tai. Ā. 1-10-1)
the wedlock of heaven and earth is stated.
In Ṛks such as
प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी नमोभिः सबाध ईळे बृहती यजत्रे । ते चिद्भिः पूर्वे कवयो गृणंतः पुरो मही वधिरे देवपुत्रे ॥ (*pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī namobhiḥ sabādha īḷe bṛhatī yajatre | te cidbhiḥ pūrve kavayo gṛṇaṃtaḥ puro mahī vadhire devaputre ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-53-1)
the epithet देवपुत्रे (*devaputre*) shows that heaven and earth are the parents not only of men but also of the gods.

दिवः अधिरोचने (*divaḥ adhirocane*)—द्योतमानस्य आदित्यस्य रोचमाने मंडले (*dyotamānasya ādityasya rocamāne maṃḍale*): in the brilliant orb of the shining Āditya. परं अवरं तृतीयं दधाति (*paraṃ avaraṃ tṛtīyaṃ dadhāti*): the sacrificer obtains the names in the form of son, grandson and so on. Here the identity of Indra and Viṣṇu with Āditya is stated, and it is also said that the sacrificer's welfare comes by their favour. Sāyaṇa explains the relation of cause and effect between the wealth of sons and so on and the favour of Indra and Viṣṇu thus:
अग्नौ हुताः सोमाहुतयः आदित्यमंडलं प्राप्य द्वादशात्मनः सवितुर्मूर्त्यंतरौ इंद्राविष्णू पोषयंति । तुष्टौ तौ मेघद्वारा वर्षतः । तया वृष्ट्या सस्यादिद्वारा प्रजाः पुत्रपौत्रादिरूपेण वर्धयत इत्येवं महानुभावौ इंद्राविष्णू इति । (*agnau hutāḥ somāhutayaḥ ādityamaṃḍalaṃ prāpya dvādaśātmanaḥ saviturmūrtyaṃtarau iṃdrāviṣṇū poṣayaṃti | tuṣṭau tau meghadvārā varṣataḥ | tayā vṛṣṭyā sasyādidvārā prajāḥ putrapautrādirūpeṇa vardhayata ityevaṃ mahānubhāvau iṃdrāviṣṇū iti |*).
The Soma oblations offered in the fire reach the orb of Āditya and nourish Indra and Viṣṇu, who are other forms of Savitṛ. Satisfied by this, they send down rain through the cloud. By that rain plants and so on arise, which turn into food and become the cause of the growth of sons, grandsons and so on: such, Sāyaṇa says, is the purport of this sentence. This sentence states the close relation among sacrifice, Indra, Viṣṇu and Āditya, and shows how they are the cause of the increase of progeny in the world. There is also abundant support from Śruti passages for saying that this explanation is correct.

स उ एव मखः स विष्णुः । तत इंद्रो मखवानभवन्मखवान्ह वै तं मघवानित्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवाः॥ (*sa u eva makhaḥ sa viṣṇuḥ | tata iṃdro makhavānabhavanmakhavānha vai taṃ maghavānityācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devāḥ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-13).
In this sentence the identity of Makha (sacrifice) and Viṣṇu is stated, and it is shown that because Indra possesses Makha, the name Makhavān (Maghavān) is well known for him.

### Printed p. 616

अथ यास्तद्देवाः । जुष्टास्तनूः प्रियाणि धामानि सार्धग्ं समवददिरे तदिंद्रे संन्यदधतैष वा इंद्रो य एष तपति न ह वा एषोऽग्रे तताप यथा हैवेदमन्यत्कृष्णमेवं हैवास तेनैवैतद्वीर्येण तपति तस्माद्यदि बहवो दीक्षॆरन् गृहपतय एव व्रतमभ्युत्सिच्य प्रयच्छेयुः स हि तेषामिंद्रभाजनं भवति । (*atha yāstaddevāḥ | juṣṭāstanūḥ priyāṇi dhāmāni sārdhagṃ samavadadire tadiṃdre saṃnyadadhataiṣa vā iṃdro ya eṣa tapati na ha vā eṣo 'gre tatāpa yathā haivedamanyatkṛṣṇamevaṃ haivāsa tenaivaitadvīryeṇa tapati tasmādyadi bahavo dīkṣèran gṛhapataya eva vratamabhyutsicya prayaccheyuḥ sa hi teṣāmiṃdrabhājanaṃ bhavati |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-4-2-15).
In these sentences एष वा इंद्रो य एष तपति (*eṣa vā iṃdro ya eṣa tapati*) it is said that Āditya, shining in the atmosphere, is Indra; that the prescribed offering of oblations by the initiated is the cause of Āditya's radiance; and, to show that sacrifice too is a cause of men's prosperity, since without Āditya's light and power there is no room for the falling of rain and so on, it is also said that Indra, in the form of Āditya, becomes brilliant only through sacrifice.

In the present Ṛk, for the word पितुः (*pituḥ*) it is said पालकाद्विष्णोरनुग्रहात् (*pālakādviṣṇoranugrahāt*): the wealth of sons and so on comes by the favour of Viṣṇu the protector. That is, this point is indicated both because sacrifice and Viṣṇu are closely related, and because Indra and Viṣṇu have a natural and sacrificial relationship. This mutual relationship is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa thus:
अथैवमभिपद्य वाचयति । विष्णोः कर्माणि पश्यत यतो व्रतानि पस्पशे इंद्रस्य युज्यः सखेति वज्रं वा एष प्राहार्षीद्यो यूपमुदशिश्रियद्विष्णोर्विजितिं पश्यतेत्येवैतदाह .... .... .... इंद्रोवै यज्ञस्य देवता वैष्णवो यूपस्तग् सेंद्रं करोति तस्मादाहेंद्रस्य युज्यः सखेति ॥ (*athaivamabhipadya vācayati | viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyata yato vratāni paspaśe iṃdrasya yujyaḥ sakheti vajraṃ vā eṣa prāhārṣīdyo yūpamudaśiśriyadviṣṇorvijitiṃ paśyatetyevaitadāha .... .... .... iṃdrovai yajñasya devatā vaiṣṇavo yūpastag seṃdraṃ karoti tasmādāheṃdrasya yujyaḥ sakheti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-7-1-17).
Here it is said that Indra and Viṣṇu have a natural friendship, that the Vaiṣṇava share of the sacrifice is to be assigned to Indra also, and that therefore both are partakers of the fruit of the sacrifice.

अथ चषालमुदीक्षते । तद्विष्णोः परमं पदग्ं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः। दिवीव चक्षुराततं । (*atha caṣālamudīkṣate | tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padagṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ| divīva cakṣurātataṃ |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-7-1-18).
Here it is said that Viṣṇu's highest place is the orb of Āditya shining in the world of heaven.

Thus, because of this mutual relation among Indra, Viṣṇu, sacrifice and the orb of Āditya, the present Ṛk declares that the sacrificers' increase of progeny, sons, grandsons and so on, comes by the favour of Indra and Viṣṇu.

### Printed p. 617

रेतसे (*retase*)—पुत्राम्यत्पादनसामर्थाय (*putrāmyatpādanasāmarthāya*): it is explained as "for the capacity of begetting offspring". And Sāyaṇa, quoting the Saṃhitā passage
त्रीणि नाव रेतांसि पिता पुत्रः पौत्रः (*trīṇi nāva retāṃsi pitā putraḥ pautraḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-14)**NOTE**
says that the seed takes three kinds of forms: father, son and grandson. The present Ṛk expresses the same by the words तृतीयं (*tṛtīyaṃ*), परं (*paraṃ*) and अपरं (*aparaṃ*). **NOTE**
The word रेतस् (*retas*) has other meanings besides the male seed that begets offspring. The Nirukta author has included this word among the names of water, अर्णः, क्षोदः, क्षद्म (*arṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ, kṣadma*) and so on (Ni. 2-27). In Ṛks such as
दिपो न यस्य रेतसो दुघानाः संथासो यंति शवसापरीताः । तरद्वेषाः सासहिः पौंस्येभिर्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥ (*dipo na yasya retaso dughānāḥ saṃthāso yaṃti śavasāparītāḥ | taradveṣāḥ sāsahiḥ pauṃsyebhirmarutvānno bhavatviṃdra ūtī ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-3)
it means the waters of rain. And in
कथा महे पुष्टिंभराय पूष्टे कद्रुद्राय सुमखाय हनिर्दे । कद्विष्णव उरुगायाय रेतो ब्रवः कदग्ने शरवे बृहत्यै ॥ (*kathā mahe puṣṭiṃbharāya pūṣṭe kadrudrāya sumakhāya hanirde | kadviṣṇava urugāyāya reto bravaḥ kadagne śarave bṛhatyai ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-3-7)
Sāyaṇa explains the word रेतस् (*retas*) as पासव (*pāsava*), a cause of destruction. **NOTE**
The use of this word in the sense of the seed that begets offspring, and the account of the exceeding power of the seed, are given at length in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (5-6-8).

भुरण्यति (*bhuraṇyati*)—the commentator says the sense is गच्छति भजते च (*gacchati bhajate ca*), that is, "he understands" (the Kannada word given). The Nirukta author has included this word among the names of motion (Ni. 3-9). Since even that motion indicates swift movement, it is said that birds and the like also bear the name Bhuraṇyu:
भुरण्युरिति क्षिप्रनाम । भुरण्युः शकुनिर्भूरिमध्वानं नयति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यापि पोळ्ता तत्संपाती भुरण्युरनेन पावकख्यातेन । (*bhuraṇyuriti kṣipranāma | bhuraṇyuḥ śakunirbhūrimadhvānaṃ nayati svargasya lokasyāpi poḷtā tatsaṃpātī bhuraṇyuranena pāvakakhyātena |*) (si. 12-22).**NOTE**

### Printed p. 618

For flying far, a bird is called bhuraṇyu. It can carry anyone, even to heaven. The same name belongs to the sacrificer (yajamāna), the performer of the sacrifice, who moves swiftly (towards heaven) with the bird. In this connection the Nirukta author cites the Ṛk

येना पावक चक्षसा भुरण्यंतं जना अनु । त्वं वरुण पश्यसि ॥ (*yenā pāvaka cakṣasā bhuraṇyaṃtaṃ janā anu | tvaṃ varuṇa paśyasi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-6)

and has given the etymology of the word bhuraṇyu as above. So in this cited Ṛk too it is natural that the word भुरण्यंतं (*bhuraṇyaṃtaṃ*) has the sense of motion. Durgācārya in his commentary explains the word as क्षिप्रं गच्छंतं (*kṣipraṃ gacchaṃtaṃ*) with पुण्यकृतो जनाननुभुरण्यंतं पूर्वेषां पुण्यकृतां मार्गेण देवयानेन क्षिप्रं गच्छंतमनुपश्यसि (*puṇyakṛto janānanubhuraṇyaṃtaṃ pūrveṣāṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ mārgeṇa devayānena kṣipraṃ gacchaṃtamanupaśyasi*). This follows the view of the Nirukta author. But Sāyaṇa, in his commentary on the same Ṛk, gives this word the sense of holding or nourishing: भुरण्यंतं धारयंतं पोषयंतं ना इमं लोकं (*bhuraṇyaṃtaṃ dhārayaṃtaṃ poṣayaṃtaṃ nā imaṃ lokaṃ*). This meaning does not seem so fitting in that context. Since the word can also be formed from the root bhuraṇa (धारणपोषणयोः (*dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*)), which means holding and nourishing, the word is used in these senses as well. For example,

यन्यासत्या भुरण्यथो यद्वा देव भिषज्यथः । अयं वां वत्सो मतिभिर्न विंधते हविष्मंतं हि गच्छथः ॥ (*yanyāsatyā bhuraṇyatho yadvā deva bhiṣajyathaḥ | ayaṃ vāṃ vatso matibhirna viṃdhate haviṣmaṃtaṃ hi gacchathaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-9-6)

Here भुरण्यथः सर्वं जगत्सोपयथः (*bhuraṇyathaḥ sarvaṃ jagatsopayathaḥ*) — "you nourish the whole world" — is addressed to the Aśvin deities.

युवोरत्रिश्चिकेतति नरा सुम्मेन चेतसा । घर्मं यद्वामरेपसं नासत्यास्ना भुरण्यति ॥ (*yuvoratriściketati narā summena cetasā | gharmaṃ yadvāmarepasaṃ nāsatyāsnā bhuraṇyati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-73-6)

In such Ṛks it is in the sense of motion, "has reached" (प्राप्तवान् (*prāptavān*)). In the present Ṛk too it has the sense of motion, and at the end of the quarter-verse it gives the purport: the mortal knows both of Viṣṇu's two strides (only the strides over earth and atmosphere).

अभिख्याय (*abhikhyāya*) — The Nirukta author has included the word अभिख्या (*abhikhyā*) among the names for knowledge (Ni. 3-13). प्रख्याप्य (*prakhyāpya*) (by praise and the like) means "having made known", that is, having proclaimed so that it comes to the world's knowledge through praises and so on. The purport is that they make Viṣṇu's greatness famous.

### Printed p. 619

अभिख्या नो मघवन्नाधमानान्त्सखे बोधि वसुपते सखीनां । रणं कृधि रणकृत्सत्यशुष्माभक्ते चिदा भजा राये अस्मान् ॥ (*abhikhyā no maghavannādhamānāntsakhe bodhi vasupate sakhīnāṃ | raṇaṃ kṛdhi raṇakṛtsatyaśuṣmābhakte cidā bhajā rāye asmān ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-112-10)

In such Ṛks, अभिख्या अभिख्यापनेन प्रसिद्धान् कुरु (*abhikhyā abhikhyāpanena prasiddhān kuru*) gives the purport: "make our devotion and the like known to the whole world, by words of praise, and make our name famous." In the same way, in the present Ṛk too it means "to make manifest".

वयश्चन (*vayaścana*) — गंतृत्वात् पक्षिसादृश्याद्वा मरुतोऽत्र वय उच्यंते । (*gaṃtṛtvāt pakṣisādṛśyādvā maruto 'tra vaya ucyaṃte |*) Because they are always moving about, and because they resemble birds, vayaḥ here means the Maruts. That this word has many meanings — food, strength, life-span, ray and so on — has been shown earlier with examples.

##### Grammar

- वर्धंति — वृधु वृद्धौ इति धातुः । हेतुमति च इति णिच् । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोर्लघूपधस्य गुणः । णिजंतात् लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झ प्रत्ययः । तस्य अंतादेशः शप् विकरणं । छंदस्युभयथा (पा. सू. ३-४-११७) इति तस्य अर्धधातुकसंज्ञात्वात् णेरनिटि (पा सू. ६-४-५१) इति णिचो लोपः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- महि — मह पूजायां धातुः । इन् सर्वधातुभ्यः इति इन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- पौंस्यम् — पुंसः कर्म पौंस्यम् । प्यञ् प्रत्ययः । तद्धितेष्वचामादेः इति आदिवृद्धिः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् इति इत्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- मातरा — मान पूजायां धातुः । नप्तनेष्टृ (उ. सू. २-२५२) इति तृजंतत्वेन निपातितं । तस्मात् द्विवचने परे सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति तस्य आकारादेशः । ऋतो जि सर्व इति गुणः । अप्‌तृन्‌तृच् सूत्रे नियमकरणात् उपधादीर्घो न भवति । चित्त्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- नयति — णीञ् प्रापणे धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपं । तिजंतत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।

### Printed p. 620

- भुजे — भुज पालनाभ्यवहारयोः धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । चतुर्थ्येकवचनांतरूपं । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- दधाति — डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपं । पादादित्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१८९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- पुत्रः — पूञ् पवने धातुः । पुवोह्रस्वश्च (उ. सू. ४-९०४) इति क्र प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् गुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
- तृतीयम् — त्रेः संप्रसारणं च (पा. सू. ५-२-५५) इति तीय प्रत्ययः । संप्रसारणं ऋकारो भवति । प्रत्ययस्याद्युदात्तस्वरेण ईकार उदात्तो भवति ।
- रोचने — रुच दीप्तौ धातुः । तस्मात् युच् प्रत्यये आगते युवोरनाकौ (पा. सू. ७-१-१) इति तस्य अनादेशः । चित्त्वात् चितः इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- दिवः — ऊडिदं पदादि (पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

> तत्त॒दिद॑स्य॒ पौंस्यं॑ गृणीमसी॒नस्य॑ त्रा॒तुर॑वृ॒कस्य॑ मा॒ळ्हुषः॑ ।  
> यः पार्थि॑वानि त्रि॒भिरिद्विगा॑मभिरु॒रु क्रमि॑ष्टोरुगा॒याय॑  ॒॑
> जीवसे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत्त्वातत् । इत् । अस्य । पौंस्यं । गृणीमसि । इनस्य । त्रातुः । अवृकस्य । माळ्पुषः ।  
> यः । पार्थिवानि । त्रिभिः । इत् । विगामभिः । उरु । क्रमिष्ट । उरुगायाय ।  
> जीवसे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य महानुभावस्य तत्तत्पांस्यं पुंस्त्वं पराक्रमातिशयं गृणीमसि ।
> गृणीमः । स्तुमः । कीदृशस्यास्य । इनस्य सर्वस्य स्वामिनः त्रातुः पालकस्य अवृकस्य ।
> वृको हिंसकः शत्र्वादिः । तद्रहितस्य माळ्पुषः सेक्तुर्नित्यतरुणस्य । स्तुत्येषु
> पराक्रमेषु मध्य एकमुदाहरति । यो विष्णुः पार्थिवानि पृथिव्यादीनि प्रथनवंति
> वा । सामर्थ्यात् रजांसीति गम्यते । लोकत्रयस्यापि पृथिवीशब्दवाच्यत्वं पूर्व
> मुदाहृतं । तानित्रिभिरिद्विगामभिस्त्रिभिरेव विविधगमनैरुरु विस्तीर्णं यथा भवति
> तथा क्रमिष्ट क्रांतवान् । विचक्रम इत्यर्थः । उरुगायायोरुगातव्याय जीवसे
> लोकत्रयरक्षणाय । यद्वा । उरुगायाय ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी ॥ उरुगायस्य
> विष्णोरीदृशं पराक्रमं । गृणीमसि । किमर्थं । जीवसे जीवनाय रक्षणाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We praise the manliness (पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)), the surpassing valour, of each kind belonging to this great-souled one. Of what sort is he? He is इनस्य (*inasya*), lord of all; त्रातुः (*trātuḥ*), protector; अवृकस्य (*avṛkasya*) — vṛka is a harmful one such as an enemy, so, free of such; माळ्पुषः (*māḷpuṣaḥ*), the sprinkler (of seed), ever young. Among the praiseworthy exploits he cites one in particular: Viṣṇu, who with three strides in different directions strode over the पार्थिवानि (*pārthivāni*) — the earthly ones, earth and the rest, or the wide-extended ones; by implication "realms" (रजांसीति (*rajāṃsīti*)) is understood. That all three worlds are denoted by the word "earth" was cited earlier. He strode over them in such a way that it became vast (उरु (*uru*)); that is, he took his strides. उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*) means "to be sung widely"; जीवसे (*jīvase*) means for the protection of the three worlds. Or else: in उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*) the dative stands in the sense of the genitive: we praise such a valorous deed of Viṣṇu, the widely-praised one. For what purpose? जीवसे (*jīvase*): for life, for protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इनस्य (*inasya*)—(of the whole universe) the lord
- त्रातुः (*trātuḥ*)—the protector
- अवृकस्य (*avṛkasya*)—the non-harming one
- माळ्हुषः (*māḷhuṣaḥ*)—the one most abounding in power to shower down (desired things)
- (and) यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- पार्थिवानि (*pārthivāni*)—the three worlds, earth and the rest
- त्रिभिरिद्विगामभिः (*tribhiridvigāmabhiḥ*)—by a movement made in just three ways of going, in various fashions (with three feet)
- उरु (*uru*)—so as to become very wide
- क्रमिष्ठ (*kramiṣṭha*)—strode over; he
- उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*)—the one praised by many
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this great-souled Viṣṇu
- तत्तदित् पौंस्यं (*tattadit pauṃsyaṃ*)—those very various manly valorous deeds
- (उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*)—who is praised in many ways)
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—for the protection (of the three worlds)
- गृणीमसि (*gṛṇīmasi*)—we praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We praise, for the protection of the three worlds, the respective manly valorous deeds of Viṣṇu — lord of the whole universe, protector, non-harming, a youth most abounding in strength, who by moving with just three strides strode over the three worlds, earth and the rest, so that they became exceedingly wide, and who is praised by many.

##### Printed English

Therefore, verily, we celebrate the manhood of that lord (of all), the preserver, the innocuous, the vigorous, who traversed the three regions with three wide steps, in different directions, for the many-praised (preservation of) existence.

### Printed p. 622

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

इनस्य (*inasya*) — The Nirukta author has included इनः (*inaḥ*) among the names of the lord (īśvara) and given the etymology of the word: इन इत्येतत् सनित ऐश्वर्येणेति वा सनितमनेनैश्वर्यमिति वा । (*ina ityetat sanita aiśvaryeṇeti vā sanitamanenaiśvaryamiti vā |*) (Ni. 3-11). That is, one filled with lordship, or one who fills others with lordship; therefore the lord (the master) is called inaḥ. This epithet is fitting for Viṣṇu, because by his all-pervading form he has encompassed the whole universe and is lord of all, and because he himself is the cause of the growth of the universe's prosperity.

अवृकस्य (*avṛkasya*) — वृकः हिंसकः शत्र्वादिः । तद्रहितस्य । (*vṛkaḥ hiṃsakaḥ śatrvādiḥ | tadrahitasya |*) It is explained as "non-harming, not a foe". The Nirukta author cites the Ṛk

उदीरतामवर उत्परास उन्मध्यमाः पितरः सोम्यासः । असुं य ईयुरवृका ऋतज्ञास्ते नोऽवंतु पितरो हवेषु ॥ (*udīratāmavara utparāsa unmadhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ | asuṃ ya īyuravṛkā ṛtajñāste no 'vaṃtu pitaro haveṣu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-15-1)

and there explains the word avṛka as अनमित्राः (*anamitrāḥ*), "those who are not enemies". Just so Sāyaṇa too, wherever the word avṛka occurs, explains it as अनमित्रः (*anamitraḥ*), अहिंसकः (*ahiṃsakaḥ*). Here there is the positive sense "protector" and the negative sense "not a harmer".

मीळ्हुषः (*mīḷhuṣaḥ*) — This word is formed from the root mih, meaning "to sprinkle". Its basic sense can be seen in the sentence यन्मेहति तद्वर्षति (*yanmehati tadvarṣati*) (Bṛ. U. 1-1-1).

वाजयन्निव नू रथान्योगा आग्नेरुप स्तुहि । यशस्समस्य मीळ्हुषः ॥ (*vājayanniva nū rathānyogā āgnerupa stuhi | yaśassamasya mīḷhuṣaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-8-1)

In all such Ṛks it means फलस्य सेक्तुः (*phalasya sektuḥ*), "one who showers down the desired things". In the present Ṛk it is explained as "one with the capacity to sprinkle (seed) at all times": सेक्तुः नित्यतरुणस्य । (*sektuḥ nityataruṇasya |*) The purport is: one who always possesses youth. The word is used in many places as an epithet of Agni and other deities as well, in the sense "of exceedingly generous nature". The word वीळ्हुं (*vīḷhuṃ*), formed from this same root, has been included among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9), and the word मीळ्वे (*mīḷve*) among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Their particular meanings will be explained in their own contexts.

पार्थिवानि (*pārthivāni*) — पृथिव्यादीनि प्रथनवंति ना । (*pṛthivyādīni prathanavaṃti nā |*) That is, the three worlds, earth and the rest, which are extended very widely. लोकत्रयस्यापि पृधिवीशब्दवाच्यत्वं पूर्व- (*lokatrayasyāpi pṛdhivīśabdavācyatvaṃ pūrva-*)

### Printed p. 623

मुदाहृतं । (*mudāhṛtaṃ |*) That the three worlds are denoted by the word "earth" has been shown earlier with examples (in this same volume, in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-154-1). Even these three worlds,

त्रिभिरिद्विगामभिः उरु क्रमिष्ट (*tribhiridvigāmabhiḥ uru kramiṣṭa*) — he made still more exceedingly wide by his goings in his various forms; and he himself pervaded and strode over them all: उरु विस्तीर्णं भवति यथा तथा क्रांतवान् । (*uru vistīrṇaṃ bhavati yathā tathā krāṃtavān |*) For the fact that Viṣṇu, by his power of pervasion, made the atmosphere and the other regions greatly extended, the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā tell a story on the basis of the Ṛk Saṃhitā.

सखे विष्णो वितरं वि क्रमस्व द्यौर्देहि लोकं वज्राय विष्कभे । हनाव वृत्रं रिणचाव सिंधूनिंद्रस्य यंतु प्रसवे विसृष्टाः ॥ ( (*sakhe viṣṇo vitaraṃ vi kramasva dyaurdehi lokaṃ vajrāya viṣkabhe | hanāva vṛtraṃ riṇacāva siṃdhūniṃdrasya yaṃtu prasave visṛṣṭāḥ ‖ (*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-100-12)

In this Ṛk, at the time of the slaying of the demon Vṛtra, Vṛtra had grown exceedingly vast, and when Indra's strength did not suffice to hurl the thunderbolt at him, Indra prays to Viṣṇu and to the atmosphere to expand widely and help him in slaying Vṛtra. On the basis of this Ṛk the Bṛhaddevatā story is as follows.

त्रीन् लोकानभितप्येमान् वृत्रस्तस्थौ स्वया त्विषा । तं नाशकद्धंतुमिंद्रो विष्णुमभ्येत्य सोऽब्रवीत् ॥ (*trīn lokānabhitapyemān vṛtrastasthau svayā tviṣā | taṃ nāśakaddhaṃtumiṃdro viṣṇumabhyetya so 'bravīt ‖*)
वृत्रं हनिष्ये तिष्ठस्व विक्रम्याद्य ममांतिके । उद्यतस्यैव वज्रस्य द्यौर्ददातु ममांतरं ॥ (*vṛtraṃ haniṣye tiṣṭhasva vikramyādya mamāṃtike | udyatasyaiva vajrasya dyaurdadātu mamāṃtaraṃ ‖*)
तथेति विष्णुस्तच्चक्रे द्यौश्चास्य विवरं ददौ ॥ (*tatheti viṣṇustaccakre dyauścāsya vivaraṃ dadau ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 6-121 to 124)

Vṛtra, the harmer of all three worlds, stood grown by his distorted and harmful pervasion. Indra could not check him. Then Indra approached Viṣṇu, explained his situation and prayed: "I have to slay Vṛtra; grow vast and help me in that task. May the atmosphere too expand and be favourable for the hurling of my thunderbolt." Viṣṇu consented and grew accordingly. The atmosphere too made the space Indra needed. The same point is indicated in another place in the Ṛk Saṃhitā.

उत माता महिषमन्ववेनदमी त्वा जहति पुत्र देवाः । अथाब्रवीद्वृत्रमिंद्रो हनिष्यन्सखे विष्णो वितरं वि क्रमस्व ॥ (*uta mātā mahiṣamanvavenadamī tvā jahati putra devāḥ | athābravīdvṛtramiṃdro haniṣyansakhe viṣṇo vitaraṃ vi kramasva ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-18-11)

### Printed p. 624

…in the Ṛk (4-18-11 **NOTE**) Indra's mother, seeing the unchecked growth of Vṛtra, grew anxious, and Indra then prayed to Viṣṇu in the manner described above. In both of the situations cited above there is the matter of Viṣṇu's wide-spreading growth. The same situation is also described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, which sets out the threefold expansion in the three worlds that is indicated in the description त्रिभिरिद्विगामभिः (*tribhiridvigāmabhiḥ*).

असीद्यदि ना तावदध्यग्नेरासीत्स संभवन्नग्नीषोमावभि समभवथ्य इषुमात्र मिषुमात्रं विष्वज्जवर्धत स इमान् लोकानावृणोद्यदिमान् लोकान वृणोत्तद्वत्रस्य वृत्रत्वं तस्मादिंद्रोऽबिभेदपि त्वष्टा तस्मै त्वष्टावज्रमसिंचत्तपो वै स वज्र आसीत्तमुद्यंतुं नाशक्कोदथ वै तर्हि विष्णुरन्या देवतासीत्सोब्रवीद्विष्णवेहीदना हरिष्यावो येनायमिदमिति स विष्णुस्रेधात्मानं वि न्यधत्त पृथिव्यां तृतीयमंतरिक्षे तृतीयं दिवि तृतीयमभिपर्यावर्ताद्द्य बिभेद्यत्पृथिव्यां तृतीयमासीत्तेनेंद्रो वज्र मुदयच्छद्विष्णुनुस्थितस्सोऽब्रवीन्मामे प्र हारस्ति वा इदं मयि वीर्यं तत्ते प्र दास्यामीति (*asīdyadi nā tāvadadhyagnerāsītsa saṃbhavannagnīṣomāvabhi samabhavathya iṣumātra miṣumātraṃ viṣvajjavardhata sa imān lokānāvṛṇodyadimān lokāna vṛṇottadvatrasya vṛtratvaṃ tasmādiṃdro 'bibhedapi tvaṣṭā tasmai tvaṣṭāvajramasiṃcattapo vai sa vajra āsīttamudyaṃtuṃ nāśakkodatha vai tarhi viṣṇuranyā devatāsītsobravīdviṣṇavehīdanā hariṣyāvo yenāyamidamiti sa viṣṇusredhātmānaṃ vi nyadhatta pṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamaṃtarikṣe tṛtīyaṃ divi tṛtīyamabhiparyāvartāddya bibhedyatpṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamāsītteneṃdro vajra mudayacchadviṣṇunusthitasso 'bravīnmāme pra hārasti vā idaṃ mayi vīryaṃ tatte pra dāsyāmīti*)
(Kṛ. Saṃ. 2-4-12-2) **NOTE**

Formerly Vṛtra, born from the sacrificial fire, spread very quickly over all the worlds. He grew as fast as an arrow leaves a bow, and with a vast extent. For that very reason he got the name Vṛtra. Seeing this, fear arose in Indra. Then Tvaṣṭṛ made the thunderbolt and gave it to Indra, telling him to strike Vṛtra with it. Indra could not even lift the thunderbolt, which was born of the power of austerity. Viṣṇu was standing close by at the time. Indra prayed to Viṣṇu to help him in slaying Vṛtra; Viṣṇu agreed, divided his body into three parts, and placed one part on the earth, one in the atmosphere, and the remaining third in the heaven-world. With the help of the part of Viṣṇu's body that was on the earth, Indra lifted the thunderbolt.

### Printed p. 625

Then Vṛtra, frightened, told Indra that he should not be struck and that he would give up his valour that was on the earth; when he did so, Indra handed it over to Viṣṇu. In the same way he seized Vṛtra's valour in the atmosphere and in the heaven-world and handed it to Viṣṇu. Thus he received help from Viṣṇu three times, and in return gave him his own strength three times; therefore, as was stated earlier, the oblation offered as a part of this occasion is well known by the name Tridhātu. In this way Viṣṇu's greatness, who pervaded the three worlds, stood in them, and caused all three worlds to grow widely, is praised with त्रिभिरिद्विगामभिः उरु क्रमिष्ट (*tribhiridvigāmabhiḥ uru kramiṣṭa*).

##### Grammar

- तत्तत्—नित्यवीप्सयोः (पा. सू. ८-१-४) इति द्विर्वचनं भवति । परस्य आम्रेडितसंज्ञायां जातायां अनुदात्तं च (पा. सू. ८-१-३) इति तदनुदात्तं भवति ।
- गृणीमसि—गृ शब्दे धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचने मस् प्रत्ययः । इदंतोमसिः (पा. सू. ७-१-४६) इति तस्य इकारागमः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना (पा. सू. ३-१-८१) इति श्ना विकरणः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः (पा. सू. ७-३-८०) इति धातोः ह्रस्वो भवति । हलादौ जुत् प्रत्यये परे ई हल्यघोः (पा. सू. ६-४-११३) इति विकरणस्य ईत्वम् । ऋकारस्य परत्वात् णत्वम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
- इनस्य—इण् गतौ धातुः । इण् सिंजि—(उ. सू. २-२८२) इति नक् प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् गुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति । षष्ठीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
- त्रातुः—त्रैज् पालने । कर्तरि तृच् प्रत्ययः । आदेच उपदेशेशिति (पा. सू. ६-१-४५) इति धातोः आत्वम् । चित्त्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । षष्ठीएकवचने परे ऋत उत् इति उत्वे रपरे जाते रात् सस्य इति सकारस्य लोपः । रेफस्य विसर्गः ।
- अवृकस्य—न विद्यते वृकः यस्य अवृकः तस्य—नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ९-१-१३२) इति उत्तरपदांतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- मीढुषः—मिह सेचने धातुः । दाश्वान् स्वाहान् मीढ्वांश्च (पा. सू. ९-१-१२) इति क्वसुप्रत्ययांतो निपातितः । षष्ठ्यां भसंज्ञायां वसोःसंप्रसारणम् इति संप्रसारणम् । पूर्वरूपम् । शासिवसिघसीनांच इति सकारस्य षत्वम् । वसोः स्वरो भवति ।

### Printed p. 626

##### Grammar

- क्रमिष्ट—क्रमु पादविक्षेपे धातुः । लुज् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने त प्रत्ययः । च्लेः सिचादेशः । अर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः इति तस्य इडागमः । आदेशप्रत्यययोः इति सिचः सकारस्य षत्वम् । तन्निमित्तीकृत्य प्रत्ययस्य ष्टुत्वम् । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्‌योगेऽपि इति अडागमो न भवति । यच्छब्दसंबंधात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । धातुस्वरः अवतिष्ठते ।
- जीवसे—जीव प्राणधारणे धातुः । तुमर्थे सेसेनसे—(पा. सू. ३-४-९) इति तुमर्थे असे प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । एजंतत्वात् कैन्मेजंतः इति अव्ययसंज्ञा भवति ।

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्वे इद॑स्य॒ क्रम॑णे स्व॒र्दृशो॑ऽभि॒ख्याय॒ मत्यो॑र्व भुरण्यति ।  
> तृ॒तीय॑मस्य॒ नकि॒रा द॑धर्षति॒ वय॑श्च॒न प॒तयं॑तः पत॒त्रिणः॑ ॥५॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> द्वे इति । इत् । अस्य । क्रमणे इति । स्वःदृशः । अभिख्याय । मर्त्यः । भुरण्यति ।  
> तृतीयं । अस्य । नकिः । आ । दधर्षति । वयः । चन । पतयंतः । पतत्रिणः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य स्वर्दृशः स्वर्गस्य सर्वस्य वा द्रष्टुर्विष्णोर्द्वे इत् क्रमणे द्वे एव पदे
> मर्त्यो मनुष्योऽभिख्याय सर्वभूत्यादिना प्रख्याय भुरण्यति । गच्छति । भजते।
> भुरण्यतिः कण्णाद्दिर्गतिकर्मा भुरण्यति शवतीति तत्कर्मसु पाठात् । प्रसिद्धत्वाद्मूलोकं वृष्टागमनादंतरिक्षं चेत्युभे क्रमणे जानाति । अस्य विष्णोस्तृतीयं
> क्रमणं द्युलोकाख्यं कोऽपि मर्त्योनकिर्नैवा दधर्षति ! बुद्ध्या नाभिभवति ।
> ज्ञातुं न शक्नोतीत्यर्थः । न केवलं मनुष्य एव अपि तु वयश्चन वेतारो मरुतोऽपि ! कीदृशास्ते । पतयंतः सर्वत्र गमनसमर्थाः तथा पतत्रिणः पतनशीला
> गरुडादयो वायवो वा नकिरा दधर्षति । नैव शक्नु वंति ॥ धृषेर्लॆट्यडागमः ॥
> सत्यलोकस्यात्यंतविप्रकृष्टत्वेन सर्वेषामविषयत्पादिति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of this Viṣṇu, who is स्वर्दृशः (*svardṛśaḥ*), the beholder of heaven or of everything, only द्वे इत् क्रमणे (*dve it kramaṇe*), two steps, are known to mortal man, who goes about (or resorts to, worships) having glorified them by their universal-being and so on. भुरण्यति (*bhuraṇyati*) means "goes", "resorts to"; he cites the Nighaṇṭu, where भुरण्यति (*bhuraṇyati*) is read among the words for going and for activity. Because they are well known, man knows the two steps: the earth, and the atmosphere through the coming of rain. The third step of this Viṣṇu, called the heaven-world, no mortal at all ventures upon (दधर्षति (*dadharṣati*)): he cannot overcome it by understanding, that is, he cannot know it. Not men only: even वयश्चन (*vayaścana*), the Maruts, who are "knowers". What are they like? They are पतयंतः (*patayaṃtaḥ*), able to go everywhere; and पतत्रिणः (*patatriṇaḥ*), those given to flying, such as Garuḍa and the rest, or the winds: these too cannot venture upon it. The augment aṭ in दधर्षति (*dadharṣati*) is the Vedic leṭ of the root dhṛṣ. The sense is that, since the Satya-world is extremely remote, it lies beyond the range of all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वर्दृशः (*svardṛśaḥ*)—of the one who beholds everything or the heaven-world
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Viṣṇu
- द्वे इत् क्रमणे (*dve it kramaṇe*)—only two steps (only the earth and the atmosphere, where he sets two steps)
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—man
- अभिख्याय (*abhikhyāya*)—having praised
- भुरण्यति (*bhuraṇyati*)—(moves about) comes to know
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Viṣṇu
- तृतीयं (*tṛtīyaṃ*)—the heaven-world, where he sets the third step
- नकिः आ दधर्षति (*nakiḥ ā dadharṣati*)—(no man) can at all know it
- पतयंतः (*patayaṃtaḥ*)—(in all regions) capable of moving about
- वयश्चन (*vayaścana*)—the Maruts also (likewise)
- पतत्रिणः (*patatriṇaḥ*)—birds also (cannot know it)

### Printed p. 627

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Man comes to know, by praising them, only the earth and the atmosphere, where Viṣṇu, the beholder of heaven, sets two steps. The heaven-world, where this Viṣṇu sets the third step, no man at all can know. The Maruts, who are able to move about in all regions, and likewise the birds, cannot know it.

##### Printed English

Man, glorifying (Vishnu), tracks two steps of that heaven-beholding (deity), but he apprehends not the third ; nor can the soaring-winged birds (pursue it).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स्वर्दृशः (*svardṛśaḥ*)—स्वर्गस्य सर्वस्य वा द्रष्टुः (*svargasya sarvasya vā draṣṭuḥ*). This is an epithet of Viṣṇu, "beholding heaven" or "knowing everything". The word is used in both senses; but first one should examine the derivation of the word स्वर् (*svar*) and its uses in different senses, and then the nature of the compound स्वर्दृशः (*svardṛśaḥ*) can be understood.

This word is read among the common names, स्वः (*svaḥ*), पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*), नाकः (*nākaḥ*) and so on. साधारणान्युत्तराणि षड्डिवश्चादित्यस्य च (*sādhāraṇānyuttarāṇi ṣaḍḍivaścādityasya ca*) (Ni. 2-13). The Nirukta authors state that the six words स्वः (*svaḥ*), पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*), नाकः (*nākaḥ*), गौः (*gauḥ*), विष्टपं (*viṣṭapaṃ*) and नभः (*nabhaḥ*) are common designations, both synonyms of the heaven-world and synonyms of the Āditya (Sun). Then, explaining, for the use as a synonym of the Āditya, what the root of स्वर् (*svar*) is and what the derivation of the word is, they say:

स्वरादित्यो भवति सु अरणः, सु ईरणः, स्वृतो रसान्, स्वृतो भासं ज्योतिषां । स्वृतो भासेति वा । (*svarādityo bhavati su araṇaḥ, su īraṇaḥ, svṛto rasān, svṛto bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāṃ | svṛto bhāseti vā |*)
(Ni. 2-14)

### Printed p. 628

The Nirukta authors explain that the Āditya has this name either because he is very far away, or because he scatters and wholly destroys (darkness), or because he enters into the sap and becomes inward with it, or because he spreads his radiance into the orb of light and becomes one with it, or because he pervades the universe in the form of brightness; and that for this very reason, एतेन द्यौर्व्याख्याता (*etena dyaurvyākhyātā*), the heaven-world too has this name.

स्वरादित्यो भवति स एनानि सारयति (*svarādityo bhavati sa enāni sārayati*)
(A. 5-4) **NOTE**

The Āditya has the name स्वः (*svaḥ*) also because he makes the days move. In the Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā, in Ṛks such as

प्रत्यज् देवानां विशः प्रत्यज्जुदेषि मानुषान् । प्रत्यङ्विश्वं स्वर्दृते ॥ (*pratyaj devānāṃ viśaḥ pratyajjudeṣi mānuṣān | pratyaṅviśvaṃ svardṛte ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-210-5)

the word is taken as the Svar-world; in places such as

त्मना वहंतो दुरो व्यृण्वन्नवंत विश्वे स्वर्दृशीके । (*tmanā vahaṃto duro vyṛṇvannavaṃta viśve svardṛśīke |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-69-10)

it is taken as स्व-नभसि (*sva-nabhasi*), "in the sky", the atmosphere; and in Ṛks such as

दा नो अग्ने बृहतो दाः सहस्रिणो दुरो न वाजं श्रुत्या अपा वृधि । प्राची द्यावापृथिवी ब्रह्मणा कृधि स्वर्ण शुक्रमुषसो वि विद्युतुः ॥ (*dā no agne bṛhato dāḥ sahasriṇo duro na vājaṃ śrutyā apā vṛdhi | prācī dyāvāpṛthivī brahmaṇā kṛdhi svarṇa śukramuṣaso vi vidyutuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-2-7)

it is taken as the Āditya.

For the compound स्वर्दृशः (*svardṛśaḥ*) the meaning given above, "beholding heaven" or "beholding everything", has been adopted. Not only that, but according to the context other derivations have also been shown and meanings given. Taking some examples:

सम्राजावस्य भुवनस्य राजथो मित्रावरुणा विदथे स्वर्दृशा । वृष्टिं नां राधो अमृतत्वमीमहे द्यावापृथिवी वि चरंति तन्यवः ॥ (*samrājāvasya bhuvanasya rājatho mitrāvaruṇā vidathe svardṛśā | vṛṣṭiṃ nāṃ rādho amṛtatvamīmahe dyāvāpṛthivī vi caraṃti tanyavaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-2)

In this Ṛk the word स्वर्दृशा (*svardṛśā*) is an epithet of Mitra and Varuṇa. It can be explained in two ways. First, taking स्वर् (*svar*) as the Āditya, स्वर्दृशा (*svardṛśā*) can mean, like the words तादृशः (*tādṛśaḥ*) and मादृशः (*mādṛśaḥ*), "like the Sun", that is, "equal to the Sun", or "shining with the brilliance of the Āditya". The scholar Peterson, explaining the meaning of this word, gives the opinions of Oldenberg and other scholars as follows:

### Printed p. 629

I) स्वर्दृश (*svardṛśa*) appearing (dazzling) like the Sun (used of the Gods, ) ii) looking on the Sun, i. e. alive or (Geldner) seeing with Sun's light (used of men in four places). Geldner thinks that the latter Interpretation will do in all cases. विदथे स्वर्दृशा (*vidathe svardṛśā*) is probably to be understood as "appearing dazzling at the sacrifice".
( Hymns from the Rig-Veda—II Series. P. 318 )

The gist of this opinion has been given above. Besides this:

अश्मास्यमवतं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभि यमोजसातृणत् । तमेव विश्वे पपिरे स्वर्दृशो बहु साकं सिसिचुरुत्समुद्रिणं ॥ (*aśmāsyamavataṃ brahmaṇaspatirmadhudhāramabhi yamojasātṛṇat | tameva viśve papire svardṛśo bahu sākaṃ sisicurutsamudriṇaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-24-4)

In this Ṛk the word स्वर्दृशः (*svardṛśaḥ*) is explained as स्वः आदित्यः तस्य संबंधिनो द्रष्टारो रश्मयः (*svaḥ ādityaḥ tasya saṃbaṃdhino draṣṭāro raśmayaḥ*), that is, the rays of the Āditya (Sun); and

शुचिं न यामन्निषिरं स्वर्दृशं केतुं दिवो रोचनस्थामुषर्बुधं । अग्निं मूर्धानु दिवो आप्रतिष्ठुतं तमीमहे नमसा वाजिनं बृहत् (*śuciṃ na yāmanniṣiraṃ svardṛśaṃ ketuṃ divo rocanasthāmuṣarbudhaṃ | agniṃ mūrdhānu divo āpratiṣṭhutaṃ tamīmahe namasā vājinaṃ bṛhat*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-14)

here the word स्वर्दृशं (*svardṛśaṃ*) is an epithet of अग्निं (*agniṃ*) and, as Sāyaṇa says in the Ṛk under discussion, is explained as सर्ववृशं सर्वपदार्थविज्ञानयुक्तं (*sarvavṛśaṃ sarvapadārthavijñānayuktaṃ*) **NOTE**, that is, Agni, endowed with special knowledge by which he knows everything.

जनूश्चिद्वो मरुतस्त्वेष्येण भीमासस्तु विमन्यवोऽयासः । प्र ये महोभिरोजसोत संति विश्वो वो यामन् भयते स्वर्दृक् ॥ (*janūścidvo marutastveṣyeṇa bhīmāsastu vimanyavo 'yāsaḥ | pra ye mahobhirojasota saṃti viśvo vo yāman bhayate svardṛk ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-58-2)

In this Ṛk, सूरस्य द्रष्टा सर्वो जीवसमूहः (*sūrasya draṣṭā sarvo jīvasamūhaḥ*): the whole multitude of living beings that behold the Sun; or else स्वरंतरिक्षं । तत्पश्यतीति वृक्षः स्वर्दृक् सर्वदोत्तिष्ठन्नित्यर्थः । (*svaraṃtarikṣaṃ | tatpaśyatīti vṛkṣaḥ svardṛk sarvadottiṣṭhannityarthaḥ |*): the word स्वर् (*svar*) is explained as the atmosphere, and a tree, which always stands upward-facing and looks at the atmosphere, is named स्वर्दृक् (*svardṛk*).

यत्रा नरः समयंते कृतध्वचो यस्मिन्ना जा भवति किं चन प्रियं । यत्रा भयंते भुवना स्वर्दृशस्त्रत्रा न इंद्रावरुणाधि वोचतं ॥ (*yatrā naraḥ samayaṃte kṛtadhvaco yasminnā jā bhavati kiṃ cana priyaṃ | yatrā bhayaṃte bhuvanā svardṛśastratrā na iṃdrāvaruṇādhi vocataṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-83-2)

Here it is an epithet of heroes who are turned towards heaven. Having thus shown that meanings according to context are possible, he (Sāyaṇa) in the Ṛk under discussion explains स्वर्गस्य द्रष्टुः (*svargasya draṣṭuḥ*) or सर्वस्य द्रष्टुः (*sarvasya draṣṭuḥ*), of Viṣṇu, as…

### Printed p. 630
(The sentence continues from the previous page.) The Kannada commentary explains the word as above. Since Viṣṇu's highest step faces the Āditya, it will not be wrong to take the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) here to mean the Āditya (the sun) as well.

तृतीयं नकिः आ दधर्षति (*tṛtīyaṃ nakiḥ ā dadharṣati*)—the third stride, called the world of heaven: no mortal is able to know it by understanding. As for Viṣṇu's third step, the world of heaven, it cannot be known by any human being, nor by sky-ranging birds such as Garuḍa, nor even by the Maruts. This is the purport.

नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—This word is read among the words that express the sense of "all" (sarva-pada-samāmnāya). In this Ṛk the word has a negative sense, and it stresses that no one at all can know Viṣṇu's third step.

##### Grammar

- क्रमणे — क्रमु पादविक्षेपे धातुः । भावार्थे ल्युट् प्रत्ययः । युवोरनाकौ इति तस्य अनादेशः । अट्‌कुप्वाज् इति सूत्रेण नकारस्य णत्वं । लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इति प्रत्ययात् पूर्वमुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- स्वर्दृशः — दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । षष्ठीएकवचनांतरूपं ।
- अभिख्याय — ख्या प्रकथने धातुः । तस्मात् क्त्वा प्रत्यये समासेन नञ्पूर्वे (पा. सू. ७-१-७२) इति तस्य ल्यबादेशः । पित्त्वात् सोऽनुदात्तो भवति । **NOTE**
- भुरण्यति — भुरण्य गत् धातुः । कंड्वादिः । भुरण्यति शवति (निरु. १४-१६) इति गतिकर्मकधातूनां मध्ये पठितः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपं । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- दधर्षति — धृषि शसी वैयात्ये धातुः । इध्यषा प्रागल्भ्ये धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपः श्लु आदेशः । लेटोऽडाट् (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) इति प्रत्ययस्य अडागमः । धातोर्द्वित्वादि । प्रत्ययनिमित्तत्वेन धातोर्लघोपधाया गुणः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
- वयः — वा गतिगंधनयोः धातुः । वातेर्डिच्च (उ. सू. ४-५७३) इति इण् प्रत्ययः । तस्य डित्त्वविधानात् धातोः टेः (आ) लोपः । वि शब्दो भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपं ।

- पतयंतः — पत्ल्य गतौ धातुः । अस्मात् ण्यंतात् शतृप्रत्ययः । शप् विकरणः । णिचि निमित्ते धातोरकारस्य लोपः । तस्य स्थानिवद्भावात् उपधावृद्धिर्न भवति । शप् निमित्ते णिचो गुणः । अयादेशः । तास्यनुदात्तेत् इति सूत्रेण लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वात् णिच्स्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Viṣṇu, whose nature is the Āditya, together with four and ninety, that is, ninety-four, (in all) — these are the parts of time of that number. By his "names", that is, his own modes of inclining or movement, his special impulsions, he sets them in motion so that they are rounded: व्यतीन् (*vyatīn*), of varied extension. As one whirls a wheel, a round wheel with many spokes, by throwing it above the enemy, so he makes the said parts of time whirl; अवीविपत् (*avīvipat*) means "makes tremble, makes revolve" (root टुवेपृ (*ṭuvepṛ*), to tremble; from the causal, the form is with luk and cajji). Which are they? One year; two solstices; five seasons; twelve months; twenty-four half-months; thirty days-and-nights; eight watches; and, in one day, the twelve signs beginning with Meṣa that revolve (and are attached). Taken together these are ninety-four, which he whirls. (The bhāṣya continues on the next page.)

> दीनि द्वादश लग्नानीति मिलित्वा चतुरधिकनवतिसंख्याकानवीविपत् । नन्वादित्यः स्वयमपीतरवत्परिभ्रमति कथं भ्रमयतीत्युच्यते । नैष दोषः । एतेषां भ्रामकस्य ध्रुवस्य

> स्तुतिमद्भिर्मंत्रवद्भिर्वा विमिमानः । यद्यपि विभुस्तथापि भक्ताध्यीनत्वात् स्तुत्या
> मीयते । युवा सर्वत्र मिश्रणशीलो नित्यतरुणो वा आत एवाकुमारोऽसल्पः
> एवंभूतो महाविष्णुराहवमाह्वानं प्रत्येकति । गच्छति यज्ञदेशं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Objection: the Āditya himself revolves like the others, so how can he be said to make them revolve? Answer: there is no fault, because the fixed Viṣṇu who sets them revolving is another form of Viṣṇu; or else, because the revolution of the others depends on his own revolution, he is said to make them revolve himself. So Viṣṇu, whose nature is time, is vast of body, because the bodies of all gods, men and the rest are his own body in the form of the Virāṭ. He justifies this "vast body": विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*), measuring himself in diverse ways, establishing himself by dividing into the forms of gods, beasts and others. Or else: he is "measured out" by ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*), by the praising or the mantra-possessing; though all-pervading, he is dependent on his devotees and is measured by praise. युवा (*yuvā*): mingling everywhere, or ever young; therefore अकुमारः (*akumāraḥ*), not small. Such a Mahāviṣṇu goes to the invocation (āhava), that is, to the place of sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नामभिः (*nāmabhiḥ*)—by his modes of revolving (the Viṣṇu who is the Āditya)
- चतुर्भिस्साकं नवतिं च (*caturbhissākaṃ navatiṃ ca*)—ninety-four in number
- व्यतीन् (*vyatīn*)—the parts of time that stand divided separately
- चक्रं न (*cakraṃ na*)—like a wheel revolving about its spokes
- वृत्तं (*vṛttaṃ*)—as if turning in a circle
- अवीविपत् (*avīvipat*)—he makes (them) revolve
- बृहच्छरीरः (*bṛhaccharīraḥ*)—he who has the body of the Virāṭ
- ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*)—by praises in the form of mantras
- विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*)—he who divides (his own nature) into diverse forms such as gods and beasts and evolves
- युवा (*yuvā*)—he who joins everywhere, or the ever young
- अकुमारः (*akumāraḥ*)—(yet) one who is not of infant form, Mahāviṣṇu
- आहवं (*āhavaṃ*)—having regard to our invocation
- प्रत्येति (*pratyeti*)—comes (to the place of sacrifice)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Viṣṇu, whose nature is the Āditya, by his modes of revolution makes the parts of time, year and the rest, ninety-four in number and divided separately, revolve in a circle like a wheel turning round its spokes. He who has the body of the Virāṭ, who by praises in mantra-form divides his own nature into the diverse forms of gods, beasts and others and evolves, who is ever young yet not of infant form, Mahāviṣṇu, comes to the sacrificial ground regarding our invocation.

##### Printed English

He causes, by his gyrations, ninety and four periodical revolutions, like a circular wheel, vast of body, and evolving in many forms, through the praises (addressed to him); ever young, though not infantine, he comes at our invocations,

### Printed p. 633

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here the greatness of Viṣṇu, whose nature is the Āditya, is praised. When the Nirukta-writer shows the explanation of the word स्वसराणि (*svasarāṇi*), he says: स्वरादित्यो भवति स एनानि सारयति । (*svarādityo bhavati sa enāni sārayati |*) (Ni. 5-4). It is stated that the Āditya is named स्वः (*svaḥ*) because he makes the days move. In this Ṛk the power of Viṣṇu, whose nature is the Āditya, consisting in revolution, and the fact that he sets in motion time and all other principles, are described.

चतुर्भिस्साकं नवतिं च (*caturbhissākaṃ navatiṃ ca*)—एतत्संख्याकान् कालावयवान् । (*etatsaṃkhyākān kālāvayavān |*) Thus the parts of time are divided into ninety-four. They are:
- Year (संवत्सरः एकः (*saṃvatsaraḥ ekaḥ*)): 1
- Solstices (अयने द्वे (*ayane dve*)): 2
- Seasons (पंचर्तवः (*paṃcartavaḥ*)): 5
- Months (मासाः द्वादश (*māsāḥ dvādaśa*)): 12
- Half-months (चतुर्विंशत्यर्धमासाः (*caturviṃśatyardhamāsāḥ*)): 24
- Days-and-nights (त्रिंशदहोरात्राः (*triṃśadahorātrāḥ*)): 30
- Watches (अष्टौ यामाः (*aṣṭau yāmāḥ*)): 8
- The signs beginning with Meṣa (एकस्मिन्दिने पर्यावर्तमानानि मेषादीनि (*ekasmindine paryāvartamānāni meṣādīni*), द्वादश लग्नानि (*dvādaśa lagnāni*)): 12
- Taken together (मिलित्वा चतुरधिकनवतिसंख्याकाः (*militvā caturadhikanavatisaṃkhyākāḥ*)): total 94

Thus the parts of time are ninety-four in all.

व्यतीन् (*vyatīn*)—विविधातनस्वभावान्। (*vividhātanasvabhāvān|*) It is described that he sets in motion all these parts of time that exist in different forms.

The commentator shows that room is left here for another doubt, and gives the fitting answer: नन्वादित्यः स्वयमपि इतरवत्परिभ्रमति कथं भ्रमयति इत्युच्यते । (*nanvādityaḥ svayamapi itaravatparibhramati kathaṃ bhramayati ityucyate |*)

### Printed p. 634
Raising the doubt that, since the Āditya himself has the nature of revolution like the other planets and so on, how can he make other things move, the commentator answers that there is nothing unnatural in the description, because all other things in the world are only other forms of Viṣṇu, and because all their movements depend on the revolution of Viṣṇu who is the Āditya.

In answering this objection Sāyaṇa has given in summary the cosmic principle whose nature is time. By saying कालात्मकः विष्णुः (*kālātmakaḥ viṣṇuḥ*) and by विराडात्मना सर्वदेवमनुष्यादिशरीराणां स्वशरीरत्वात् (*virāḍātmanā sarvadevamanuṣyādiśarīrāṇāṃ svaśarīratvāt*) he states the identity of Viṣṇu with the universe, and that the whole activity of the universe depends on Viṣṇu's action. By the epithet विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*) it is said that Viṣṇu (who is described in another form as Prajāpati) is the cause even of creation, maintenance and the rest. By describing, in one place in one way and in another place in another, the ninety-four parts of time, of wheel-form, belonging to Viṣṇu who is the Āditya, it is shown that these are the very principles of Prajāpati, the cause of the universe.

द्वादशारं नहि तज्ञराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य । आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः । (*dvādaśāraṃ nahi tajñarāya varvarti cakraṃ pari dyāmṛtasya | ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiśca tasthuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-11)
सत्यात्मकस्यादित्यस्य चक्रं पुनःपुनः क्रमणशीलं मंडलाख्यं रथचक्रं वा वर्वति । (*satyātmakasyādityasya cakraṃ punaḥpunaḥ kramaṇaśīlaṃ maṃḍalākhyaṃ rathacakraṃ vā varvati |*)
पंचपादं पितरं द्वादशाकृतिं दिव आहुः परे अर्धे पुरीषिणं । अथेमे अन्य उपरॆ विचक्षणं सप्तचक्रे षळर आहुरर्पितं ॥ ; (*paṃcapādaṃ pitaraṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ diva āhuḥ pare ardhe purīṣiṇaṃ | atheme anya uparè vicakṣaṇaṃ saptacakre ṣaḷara āhurarpitaṃ ‖ ;*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-12)
पंचारे चक्रे परिवर्तमाने तस्मिन्ना तस्थुर्भुवनानि विश्वा । तस्य नाक्षस्तप्यते भूरिभारः सनादेव न शीर्यते सनाभिः ॥ (*paṃcāre cakre parivartamāne tasminnā tasthurbhuvanāni viśvā | tasya nākṣastapyate bhūribhāraḥ sanādeva na śīryate sanābhiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-13)

The wheel of the Āditya, with twelve spokes (the months), has in the sky a revolution of repeated turning. It suffers no decay, its revolution is everlasting. The pair of days-and-nights, in twinned form, of seven hundred and twenty in number, for the Āditya of infant form, is contained within this wheel of time. This wheel of time, made up of the solstices and other parts, continues its revolution without break. This is the cosmic principle. This principle is contained in Prajāpati the creator, and reflects his outer principles. This principle of time is described in various ways in the Saṃhitā, Brāhmaṇa and Upaniṣads

### Printed p. 635
everywhere. Showing the identity of this principle of time and the principle of sacrifice, and that Prajāpati is the support of both, the Taittirīya Saṃhitā describes it thus:

प्रजापतिरग्निमचिनुतर्तुभिस्संवध्सरं वसंतेनैवास्य पूर्वार्धमचिनुत ग्रीष्मेण दक्षिणं पक्षं वर्षाभिः पुच्छग्ं शरदोत्तरं पक्षग्ं हेमंतेन मध्यं ब्रह्मणा वा अस्य तत्पूर्वार्ध मचिनुत क्षत्रेण दक्षिणं पक्षं पशुभिः पुच्छं विशोत्तरं पक्षमाशया मध्यं य एवं विद्वानग्निं चिनुत ऋतुभिरेवैनं चिनुतेऽथो एतदेव सर्वमव ॥ (*prajāpatiragnimacinutartubhissaṃvadhsaraṃ vasaṃtenaivāsya pūrvārdhamacinuta grīṣmeṇa dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣaṃ varṣābhiḥ pucchagṃ śaradottaraṃ pakṣagṃ hemaṃtena madhyaṃ brahmaṇā vā asya tatpūrvārdha macinuta kṣatreṇa dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣaṃ paśubhiḥ pucchaṃ viśottaraṃ pakṣamāśayā madhyaṃ ya evaṃ vidvānagniṃ cinuta ṛtubhirevainaṃ cinute 'tho etadeva sarvamava ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-10-1)

It says that, as the year is built of the seasons, spring and the rest, he built all the parts of the sacrificial altar, the eastern and the others. And in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, showing the identity of the sacrificial horse, whose form is Prajāpati, with the parts of time:

उषा वा अश्वस्य (*uṣā vā aśvasya*) … सिंधवो .... .... .... वागेवास्य नागहर्वा अश्वं पुरस्तान्महिमान्वजायत तस्य पूर्वे समुद्रे योनी रात्रिरेनु पश्चान्महिमान्वजायत ................. !! (*siṃdhavo .... .... .... vāgevāsya nāgaharvā aśvaṃ purastānmahimānvajāyata tasya pūrve samudre yonī rātrirenu paścānmahimānvajāyata ................. !!*) **NOTE** (Śa. Brā. 10-6-4-1) **NOTE**

It describes: for the sacrificial horse in the form of Prajāpati, or Prajāpati in the form of the sacrificial horse, the dawn is the head, the sun the eye, the wind the breath, the fire Vaiśvānara the mouth, the year the body, .... .... .... the seasons the limbs, the months and half-months the joints, the days-and-nights the supporting pillars, and so on. This description, as explained in the bhāṣya on the present Ṛk (1-155-6) by कालात्मको विष्णुः (*kālātmako viṣṇuḥ*) and विविधमात्मानं विमानः देवतिरगात्मना विभज्य स्थापयन् (*vividhamātmānaṃ vimānaḥ devatiragātmanā vibhajya sthāpayan*), is the description of Prajāpati, whose nature is the Āditya, containing the cosmic principle. Western scholars, praising this exposition as the basis of the physical and spiritual principles later set out in the Upaniṣads and elsewhere, have stated their view thus:

In the elaborate rite of the piling of the fire-aliars lies the most philosophic content of the Samhita, for in it finds expression the chief doctrine of the sacrificial ritual, the sacrifice as a cosmic power of the highest potency. The first expression of it is preserved

### Printed p. 636
The passage on the Purusha hymn of the Ṛgveda (X-90) continues: there the creation of the universe is figured as the sacrifice of a Primeval Purusha, who is all that is and that shall be. This creation cannot be regarded as ever proceeding, and the year, the symbol of time, takes its part in that the three seasons, spring, summer and autumn form the ghee, the kindling sticks and the oblation, undoubtedly an attempt to recognise and explain time in its relation to the Universe.
(A. B. Keith: The Taittirīya Saṃhitā — I. Introduction: Harvard Oriental Series Vol. 18, p. CXXVI)

The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa in the tenth book (X. 6·4), which deals with the secret of the fire, develops the theme more philosophically. Prajāpati is the year, for he is essentially, as the creator, time, and the year is at once the symbol of time, and the period in which the working of nature completes a round and commences again.
(A. B. Keith, The Religion and Philosophy of the Veda, Vol. II, p. 466.)

The summary of the above opinion is that a profound cosmic principle lies hidden in this account: just as the year, together with its beginning and end and its parts such as the solstices, goes on continuously and endlessly by repeated recurrences, so also the life of the universe proceeds continuously, with individual beginnings and ends, yet as a whole with a beginningless, endless flow of revolution.

Just as the present Ṛk describes the whole cosmic principle as contained in the body of Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of the Sun, so the Upaniṣads and other texts describe all the principles of the nature of time as contained in Prajāpati, who is of the nature of the Sun; Agni, Viṣṇu, Āditya and Prajāpati all reflect one cosmic principle; time is the basis of all the affairs of the world; and that time is a part of Viṣṇu in the form of Prajāpati.

विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपंतं । सहस्ररश्मिः शतधा वर्तमानः प्राणः प्रजानामुदयत्येष सूर्यः ॥ (*viśvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ jātavedasaṃ parāyaṇaṃ jyotirekaṃ tapaṃtaṃ | sahasraraśmiḥ śatadhā vartamānaḥ prāṇaḥ prajānāmudayatyeṣa sūryaḥ ‖*) (Praśna Upaniṣad, 1-8). In this passage Āditya, the life-breath of all beings, is described as the universal-formed, the omniscient, the final goal (parāyaṇa), the one light of the whole world, existing in thousands of forms; the sun, the Āditya who is the soul of the universe, is thus described, and then:

### Printed p. 637
संवत्सरो वै प्रजापतिस्तस्यायने (*saṃvatsaro vai prajāpatistasyāyane*) … .... ॥ (*.... ‖*) **NOTE**
पंचपादं पितरं द्वादशाकृतिं दिव आहुः परे अर्धे पुरीषिणं । अथेमे अन्य उपरे विचक्षणं सप्तचक्रे षळर आहुरर्पितं ॥ ( (*paṃcapādaṃ pitaraṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ diva āhuḥ pare ardhe purīṣiṇaṃ | atheme anya upare vicakṣaṇaṃ saptacakre ṣaḷara āhurarpitaṃ ‖ (*)
(Repetition of Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-12)
मासो वै प्रजापतिस्तस्य कृष्णपक्ष एव रयिः शुक्लः प्राणः । (*māso vai prajāpatistasya kṛṣṇapakṣa eva rayiḥ śuklaḥ prāṇaḥ |*)
अहोरात्रो वै प्रजापतिस्तस्याहरेव प्राणो रात्रिरेव रयिः । (*ahorātro vai prajāpatistasyāhareva prāṇo rātrireva rayiḥ |*)
(Praśna Upaniṣad 1-9 to 13)

In these passages the identity of day-and-night, the month, the fortnights and Prajāpati is stated, and all the parts of time are said to be portions of Prajāpati.

Thus in all the Śruti passages quoted above a relation of part and whole is stated between time and Prajāpati, while in the present Ṛk such a relation is stated between time and Viṣṇu; if this raises a doubt, one may look at passages that teach non-difference: Prajāpati is of the nature of the Sun, and Viṣṇu is of the nature of the Sun.

एष ब्रह्मैष इंद्र एष प्रजापतिरेते सर्वे देवा इमानि च पंच महाभूतानि पृथिवी वायुराकाश आपो ज्योतींषीत्येतानीमानि च क्षुद्रमिश्राणीव ॥ (*eṣa brahmaiṣa iṃdra eṣa prajāpatirete sarve devā imāni ca paṃca mahābhūtāni pṛthivī vāyurākāśa āpo jyotīṃṣītyetānīmāni ca kṣudramiśrāṇīva ‖*) (Aitareya Upaniṣad 3-3)
देवो वरुणः प्रजापतिः सविता । (*devo varuṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ savitā |*) (Chā. U. 1-12-5)

In these and similar passages Prajāpati is described as the soul of all. Just as Sāyaṇa calls Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of the Sun, the soul of all, so in these passages Prajāpati, of the nature of the Sun, is called the soul of all. The Sun is of the nature of time, the basis of time, and the impeller of temporal activities. Hence Sāyaṇa's solution is that Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of the Sun, carries on his own revolution and the revolutions of the times as non-different; this is supported by the sentence स्वभ्रमणाधीनत्वादितरेषां परिभ्रमणस्य । अतः स्वयं भ्रमतीत्युच्यते । (*svabhramaṇādhīnatvāditareṣāṃ paribhramaṇasya | ataḥ svayaṃ bhramatītyucyate |*)

विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*)—विविधमात्मनं मिमानः देवतिर्यगात्मना विभज्य स्थापयन् । (*vividhamātmanaṃ mimānaḥ devatiryagātmanā vibhajya sthāpayan |*) This is explained as: developing his own subtle self-principle in forms such as gods and animals, and establishing it in different forms. The purport is: though one in origin, he himself undergoes manifold transformations and in effect takes on different states and forms.

## Sūkta 156 (Maṇḍala 1)
[[b-intro not separate]]
Introduction (the printed Sanskrit introduction): the sūkta भवा मित्र (*bhavā mitra*) of five Ṛks is the seventeenth sūkta; it is by Dīrghatamas, of the Dairghatamasa line; since it is said "jāgata" it is also jāgata (Jagatī metre); since "vaiṣṇava" is said, it is Viṣṇu's; the Anukramaṇī says भव पंच (*bhava paṃca*). It is applied in the Ukthya rite, at the third pressing, for the Acchāvāka's recitation; the Sūtra in the section उक्ष्ये तु होत्रकाणामिति (*ukṣye tu hotrakāṇāmiti*) prescribes it: भवा मित्रः सं नां कर्मणा (*bhavā mitraḥ saṃ nāṃ karmaṇā*) (Ā. 6-1). In the Saumya-caru, ghee is to be used on both sides; in the upper ghee-offering the ordinary yājyā is उरु विष्णो वि क्रमस्व (*uru viṣṇo vi kramasva*); on the tenth day this Ṛk भवा मित्र (*bhavā mitra*) is to be used in its place, as the section दशमेऽहनि (*daśame 'hani*) states: उरु विष्णो वि क्रमस्वीति धृतयज्यास्थाने भवा मित्रः (*uru viṣṇo vi kramasvīti dhṛtayajyāsthāne bhavā mitraḥ*) (Ā. 8-12).

**Anuvāda.** This sūkta भवा मित्र (*bhavā mitra*) is the seventeenth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Dīrghatamas, son of Ucathya; the deity is Viṣṇu; the metre Jagatī. The Anukramaṇī says "bhava pañca". In the Ukthya sacrifice, at the third pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this sūkta, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section "Ukthe tu hotrāṇām", by the sūtra "Bhavā mitraḥ saṃ nāṃ karmaṇā" (Ā. 6-1). In both caru-oblations connected with Soma, ghee is to be used; in this ghee-offering the Ṛk "Uru viṣṇo vi kramasva" is to be used as the ordinary yājyā; but on the tenth day the Ṛk "Bhavā mitra" is to be used in place of it, as the sūtra "Uru viṣṇo vikramasveti dhṛtayājyāsthāne bhavā mitraḥ" in the section "Daśame 'hani" of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra directs (Ā. 8-12).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Viṣṇu, like Mitra": Mitra is the friend, the Āditya who saves from distress; he cites Nirukta 10-21, प्रमीतेस्त्रायत इति (*pramītestrāyata iti*). Like him, Viṣṇu is शेव्यः (*śevyaḥ*), good at giving happiness, the maker of happiness, and घृतासुतिः (*ghṛtāsutiḥ*) (continued in the next block).

> होत्रा स्तोमो राध्यो हविष्मता यज्ञश्च राध्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

घृतासुतिः (*ghṛtāsutiḥ*): he by whom water is pressed out; or else he to whom ghee is brought face to face. विभूतद्युम्नः (*vibhūtadyumnaḥ*): of abundant fame, or of abundant food. एवयाः (*evayāḥ*): the one who brings or bestows protection. सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*): broad on all sides. Each of these epithets is connected with "be to us". उ (*u*) is a verse-filler. O Viṣṇu, since you are such, therefore your स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*), a special praise, is अर्ध्यः (*ardhyaḥ*) for the knowing sacrificer who knows your greatness: fit to be furthered again and again; it is not completed by being done once. Likewise your sacrifice is राध्यः (*rādhyaḥ*), to be accomplished by that sacrificer who has the oblation. Or else: the praise is to be accomplished by the knowing Hotṛ, and the sacrifice by the sacrificer with the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रो न (*mitro na*)—like a friend, or like the Āditya in the form of Mitra
- शेव्यः (*śevyaḥ*)—the giver of happiness
- धृतासुतिः (*dhṛtāsutiḥ*)—the accepter of the offering of ghee
- विभूतद्युम्नः (*vibhūtadyumnaḥ*)—having abundant fame, or abundant food
- एवयाः (*evayāḥ*)—the giver of protection
- सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*)—easily approachable on every side
- भव (*bhava*)—be (in our regard)
- विष्णो (*viṣṇo*)—O Viṣṇu
- अध (*adha*)—because you are filled with these qualities
- ते (*te*)—your
- स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)—special praise
- विदुषा (*viduṣā*)—by the sacrificer who knows (your greatness)
- अर्ध्यः (*ardhyaḥ*)—to be recited again and again
- यज्ञश्च (*yajñaśca*)—and the sacrifice (directed to you)
- हविष्मता (*haviṣmatā*)—by the sacrificer who has the oblation
- राध्यः (*rādhyaḥ*)—to be accomplished

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, be to us like a friend: the giver of happiness, the accepter of the ghee offering, of abundant fame, the giver of protection, and easily approachable on every side. O Viṣṇu, since you are filled with these qualities, your special praise is to be recited again and again by the sacrificer who knows your greatness; and the sacrifice directed to you is also to be accomplished by the sacrificer who has the oblation.

##### Printed English

Be (to us), Vishnu, like a friend, the giver of happiness, the accepter of oblations, abounding with food, the granter of protection, and every way accessible; on which account your praise is to be repeatedly recited by the wise, and your worship to be celebrated by the offerer of oblations.

### Printed p. 642

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Vishnu is compared to Mitra. The word Mitra is explained here in two ways: it may mean the worldly friend, or Mitra in the form of Āditya, who has the qualities of that friend. To show that the same benefits of happiness and joy that come from a friend come to the world from Mitra in the form of Āditya, the Nirukta-writer has given a derivation of this word—
मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते । संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा । मेदयतेर्वा । (*mitraḥ pramītestrāyate | saṃminvāno dravatīti vā | medayatervā |*)
Yāska explains that the name Mitra arises either from protecting from destruction, or from moving about while measuring (examining) all principles, or from nourishing the world by giving it food and the like and so making the world well-fed. (Ni. 10-21) And further, he quotes the Ṛk
मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां । मित्रः कृष्णीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं धृतवज्जु होत ॥ (*mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ | mitraḥ kṛṣṇīranimiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ dhṛtavajju hota ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-1)
and, by showing Mitra's beneficial guidance, the manner in which he upholds heaven and earth, and his being ever watchful and protecting the people who belong to him, he explains the qualities of a trusted friend found in Mitra. In the present Ṛk also, Mitra's nature is described by the epithets beginning with शेव्यः (*śevyaḥ*).

शेव्यः (*śevyaḥ*)—साधुः सुखकर्ता (*sādhuḥ sukhakartā*): one who gives happiness. शेव (*śeva*) means happiness. This word is generally used when the happiness that is the fruit of sacrifice is indicated.
यज्ञ साहं दुव इषेग्निं पूर्वस्य शेवस्य । अद्रेः सूनुमायुमाहुः ॥ (*yajña sāhaṃ duva iṣegniṃ pūrvasya śevasya | adreḥ sūnumāyumāhuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-20-7)
Here the word शेव (*śeva*) is used as a synonym for happiness that is excellent and is the fruit of sacrifice. In the present Ṛk, in describing Mitra's nature, it is said that Mitra produces happiness of such excellence; and Vishnu too is prayed to be such a Mitra.

फृतासुतिं (*phṛtāsutiṃ*)—it means an āsuti in the form of ghee. Āsuti means food in the form of juice; milk and the like, the Soma juice that is an oblation, or an oblation in the form of ghee, are all indicated by the word āsuti.
त्वे अग्ने विश्वे अमृतासो अद्रुह आसा देवा हविरदंत्याहुतिं । त्वया मर्तासः स्वदंत आसुतिं त्वं गर्भो वीरुधां जज्जिषे शुचिः ॥ (*tve agne viśve amṛtāso adruha āsā devā haviradaṃtyāhutiṃ | tvayā martāsaḥ svadaṃta āsutiṃ tvaṃ garbho vīrudhāṃ jajjiṣe śuciḥ ‖*)
### Printed p. 643
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-14)
Here, saying that by Agni's grace men enjoy foods such as milk, in the form of juice, the word āsuti is used as a synonym of milk and the like. In the present Ṛk it means an āsuti in the form of ghee.

विभूतद्युम्नः (*vibhūtadyumnaḥ*)—प्रभूतयशाः प्रभूतान्नो वा (*prabhūtayaśāḥ prabhūtānno vā*): one of abundant fame, or one of abundant food. The Nirukta-writers have included the word द्युम्न (*dyumna*) among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). Moreover, when giving a derivation of this word again, द्युम्नं द्योततेर‍्यशो वा अन्नं वा (*dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vā annaṃ vā*) (Ni. 5-5), they show that, formed from the root द्युत् (*dyut*) meaning "to shine", it means either fame or food. Quoting the Ṛk
शतं ते शिप्रिन्नू तयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु । जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥ (*śataṃ te śiprinnū tayaḥ sudāse sahasraṃ śaṃsā uta rātirastu | jahi vadharvanuṣo martyasyāsme dyumnamadhi ratnaṃ ca dhehi ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-25-3)
they show that, when the prayer is made "give us द्युम्न (*dyumna*) and treasure", wealth is indicated by the word रत्न (*ratna*), and so द्युम्न (*dyumna*) means fame or food. (Ni. 5-5) Likewise in the present Ṛk it means one of abundant fame or of abundant food.

एवयाः (*evayāḥ*)—this word is generally an epithet of the Maruts. In many places, as in एवैः सखिभिः (*evaiḥ sakhibhiḥ*)—गमनशीलैर्मित्रभूतैर्मरुद्भिः (*gamanaśīlairmitrabhūtairmarudbhiḥ*), it indicates the Maruts' nature of moving about and their being always together. Although the root has the sense of moving, in the present Ṛk the sense is "one who unites, who joins", that is, one who provides protection.

सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*)—सर्वतः पृथुः (*sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*): spread widely all around. The Nirukta-writers explained the basic meaning of this word thus (Ni. 6-8),
त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असि जुष्टो होता वरेण्यः । त्वया यज्ञं वि तन्वते ॥ (*tvamagne saprathā asi juṣṭo hotā vareṇyaḥ | tvayā yajñaṃ vi tanvate ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-13-4)
and quoting this Ṛk they showed the fitting meaning of the word there as stated above. In the present Ṛk, however, that meaning is somewhat extended: the commentator explains the purport as "be large-bodied all around us".

### Printed p. 644
अध्यः (*adhyaḥ*)—पुनः पुनः प्रवर्धनार्हः । एकवारकरणे न संपूर्णत इत्यर्थः ! (*punaḥ punaḥ pravardhanārhaḥ | ekavārakaraṇe na saṃpūrṇata ityarthaḥ !*) The stoma-hymn that praises you is to be recited again and again, to sing your qualities; it is not to be finished by reciting once. This is the meaning.
राध्यः (*rādhyaḥ*)—समाराधनीयः (*samārādhanīyaḥ*): one to be performed with splendour.

##### Grammar

- भव—भू सत्तायां धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । द्वचोतस्तिज- (पा. सू. ६-३-१३५) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति । पादादित्वान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । शप् पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरो अवशिष्यते ।
- मित्रः—इमिदा स्नेहने धातुः । अमिजिमि- (उ. सू. ४.६०-३) इति क्र प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वाल्लघूपधगुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तो भवति । **NOTE**
- शेव्यः—शेवे साधुः शेव्यः । साध्वर्थे यत् प्रत्ययः । यतोनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इत्याद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
- धृतासुतिः—धृतं आसुतिः येन सः धृतासुतिः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । विभूतद्युम्नः इत्यत्रापि बहुव्रीहिसमासत्वात् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
- सप्रथाः—प्रथ प्रख्याने धातुः । सर्वधातुभ्यः असुन् इत्यसुन् प्रत्ययः । प्रथसा सह वर्तते इति सप्रथाः । तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे (पा. सू. २-२-२८) इति समासः । वोपसर्जनस्य (पा. सू. ६-२-८२) इति सह इत्यस्य समासे स भावः । **NOTE**
- अधा—अथ इत्यत्र छांदसत्वाद्वर्णविकारो जातः । निपातस्यच (पा सू. ६-३-१३६) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
- विदुषा—विद ज्ञाने धातुः । अस्माल्लट् आगते तस्य शत्रादेशः । विदेशिशतुर्वसुः (पा. सू. ७-१-३६) इति शतृवसुरादेशः । तृतीयाविकवचने परे वसोः संप्रसारणम् इति संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपम् ।
- अध्यः—ऋधु वृद्धौ धातुः । अस्मादर्हार्थे यत् आगते धातोर्लघूपधस्य गुणः । आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । एवमेव राध संसिद्धौ धातुः । अस्मादपि यत् आगते आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ॥ १ ॥
